Surat al-An'am

It is Meccan, and it has one hundred and sixty-five verses. It was revealed at Mecca all at once at night, and with it seventy thousand angels who had filled the space between the two horizons, making a clamour of glorification, praise and exaltation. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty, glory be to my Lord, the Mighty," and fell down in prostration. [See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/243-244.]

It is also related with a raised (marfu') report: "Whoever recites Surat al-An'am, those seventy thousand angels will send blessings upon him day and night." [Narrated by al-Tha'labi from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. In its chain is Abu 'Isma, who is accused of lying. Its beginning is in al-Tabarani's al-Saghir, in which is Yusuf ibn 'Atiyyah, who is weak; from him Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his tafsir and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf of Ibn Hajar p. 63; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/246.]

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: Surat al-An'am was revealed at Mecca, except His saying, "They did not measure Allah with His true measure," up to the end of three verses, and His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you"﴾ up to His saying, "that you may be mindful" (ta'aqqun). These six verses are Medinan. [Narrated by al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh from Ibn 'Abbas. al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/244.]

* *

﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: this verse is the first verse in the Torah and the last verse in the Torah, which is His saying, "Praise be to Allah who has not taken a son" up to the end of the verse (al-Isra': 111).

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Allah began creation with praise, saying, (Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth), and concluded it with praise, saying, (And it will be judged between them with truth), i.e., between the creatures, and (It will be said: "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds") (al-Zumar: 75).

His saying, "Praise be to Allah," means that Allah praised Himself, teaching His servants, i.e., "Praise Allah who created the heavens and the earth." He singled out the heavens and the earth for mention because they are the greatest of creatures as far as the servants can see, and in them are lessons and benefits for the servants. ﴿And made the darknesses and the light﴾. The "making" here means "creating." al-Waqidi said: everything in the Qur'an concerning "darknesses" and "light" means disbelief and faith, except in this verse, where by them he means night and day.

al-Hasan said: "And made the darknesses and the light" means disbelief and faith. It was also said: by the darknesses he meant ignorance, and by the light, knowledge.

Qatadah said: it means Paradise and Hell.

It was also said: the meaning is that Allah created the heavens and the earth, and He had already made the darknesses and the light, because He created darkness and light before the heavens and the earth.

Qatadah said: Allah created the heavens before the earth, darkness before light, and Paradise before Hell. It is related from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Allah, may He be exalted, created the creation in darkness, then cast upon them of His light; whoever is struck by that light is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray." [Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Iman, chapter on the division of this community: 7/401, and he said: this is a hasan hadith. Ibn Hibban (p. 449) and al-Hakim (1/30-31) declared it sahih. Ahmad narrated it: 2/176, 197. al-Haythami said: Ahmad narrated it through two chains, and al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani too, and the narrators of one of Ahmad's chains are trustworthy. Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/194. al-Khatib mentioned it in Mishkat al-Masabih: 1/37, and al-Albani declared it sahih.]

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾. That is: yet those who disbelieve after this clarification ascribe equals to their Lord, i.e., they associate others with Him. Its root is from the equating of one thing with another, and from it comes "'adl" (justice). That is, they make others equal to Allah, the Exalted. It is said: "I equated this with that" when I made them equal. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said this, and that the "ba'" (bi-) here means "'an" (from), so the meaning is "from their Lord they turn away," i.e., they incline and deviate, from al-'udul (deviation). Allah, the Exalted, said (a spring from which the servants of Allah drink), i.e., from it.

It was also said: under His saying, "Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord," there is a subtle meaning, similar to the saying of one who says: "I have bestowed favours upon you with such-and-such, and I have shown you grace with such-and-such, yet you disbelieve in My blessing."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 2–3:**

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾. This means Adam, peace be upon him, and He addressed them with it because they were his descendants. Al-Suddi said: Allah the Exalted sent Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, to the earth to bring Him a portion of it. The earth said, "I seek refuge in Allah from you, lest you diminish me." So Jibril returned without taking anything and said, "O Lord, it sought refuge in You." Then He sent Mika'il (Michael), and it sought refuge, so he returned. Then He sent the Angel of Death, and it sought refuge in Allah from him. He said, "And I seek refuge in Allah from disobeying His command." So he took from the surface of the earth and mixed the red, the black and the white. Therefore the colours of the children of Adam differ. Then he kneaded it with sweet water, salt water and bitter water, and therefore their characters differ. Then Allah the Exalted said to the Angel of Death: "Jibril and Mika'il showed mercy to the earth, but you did not show it mercy. Surely I will make the souls of whomever I create from this clay to be in your hand."

It is related from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Allah created Adam, peace be upon him, from dust and made it clay. Then He left it until it became black mud, moulded (ḥama'an masnunan). Then He created him and shaped him, and left him until he became dry clay like pottery. Then He breathed into him His spirit." [[Narrated by Abu Ya'la, and in its chain is Isma'il ibn Rafi'. Al-Bukhari said: "Trustworthy, close to acceptable in narration." The majority weakened him. The rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih. Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/197.]]

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Then He decreed a term, and a named term is with Him﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: The first term is from birth to death, and the second term is from death to resurrection, which is the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection). This is also related from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Every person has two terms: a term until death, and a term from death until resurrection. If he is righteous, pious and keeps the ties of kinship, his term of resurrection is added to his term of life. If he is wicked and severs the ties of kinship, his term of life is reduced and his term of resurrection is increased." Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The first term is the term of this world, and the second term is the term of the Hereafter. Atiyyah reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾ that it means sleep, in which the soul is taken and then returned upon waking. ﴿And a named term is with Him﴾ means the term of death. It was also said that both are one and the same, its meaning being: [Then He decreed a term] [[Addition from "B".]], meaning: He made for your lives a duration at which you will arrive; ﴿and a named term is with Him﴾ meaning: it is a named term with Him, which no one else knows. ﴿Then you doubt﴾ means you are in doubt about the resurrection.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and in the earth﴾. This means: He is the God of the heavens and the earth, like His saying: (And He is the one who in the heaven is God, and in the earth is God). It was also said: He is the One worshipped in the heavens and the earth. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is that He is in the heavens, knowing your secret and your open speech, and in the earth. [Al-Zajjaj said: There is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its estimated meaning being: "And He is Allah, ﴿knowing your secret and your open speech﴾ in the heavens and the earth."] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from "B".]] ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾, meaning what you do of good and evil.

﴿And no sign from the signs of their Lord comes to them﴾, meaning the people of Makkah, ﴿except that they turn away from it﴾, ignoring it and denying it. Such as the splitting of the moon and others. ʿAṭāʾ said: he means signs of the Qur'an.

﴿They have denied the truth﴾, meaning the Qur'an; it is also said: Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿when it came to them. Soon there will come to them the news of what they used to mock﴾, that is: the reports of their mockery and its consequence, meaning: they will know the outcome of their mockery [116a] when they are punished.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Do they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ meaning the past nations. A qarn (generation) is a group of people, and its plural is qurūn. It is also said that a qarn is a period of time: eighty years, it is said; sixty years, it is said; forty years, it is said; thirty years, it is said; and it is said one hundred years, based on what is narrated: the Prophet (ﷺ) said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr al-Māzinī: "You will live a qarn," and he lived one hundred years. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh al-Saghir, p. 93. See: al-Isabah: 4/23; Usd al-Ghabah: 3/125.]]

So, according to these opinions, its meaning is from a generation, ﴿We had established them on the earth as We have not established you﴾, that is: We gave them what We have not given you. Ibn ʿAbbas said: We gave them a long life, like the people of Nuh, ʿAd and Thamud. It is said: makkantuhu and makkantu lahu (both mean "I established him"). ﴿And We sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾, meaning the rain. Midrar is on the pattern of miftar, from the root darr (flowing abundantly). Ibn ʿAbbas said: midrar means continuous at the times of need.

His saying: ﴿as We have not established you﴾ is a shift in address (al-talwin, meaning a shift between grammatical persons). The speech moved from the report in "Do they not see" to direct address, as in His saying: ﴿until, when you were in the ship and they sailed with them﴾ [Yunus: 22].

The people of Basra said: He informed about them with His saying "Do they not see," and among them were Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions; then He addressed them directly along with them. The Arabs say: "I said to ʿAbd Allah, how noble he is," and "I said to ʿAbd Allah, how noble you are." ﴿And We made the rivers flow beneath them, then We destroyed them for their sins, and We brought into being﴾, that is, We created and originated, ﴿after them another generation﴾.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a book on paper﴾, to the end of the verse. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul p. 246; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/393.]] said: it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayyah and Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid. They said: "O Muhammad, we will not believe in you until you bring us a book from Allah, accompanied by four angels who testify that it is from Allah and that you are His messenger." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a book on paper﴾, written from Me, ﴿and they touched it with their hands﴾, that is: they saw it and touched it with their hands. He mentioned touching and did not mention seeing, because touching is more effective in producing certain knowledge than seeing, for magic works on what is seen and does not work on what is touched. ﴿Those who disbelieved would certainly say: This is nothing but obvious magic.﴾ Its meaning: nothing will benefit them, because of what has already been decreed concerning them by My knowledge.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 8–11:

﴿And they say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him"﴾ upon Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿"an angel?" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided﴾. That is, the punishment would have become obligatory and the affair would have been concluded. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 12–13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾ If they answer you, well; otherwise, you (say): ﴿To Allah.﴾ He commanded him to give the answer immediately after the question, so that it would be more effective in impact and stronger as proof. ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ means He has decreed it for Himself. This is an appeal from Him, exalted is He, to the believers, urging them to turn toward Him, and an informing them that He is Merciful to the servants, does not hasten punishment, and accepts repentance and return.

Abu 'Ali Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami informed us: Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Allah had finished creating the creation, He wrote a Book, which is with Him above the Throne: Indeed My mercy has overcome My anger."

And Abu al-Zinad narrated from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra: "Indeed My mercy has [preceded] [in B: (encompassed)] My anger."

Shaykh Abu al-Qasim Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Kirkani informed us: Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Abd al-Rahman al-Marwazi informed us: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us: Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman informed us, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah has one mercy among the jinn, the humans, the animals and the insects; by it they show compassion to one another, by it they show mercy to one another, and by it the wild beasts show tenderness to their young. And Allah has postponed ninety-nine mercies with which He will show mercy to His servants on the Day of Resurrection."

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Abu Ghassan informed us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from his father, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: Captives were brought to the Prophet (ﷺ), and there was a woman among the captives whose breasts were dripping with milk, running about; whenever she found a child among the captives, she seized it, pressed it to her belly and nursed it. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to us: "Do you think this woman would throw her child into the fire?" We said: "No, while she is able not to throw it." He said: "Allah is more merciful to His servants than this woman is to her child."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He will surely gather you﴾: the lam here is the lam of oath and the nun is the emphatic nun; its sense is: "By Allah, He will surely gather you," ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, i.e., on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: its meaning is that He will gather you in your graves until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿There is no doubt about it. Those who have lost their souls﴾ are those who were deceived about themselves, ﴿they are the ones who do not believe.﴾

﴿And to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day﴾: "dwells" means "rests." It was said: He meant what rests and what moves, as in His saying: (garments that protect you from the heat), meaning the heat and the cold. It was also said: resting was singled out for mention because the blessing in it is greater. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: everything upon which the sun rises and sets is among what dwells in the night and the day, and what is meant is all that is on the earth. It was also said: its meaning is whatever the night and the day pass over. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of their voices, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of their secrets.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 14:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Shall I take other than Allah as a protector?﴾ [This was] when he (the Prophet's opponent) called to the religion of his fathers. So He, exalted is He, said: Say, O Muhammad: Shall I take other than Allah as a protector, [as a lord, an object of worship, a helper and an aide]? [[Addition from "b".]] ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., their Creator, their Innovator, and the One who began them. ﴿And He feeds but is not fed﴾, i.e., He provides sustenance and is not provided for, as He said: (I do not desire any provision from them, nor do I desire that they should feed Me).

﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit (aslama)﴾, meaning: of this community. Islam here means submission to the command of Allah. It was also said: aslama means "to be sincere" (akhlasa). ﴿And do not be among the polytheists (mushrikin)﴾, meaning: and it was said to me, "Do not be among the polytheists."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 15–17:

﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day﴾ [then worship other than Him] [[Addition from "B".]]. That is: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Whoever is spared it﴾: that is, whoever has the punishment averted from him. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr (on the authority of 'Asim) and Ya'qub read "yuṣraf" (يَصْرِفْ) with a fatha on the yā' and a kasra on the rā', meaning: whoever God averts the punishment from, in accordance with His saying "then He has had mercy on him." The others read it with a ḍamma on the yā' and a fatha on the rā'. ﴿On that day﴾: that is, the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then He has had mercy on him. That is the clear attainment﴾: that is, the evident salvation.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾: with hardship and affliction, ﴿there is no remover of it﴾: no lifter of it, ﴿except Him. And if He touches you with good﴾: with well-being and blessing, ﴿then He is over all things competent﴾: over both good and harm.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Muleihi, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sulami informed us, who said: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Shayban al-Ramli informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah informed us, who said: Shihab ibn Khirash [he is the son of 'Abd Allah] informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A mule was presented as a gift to the Prophet (ﷺ), which Khosrow had sent him. He rode it with a rope of hair, then he had me ride behind him. He travelled with me for a while, then he turned to me and said: "O boy!" I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Guard Allah and He will guard you. Guard Allah and you will find Him before you. Become known to Allah in ease and He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pen has already run with what is to be. If all of creation strove to benefit you with something Allah had not decreed for you, they would not be able to do it; and if they strove to harm you with something Allah had not written against you, they would not be able to do it. If you are able to act with patience together with certainty, then do so; but if you are not able, then be patient, for in patience over what you dislike lies much good. Know that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship comes ease."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 15–17:

﴿Say: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day﴾ [then worship other than Him] [[Addition from "B".]]. That is: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Whoever is spared it﴾: that is, whoever has the punishment averted from him. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr (on the authority of 'Asim) and Ya'qub read "yuṣraf" (يَصْرِفْ) with a fatha on the yā' and a kasra on the rā', meaning: whoever God averts the punishment from, in accordance with His saying "then He has had mercy on him." The others read it with a ḍamma on the yā' and a fatha on the rā'. ﴿On that day﴾: that is, the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Then He has had mercy on him. That is the clear attainment﴾: that is, the evident salvation.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾: with hardship and affliction, ﴿there is no remover of it﴾: no lifter of it, ﴿except Him. And if He touches you with good﴾: with well-being and blessing, ﴿then He is over all things competent﴾: over both good and harm.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Muleihi, who said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sulami informed us, who said: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Shayban al-Ramli informed us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah informed us, who said: Shihab ibn Khirash [he is the son of 'Abd Allah] informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A mule was presented as a gift to the Prophet (ﷺ), which Khosrow had sent him. He rode it with a rope of hair, then he had me ride behind him. He travelled with me for a while, then he turned to me and said: "O boy!" I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Guard Allah and He will guard you. Guard Allah and you will find Him before you. Become known to Allah in ease and He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask Allah; when you seek help, seek help from Allah. The pen has already run with what is to be. If all of creation strove to benefit you with something Allah had not decreed for you, they would not be able to do it; and if they strove to harm you with something Allah had not written against you, they would not be able to do it. If you are able to act with patience together with certainty, then do so; but if you are not able, then be patient, for in patience over what you dislike lies much good. Know that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship comes ease."

[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad through the narration of Hanash al-San'ani from Ibn 'Abbas: 1/307; and al-Tirmidhi in abridged form in the Book of Qiyamah, chapter "Narrated to us by Bishr ibn Hilal": 7/219–220, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. A similar report is in the Musnad: 1/293–303. Also 'Abd ibn Humayd in al-Muntakhab, p. 214. Ibn al-Athir mentioned it in Jami' al-Usul in the form cited by the author and said: this hadith was mentioned by Razin, and I did not find it in any of the six books except what al-Tirmidhi transmitted, and this is his wording, then he cited al-Tirmidhi's narration. See: Jami' al-Usul 11/686. 'Abd ibn Humayd also narrated it in his Musnad with a weak chain, and Ibn al-Salah in al-Ahadith al-Kulliyyah attributed it to 'Abd ibn Humayd and others; and this hadith has been narrated from Ibn 'Abbas through many routes... The route of Hanash which al-Tirmidhi transmitted is good and sound. See: Jami' al-'Ulum wa al-Hikam of Ibn Rajab, p. 174.]]

﴿وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ﴾ *"He is the Subduer over His servants."* Al-Qahir is al-Ghalib (the Victorious). Qahr (subjugation) adds a meaning beyond qudrah (power): it is preventing others from attaining their aims. It was also said: He is the One who alone manages affairs and compels creation to accept His will. *"Above His servants"* refers to the attribute of exaltation (isti'la'), which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone possesses.

﴿وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ *"And He is the All-Wise"* in His command, ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ *"the All-Aware"* of the deeds of His servants.

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً﴾ *"Say: 'What thing is greatest in testimony?'"* to the end of the verse. Al-Kalbi said: The people of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Show us someone who testifies that you are the Messenger of Allah, for we see no one who believes you. We have asked the Jews and the Christians about you, and they claim that you have no mention among them." Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafi related to us; Muhammad ibn Bishr ibn Muhammad al-Muzani informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr al-Naqqash informed us; Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani informed us; Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Dahhak al-Babili informed us; al-Awza'i informed us: Hassan ibn Atiyyah related to me, from Abu Kabshah [al-SalULi] [[In "B": (al-Sulawi).]], from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Convey from me, even if it is one verse, and narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm (in it). Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Anbiya', chapter on what has been mentioned about the Children of Israel: 6/496, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/243.]]

Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah make radiant the face of a servant who hears my saying, memorizes it, understands it, and conveys it. For many a bearer of knowledge is not himself learned, and many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who is more learned than he. The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿الَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ *"Those to whom We have given the Book"* means the Torah and the Gospel. ﴿يَعْرِفُونَهُ﴾ *"They recognize him"* means Muhammad (ﷺ) by his description and attributes, ﴿كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَاءَهُمْ﴾ *"as they recognize their own sons,"* among the children.

﴿الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ *"Those who have lost themselves"* means they defrauded themselves, ﴿فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ *"and they do not believe."* This is because Allah has made for every human being a station in Paradise and a station in Hellfire. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah gives the believers the stations of the people of the Fire in Paradise, and gives the people of the Fire the stations of the people of Paradise in the Fire. That is the loss.

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ﴾ *"And who is more unjust"* means more disbelieving, ﴿مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى﴾ *"than one who fabricates"* means invents, ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ *"a lie against Allah,"* by associating others with Him, ﴿أَوْ كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِهِ﴾ *"or denies His signs,"* meaning the Qur'an. ﴿إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ *"Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed,"* meaning the disbelievers.

﴿وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ﴾ *"He is the Subduer over His servants."* Al-Qahir is al-Ghalib (the Victorious). Qahr (subjugation) adds a meaning beyond qudrah (power): it is preventing others from attaining their aims. It was also said: He is the One who alone manages affairs and compels creation to accept His will. *"Above His servants"* refers to the attribute of exaltation (isti'la'), which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, alone possesses.

﴿وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ *"And He is the All-Wise"* in His command, ﴿الْخَبِيرُ﴾ *"the All-Aware"* of the deeds of His servants.

The words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ شَهَادَةً﴾ *"Say: 'What thing is greatest in testimony?'"* to the end of the verse. Al-Kalbi said: The people of Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Show us someone who testifies that you are the Messenger of Allah, for we see no one who believes you. We have asked the Jews and the Christians about you, and they claim that you have no mention among them." So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿قُلْ أَيُّ شَيْءٍ أَكْبَرُ﴾ *"Say: 'What is greatest,"* meaning most mighty, ﴿شَهَادَةً﴾ *"in testimony?"* If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُ﴾ *"Say: 'Allah,"* ﴿شَهِيدٌ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ *"is a Witness between me and you,"* concerning what I say, and He bears witness for me to the truth and against you in falsehood. ﴿وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنُ لِأُنْذِرَكُمْ بِهِ﴾ *"This Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you by it,"* that I may frighten you by it, O people of Makkah. ﴿وَمَنْ بَلَغَ﴾ *"and whomever it reaches"* means: whoever the Qur'an reaches, from among non-Arabs and other nations, until the Day of Resurrection.

Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hanafi related to us; Muhammad ibn Bishr ibn Muhammad al-Muzani informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr al-Naqqash informed us; Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani informed us; Yahya ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Dahhak al-Babili informed us; al-Awza'i informed us: Hassan ibn Atiyyah related to me, from Abu Kabshah [al-SalULi] [[In "B": (al-Sulawi).]], from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Convey from me, even if it is one verse, and narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm (in it). Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in the Fire."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Anbiya', chapter on what has been mentioned about the Children of Israel: 6/496, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/243.]]

Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib informed us; Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Sufyan ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "May Allah make radiant the face of a servant who hears my saying, memorizes it, understands it, and conveys it. For many a bearer of knowledge is not himself learned, and many a bearer of knowledge conveys it to one who is more learned than he. Three things are such that a Muslim's heart will not harbor rancor over them: sincerity of deed for Allah, sincere counsel to the Muslims, and adherence to their community, for their supplication surrounds those behind them."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-'Ilm, chapter on urging the conveying of what is heard, in a similar form, 7/417-418, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith; by Ibn Majah in al-Muqaddimah, chapter on whoever conveys knowledge, no. (236): 1/86; by al-Darimi in al-Muqaddimah, chapter on disliking taking opinion: 1/75; by al-Shafi'i in Kitab al-'Ilm: 1/16; by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/225 from Anas; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/236. Shaykh Abd al-Muhsin al-Abbad has a study of the hadith's narration and jurisprudence, "May Allah make radiant the face of a man...", published in 1401 AH at al-Rashid Press in Madinah al-Munawwarah.]]

**"And on the Day We will gather them all"**: that is, the worshippers and those they worshipped, on the Day of Resurrection. Ya'qub (Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hadrami) read *yahshuruhum* ("He will gather them") here, and with the *ya'* in Saba'. Hafs agreed with him in Saba'. The others read it with *nun* (*nahshuruhum*, "We will gather them").

**"Then We will say to those who associated partners [with God]: 'Where are your partners whom you used to claim?'"**: that they would intercede for you before your Lord.

**"Then their *fitnah* will not be"**: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read *yakun* ("will be") with *ya'*, because *al-fitnah* means *al-iftitan* (the act of being tested or tempted), so it is permissible to use the masculine form. The others read it with *ta'* (*takun*), because *al-fitnah* is feminine. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Hafs, on the authority of Asim, read *fitnatuhum* ("their *fitnah*") in the nominative (*raf'*), making it the subject of *kana* ("was"). The others read it in the accusative (*nasb*), making the subject of *kana* the phrase *an qalu* ("that they said") and *fitnatuhum* the predicate. The meaning of *fitnatuhum* is: their statement and their answer. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: their excuse. *Al-fitnah* means a trial or testing. Since their questioning was a test to reveal what was in their hearts, it was called a *fitnah*.

Al-Zajjaj said concerning His words, **"Then their *fitnah* will not be"**: this is a subtle meaning. It is like a man who becomes infatuated with someone he loves, then suffers a *mihnah* (an ordeal) because of it, and so disowns the one he loved. It is said: "Your infatuation was only this." Likewise, the disbelievers were infatuated with love for the idols, and when they saw the punishment they disowned them. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: **"Then their *fitnah* will not be"**, in their love for the idols, **"except that they will say: 'By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists.'"** Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *Rabbana* ("our Lord") in the accusative, as a vocative addressed to one who is attached to a pronoun (*naday al-mudaf*). The others read it in the genitive (*khafd*), as an attribute of *Allah*.

It is said: when they see on the Day of Resurrection God's forgiveness and His pardoning of the people of monotheism, some of them say to others: "Come, let us conceal our polytheism, so that perhaps we may be saved along with the people of monotheism." So they say: "By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists." Then their mouths are sealed, and their limbs bear witness against them to their disbelief.

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, says: **"Look how they lied against themselves"**, by their excuse with falsehood and their disowning of polytheism, **"and what they used to invent [against God]"** of the idols **"has gone astray from them"**, that is, has vanished and departed from them. The reason is that they used to hope for the intercession and support of the idols, so all of that became void on that Day.

The Qur'anic verse "And among them are those who listen to you" and the rest of the verse. Al-Kalbi said: Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, 'Utba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabi'a, Umayya and Ubayy, the two sons of Khalaf, and al-Harith ibn 'Amir gathered and were listening to the Qur'an. They said to al-Nadr, "O Abu Qutayla, what is Muhammad saying?" He replied, "I do not know what he is saying, except that I see him moving his tongue and saying, 'the myths of the ancients,' just as I used to tell you about the past generations." Al-Nadr was known for recounting the stories of the earlier generations and their reports [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul (occasions of revelation) by al-Wahidi, p. (247).]]. Then Abu Sufyan said, "I see that some of what he says is true." Abu Jahl said, "Never! We do not acknowledge any of this." In another narration, he said, "Death is easier for us than this." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And among them are those who listen to you," that is, to you and to your words. "And We have placed over their hearts coverings" (akinna), meaning coverings, the plural of kinan, like a'innah being the plural of 'anan. "Lest they understand it" (an yafqahuhu) means lest they comprehend it. It was said: its meaning is "lest they do not understand it," and it was said: "out of aversion to their understanding it." "And in their ears is deafness" (waqran), meaning deafness and heaviness. This is evidence that Allah, exalted is He, turns the hearts: He opens some of them to guidance, and places others under coverings, so they do not understand the speech of Allah and do not believe. "And if they see every sign" (ayah), meaning of the miracles and proofs, "they will not believe in it, until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say, 'This is nothing but the myths of the ancients.'" That is, their tales and stories. Asatir is the plural of usturah and isharah, and it was said that it means nonsense and falsehoods. Its root is from satartu, meaning I wrote.

"And they forbid others from it" (wa hum yanhawna 'anhu), that is, they forbid the people from following Muhammad (ﷺ). "And they keep away from it" (wa yan'awna 'anhu), that is, they keep themselves far from it. It was revealed concerning the disbelievers of Makka. This was said by Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak. Qatada said: they forbid people from the Qur'an and from the Prophet (ﷺ), and they keep away from him.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. (247-248); Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 6/406.]]: it was revealed concerning Abu Talib. He used to forbid the people from harming the Prophet (ﷺ) and would protect him, but he kept away (yana'a) from faith in him, that is, he stayed far from it. It is related that the chiefs of the polytheists gathered around him and said, "Take a young man from among us who is the most handsome, and hand over to us Muhammad." Abu Talib said, "You have not been fair to me. Should I hand over to you my son so that you may kill him, and I raise your son?" It is also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) invited him to faith, and he said, "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me, I would have brought comfort to your eyes by it. But I will defend you as long as I live." He also said verses about this:

By Allah, they will never reach you with their gathering
until I am laid in the dust, buried.

So proclaim your matter, and there is no harm to you in it,
and rejoice in it, and let your eyes be cooled by it.

You invited me, and I knew that you are sincere with me,
and you have indeed spoken the truth, and you were trustworthy there.

You presented a religion that I know to be
among the best religions of mankind.

Were it not for blame, or fear of disgrace,
you would have found me generous in that, clearly.

"And they destroy only themselves" (wa in yuhlikuna), that is, they destroy only themselves. "Only themselves" means the consequence of their deeds returns only to them, and the burdens of those who turn them away fall upon them. "And they are not aware" (wa ma yash'urun).

He used to forbid the people from harming the Prophet (ﷺ) and would protect him, but he kept away (yana'a) from faith in him, that is, he stayed far from it. It is related that the chiefs of the polytheists gathered around him and said, "Take a young man from among us who is the most handsome, and hand over to us Muhammad." Abu Talib said, "You have not been fair to me. Should I hand over to you my son so that you may kill him, and I raise your son?" It is also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) invited him to faith, and he said, "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me, I would have brought comfort to your eyes by it. But I will defend you as long as I live." He also said verses about this:

By Allah, they will never reach you with their gathering
until I am laid in the dust, buried.

So proclaim your matter, and there is no harm to you in it,
and rejoice in it, and let your eyes be cooled by it.

You invited me, and I knew that you are sincere with me,
and you have indeed spoken the truth, and you were trustworthy there.

You presented a religion that I know to be
among the best religions of mankind.

Were it not for blame, or fear of disgrace,
you would have found me generous in that, clearly.

"And they destroy only themselves" (wa in yuhlikuna), that is, they destroy only themselves. "Only themselves" means the consequence of their deeds returns only to them, and the burdens of those who turn them away fall upon them. "And they are not aware" (wa ma yash'urun).

The Qur'anic phrase: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before the Fire﴾. He means: in the Fire, as in His saying: ﴿on the kingdom of Solomon﴾, meaning in the kingdom of Solomon. It is also said: they are presented to the Fire. The response (jawab) of "law" (if) is omitted, and its meaning is: If you saw them in that state, you would see a marvel.

﴿They will say: "Oh, would that we were returned"﴾, meaning: to the worldly life. ﴿"And we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."﴾ The recitation of all the common readers (al-'ammah) is with raf' (nominative, ḍamm/raf') for "wa-lā nukadhdhibu" and "wa-nakūnu", on the meaning: "Oh, would that we were returned, and we would not deny, and we would be among the believers." Ḥamzah, Ḥafṣ and Ya'qūb read "wa-lā nukadhdhiba wa-nakūna" with naṣb (accusative, fatḥah) on the bā' and the nūn, as a response to the wish (jawāb al-tamannī, the answer to a wish). The meaning is: "Would that our return took place, and that we would not deny and would be [among the believers]." The Arabs put the response to a wish in the accusative after the wāw just as they do after the fā'. Ibn 'Āmir read "nukadhdhibu" with raf' and "nakūna" with naṣb, because they wished to be among the believers, and they reported about themselves that they would not deny the signs of their Lord if they were returned to the worldly life.

﴿Nay, there has become apparent to them﴾. His saying "bal" (nay, but rather) contains a rejection of their claim, meaning: the matter is not as they said, that if they were returned they would believe. ﴿Rather, there has become apparent to them﴾, meaning: there has appeared to them, ﴿what they used to conceal﴾, meaning: what they kept secret, ﴿from before﴾, meaning: in the worldly life, of their disbelief and their acts of disobedience. It is also said: "what they used to conceal" refers to their saying: ﴿"By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ (Al-An'am, 23). So they concealed their polytheism and hid it until their limbs testified against them concerning what they had hidden and covered up, because they did not conceal their disbelief in the worldly life. Unless the verse is taken to refer to the hypocrites. Al-Mubarrad said: "Nay, there has become apparent to them" means the recompense of what they used to conceal. Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl said: "Nay, there has become apparent from them" (bada 'anhum).

Then He said: ﴿And if they were returned﴾ to the worldly life, ﴿they would return to what﴾, meaning: to that which ﴿they were forbidden﴾ from, of disbelief. ﴿And indeed they are liars﴾ in their saying: "If we were returned to the worldly life, we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers."

﴿And they say: "There is not but our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ This is a report of their denial of the resurrection (al-ba'th). 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: this is part of what they would have said if they were returned.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord﴾, meaning: before His judgment, His decree and His questioning. It is also said: they are presented before their Lord. ﴿He will say﴾ to them. It is also said: the guardians (al-khazanah) will say to them, by the command of Allah: ﴿"Is this not the truth?"﴾ meaning: Is this resurrection and punishment not the truth? ﴿They will say: "Yes, by our Lord"﴾, that it is true. Ibn 'Abbās said: this is at one station, and their saying "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists" is at another station, for there are many stations on the Day of Resurrection: at one station they acknowledge, and at another they deny.

﴿He will say: "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verses 31–33:

﴿Indeed, they have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.﴾ That is, they lost themselves by denying their return to Allah through resurrection after death. ﴿Until, when the Hour came upon them suddenly﴾, that is, the Resurrection, ﴿suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, ﴿they said, "Alas for us!"﴾, meaning, "Our regret!" [It is mentioned] [[The words in brackets are missing from manuscript "A" and we have restored them from manuscript "B".]] in the form of a vocative, for emphasis. Sibawayh said: it is as if they are saying, "O regret, this is your time." ﴿for what we neglected﴾, that is, what we fell short in, ﴿concerning it﴾, that is, concerning obedience. It was also said: "what we left behind in the world of the deeds of the Hereafter."

Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: [[See Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/325, where he says: "The 'ha' and 'alif' in His words 'concerning it' refer to 'the transaction'. But the mention of it was dispensed with, because His words 'Indeed, they have lost who denied the meeting with Allah' indicate it, since it is known that 'loss' can only occur in a transaction that has taken place."]] The pronoun refers to the transaction. When the loss of their transaction became clear to them, by their trading the Hereafter for this world, they said, "Alas for us, for what we neglected concerning it," that is, concerning the transaction. [So the mention of "the transaction" is omitted] [[See Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/325, with the same wording as above.]] being sufficiently indicated by His words ﴿have lost﴾, because loss only occurs in a transaction of sale. And al-hasrah is the intensity of regret, to the point that the one regretting becomes exhausted, like the one whose mount is worn out on a long journey. ﴿while they carry their burdens﴾, that is, their loads and their sins, ﴿upon their backs.﴾ Al-Suddi and others said: When the believer is raised from his grave, he is met by the most beautiful thing in form and the sweetest in scent, and it says to him, "Do you recognize me?" He says, "No." It says, "I am your good deed. Mount me, for you have often mounted me in the world." This is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic: (On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation) [Maryam 19:85], that is, as riders. As for the disbeliever, he is met by the ugliest thing in form and the foulest in scent, and it says, "Do you recognize me?" He says, "No." It says, "I am your evil deed. You have often mounted me in the world, so today I shall mount you." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾. [Regarding "they carry"], Ibn Abbas said: "Evil is the load they have carried."

﴿The life of this world is nothing but play and amusement﴾, falsehood and deception, having no permanence. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah.﴾ Ibn Amir read ﴿wa-la-dar al-akhirah﴾ with the genitive construction, annexing "the abode" to "the Hereafter", and a thing may be annexed to itself when the two words differ, as in His words (and the grain of the harvest) [Qur'an 55:12, as cited], and in their saying "Rabi' al-Awwal" and "Masjid al-Jami'". The world is called "al-dunya" because of its nearness (dunuww), and it was said it is so called because of its lowliness (dana'ah). The Hereafter is so called because it comes after the world. ﴿better for those who fear﴾ shirk, ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ that the Hereafter is superior to this world. The people of Madinah, Ibn Amir, and Ya'qub read ﴿ta'qilun﴾ ("will you not reason") with the letter ta' here, in al-A'raf, in Surah Yusuf, and in Ya-Sin. Abu Bakr agreed with them in Surah Yusuf, and Hafs agreed except in Surah Ya-Sin. The others read it with the letter ya' in all of these.

His words, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾. Al-Suddi said: Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq met Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and al-Akhnas said to Abu Jahl, "O Abu al-Hakam, tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? For there is no one here who hears your words except me." Abu Jahl said, "By Allah, Muhammad is truthful, and Muhammad has never lied. But when the sons of Qusayy take the banner, the water-provision, the custodianship of the Ka'bah, the council-house, and prophethood, what will remain for the rest of Quraysh?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse. [[Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 249; Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/333.]]

Najiyah ibn Ka'b said: Abu Jahl said to the Prophet ﷺ, "We do not accuse you, nor do we call you a liar, but we call a liar what you have brought." So Allah Most High revealed: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾. [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi through the chain of Abu Kurayb from Ali, in the book of Tafsir, Surah al-An'am, 8/437; then through the chain of Ishaq ibn Mansur from Sufyan from Abu Ishaq from Najiyah, that Abu Jahl... and he mentioned something similar, without mentioning Ali in it, and said: "This is more authentic." The hadith of Ali was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 2/315, and he said: "Authentic according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs." Al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "The two of them did not narrate anything from Najiyah." See also: Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 249; al-Tabari, 11/334; al-Qurtubi, 6/416.]]

﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you﴾, [namely] that you are a liar, ﴿for it is not you they deny﴾. Nafi' and al-Kisa'i read it with the light form (takhfif), while the others read it with the doubled form (tashdid) from "taktheeb". Al-Takdhib (to call someone a liar) means to ascribe lying to him and say to him, "You have lied." Al-Ikdhab means to find him to be a liar. The Arabs say: "I found the land barren (ajdabtu al-ard) and fertile (akhsabtuha)" when they find it barren or fertile. ﴿but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah.﴾ He means: they do not deny you in secret, because they knew your truthfulness before, but they deny my revelation and reject my signs, as He said: "And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them" [Qur'an 27:14].

Al-Suddi said: Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq met Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and al-Akhnas said to Abu Jahl, "O Abu al-Hakam, tell me about Muhammad: is he truthful or a liar? Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verses 31–33:

﴿Indeed, they have lost who denied the meeting with Allah.﴾ That is, they lost themselves by denying their return to Allah through resurrection after death. ﴿Until, when the Hour came upon them suddenly﴾, that is, the Resurrection, ﴿suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, ﴿they said, "Alas for us!"﴾, meaning, "Our regret!" [It is mentioned] [[The words in brackets are missing from manuscript "A" and we have restored them from manuscript "B".]] in the form of a vocative, for emphasis. Sibawayh said: it is as if they are saying, "O regret, this is your time." ﴿for what we neglected﴾, that is, what we fell short in, ﴿concerning it﴾, that is, concerning obedience. It was also said: "what we left behind in the world of the deeds of the Hereafter."

Muhammad ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: [[See Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/325, where he says: "The 'ha' and 'alif' in His words 'concerning it' refer to 'the transaction'. But the mention of it was dispensed with, because His words 'Indeed, they have lost who denied the meeting with Allah' indicate it, since it is known that 'loss' can only occur in a transaction that has taken place."]] The pronoun refers to the transaction. When the loss of their transaction became clear to them, by their trading the Hereafter for this world, they said, "Alas for us, for what we neglected concerning it," that is, concerning the transaction. [So the mention of "the transaction" is omitted] [[See Tafsir al-Tabari, 11/325, with the same wording as above.]] being sufficiently indicated by His words ﴿have lost﴾, because loss only occurs in a transaction of sale. He says, "No." It says, "I am your good deed. Mount me, for you have often mounted me in the world." This is the meaning of His words, Mighty and Majestic: (On the Day We gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation) [Maryam 19:85], that is, as riders. As for the disbeliever, he is met by the ugliest thing in form and the foulest in scent, and it says, "Do you recognize me?" He says, "No." It says, "I am your evil deed. You have often mounted me in the world, so today I shall mount you." This is the meaning of His words: ﴿while they carry their burdens upon their backs﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, evil is what they bear﴾. [Regarding "they carry"], Ibn Abbas said: "Evil is the load they have carried."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 36–38:

﴿Only those who listen will respond.﴾ That is, the believers who listen to the Reminder, follow it and benefit from it, unlike those upon whose hearing Allah has set a seal. ﴿And the dead﴾ means the disbelievers. ﴿Allah will raise them up; then to Him they will be returned.﴾ Then He will recompense them for their deeds.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And they said﴾ meaning the leaders of Quraysh, ﴿"Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ "Why" (lawla) means "why not" (halla). ﴿Say: Indeed Allah is able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.﴾ That is, they do not know what would be upon them in sending it down.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor bird that flies on its two wings﴾. The flying is restricted to "its two wings" for emphasis, as one says, "I saw with my eyes" and "I took with my hand." ﴿but they are nations like you.﴾ Mujahid said: "They are classes, distinguished and known by their names." He means that every kind of animal is a nation: birds are a nation, quadrupeds are a nation, beasts of prey are a nation, each known by its name, just as the children of Adam are known by their names; it is said, "the mankind (al-Ins) and the people (al-Nas)."

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us: Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us: al-Mubarak, that is Ibn Fudalah, informed us, from al-Hasan, from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Were it not that dogs are a nation, I would have commanded their killing. So kill from them every all-black one." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Dahaya, chapter on keeping a dog for hunting and other purposes: 4/132–133; al-Tirmidhi in al-Sayd, chapter on what has been related about killing dogs: 5/63, and he said: a hasan sahih hadith; al-Nasa'i in al-Sayd wa'l-Dhaba'ih, chapter on the description of the dogs he commanded to be killed: 7/185; Ibn Majah in al-Sayd, chapter on killing dogs except a hunting or field dog, no. (3205): 2/1069; al-Darimi in al-Sayd, chapter on killing dogs: 2/90; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/54, 56; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/211.]]

It is also said: "nations like you" means they understand from one another. It is also said: "nations like you" in creation, death and resurrection. Ata said: "nations like you" in monotheism and knowledge of God. Ibn Qutaybah said: "nations like you" in nourishment, seeking sustenance, and avoiding destruction.

﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾ that is, in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), ﴿of anything; then to their Lord they will be gathered.﴾ Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: "Their gathering is their death." Abu Hurayrah said: "On the Day of Resurrection Allah will gather all creatures: the beasts, the animals, the birds, and everything. He will take retribution for the hornless (sheep) from the horned ones. Then He will say: 'Be dust.' At that point the disbeliever will wish and say: 'Would that I were dust!'"

Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan al-Taysafuni informed us: Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari informed us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani informed us: Ali ibn Hujr informed us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, from al-Ala', from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The rights will certainly be returned to their owners on the Day of Resurrection, to the point that the hornless sheep will be avenged against the horned one." [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Birr wa'l-Silah wa'l-Adab, chapter on the prohibition of injustice, no. (2582): 4/1997.]]

**The commentary on the words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb﴾**, meaning they neither hear goodness nor speak it. **﴿In darknesses﴾**, meaning in the misguidance of disbelief. **﴿Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path﴾**, which is Islam.

**His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Have you seen yourselves?﴾** That is, "Have you seen?" The *kaf* (the "-ka" in *ara'aytakum*) here serves for emphasis. Al-Farra' said: The Arabs say *ara'aytaka* while meaning "inform us," as one says: "*Ara'aytaka* if you do such-and-such, what will you do?", meaning "Inform me." The people of Madina recited *arā'aytakum*, *arā'aytum* and *arā'ayta* with the second hamza softened (*talyīn al-hamza*, meaning making the glottal stop between two vowels lighter, pronounced between a hamza and a y), and al-Kisa'i recited them with it omitted (*hadhf*, meaning dropping the second hamza entirely). Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: "Have you seen? ﴿If the punishment of Allah comes upon you﴾ before death, **﴿or the Hour comes upon you﴾**, meaning the Resurrection, **﴿will you call upon other than Allah﴾** to remove the punishment from you, **﴿if you are truthful﴾?" **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verses 44–46:**

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾: they abandoned what they had been admonished and commanded to do. ﴿We opened for them the gates of every thing﴾: Abu Ja'far recited "fattahna" (we opened, with emphatic doubling) throughout the whole Qur'an. Ibn 'Amir recited it the same way when it was followed by a plural, and the rest read it without doubling (fatahna). This opening is an opening of gradual enticement (istidraj, the gradual leading of a person into ruin through apparent favour) and deception. That is, We replaced hardship and adversity with ease and health. ﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given﴾: this is the rejoicing of arrogance, like the rejoicing of Qarun in what he had acquired of the world. ﴿We seized them suddenly﴾: unexpectedly, when they were most secure, and when the world was most pleasing to them. ﴿Then they were in despair﴾: hopeless of every good. Abu 'Ubayda said: "al-mublis" is the one who is regretful and grieved, and the root of iblas (despair) is lowering the head out of grief and remorse.

'Uqba ibn 'Amir narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If you see Allah giving the servant what he loves while he persists in his disobedience, then that is indeed istidraj." Then he recited, "So when they forgot what they had been reminded of..." to the end of the verse.[[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad (4/145). In its chain is Rushdin ibn Sa'd, who is weak. al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/245): "Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat from his teacher al-Walid ibn al-'Abbas al-Misri, who is weak," and he attributed it elsewhere (7/20) to Ahmad and al-Tabarani.]]

﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off﴾: that is, their last ones. [The words between the brackets are an addition from manuscript "B".] Its meaning is that they were utterly uprooted by the punishment, so that not one of them remained. ﴿And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾: Allah praised Himself for cutting off their remnant, because it was a blessing upon the messengers. He mentioned praise of Allah to teach them, and those who believed in them, to praise Allah for His sufficiency against the evil of the wrongdoers, and so that Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions would praise their Lord when He destroyed the deniers.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "Have you considered"﴾, O polytheists, ﴿if Allah took away your hearing﴾, so that you would hear nothing at all, ﴿and your sight﴾, so that you would see nothing, ﴿and sealed your hearts﴾, so that you would understand nothing and would not recognize anything of what you know of worldly affairs, ﴿who is the god other than Allah who could bring it to you?﴾ He did not say "bihā" (with it, feminine) even though He had mentioned several things. It was said: its meaning is "who could bring you back what was taken from you." It was also said: the pronoun refers to the hearing mentioned first, and the rest are included under it, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: (﴿Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾) (al-Tawbah, 62). The pronoun there refers to Allah, and the pleasure of His Messenger is included within the pleasure of Allah the Exalted. ﴿Look how We explain the signs﴾: that is, We make clear to them the signs that point to tawhid (the oneness of Allah) and to prophethood (nubuwwa). ﴿Yet they turn away﴾: they turn aside from them, denying.

He means: I do not tell you any of that, so you would deny my words and reject my affair. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: what I bring you is from the revelation of Allah the Exalted. That is not impossible in reason, given the presence of the proof and the conclusive arguments. ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ Qatadah said: the disbeliever and the believer. Mujahid said: the astray and the guided. It was also said: the ignorant and the knowledgeable. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾, meaning: they are not equal.

﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly﴾, unexpectedly, ﴿or openly﴾, visibly, so that you see it as it descends. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan said: by night or by day. ﴿Will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾ meaning the polytheists.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿We send the messengers only as bearers of good news and warners. So whoever believes and does righteous deeds﴾, meaning the deed, ﴿there will be no fear for them﴾, when the people of the Fire fear, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾, when they grieve.

﴿But those who deny Our signs, the punishment will touch them﴾, meaning it will befall them, ﴿for what they used to defiantly disobey﴾, meaning they disbelieved.

﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾. This was revealed when they demanded signs, so He commanded him to say to them: ﴿I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, meaning the treasuries of His provision, so that I would give you what you want. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, so that I could inform you of what is hidden, of the past and of what will be. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel.﴾ He said this because an angel has power over what a human cannot do and sees what a human cannot see. He means: I do not tell you any of that, so you would deny my words and reject my affair. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾, meaning: what I bring you is from the revelation of Allah the Exalted. That is not impossible in reason, given the presence of the proof and the conclusive arguments. ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?﴾ Qatadah said: the disbeliever and the believer. Mujahid said: the astray and the guided. It was also said: the ignorant and the knowledgeable. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾, meaning: they are not equal.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 51–52:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And warn with it﴾, meaning frighten with it, i.e., with the Qur'an, ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered﴾, meaning be assembled and raised up to their Lord. It was also said: "fear" here means "know," because their fear arose from their knowledge. ﴿They have, besides Him,﴾ besides God, ﴿no protector﴾, meaning no close relative who benefits them, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾, meaning one who intercedes for them, ﴿so that they may fear God﴾, and so refrain from what they have been forbidden. He negated intercession for anyone other than Him, although the prophets and the saints do intercede, because they intercede only by His permission.

﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited "bil-ghudwa" (بِالْغُدْوَةِ), with a ḍamma on the ghayn, a sukun on the dal, and a waw after it, both here and in Surat al-Kahf. The others recited it with a fatḥa on the ʿayn and the dal and an alif after it.

Salman and Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said: This verse was revealed concerning us. al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi, 'Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari and their companions from among those whose hearts were to be reconciled (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum, those whom the Muslims sought to win over to Islam) came and found the Prophet ﷺ sitting with Bilal, Suhayb, 'Ammar and Khabbab, along with some weak believers. When they saw them around him, they looked down on them, so they came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, if you sat at the head of the gathering and drove these people away from us, and their rough woolen cloaks, which were all they had, were removed, we would sit with you and take from you." The Prophet ﷺ said to them: "I am not one to drive away the believers." They said: "Then we wish that you would make for us a gathering of your own, by which the Arabs would recognize our merit, for the delegations of the Arabs come to you, and we are ashamed that the Arabs should see us with these slaves. So when we come to you, remove them from us, and when we have finished, sit with them if you wish." He said: "Yes." They said: "Write us a document to that effect." So he called for the parchment and called 'Ali to write it. They said, while we were sitting in a corner, Gabriel descended with the words: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance﴾ up to His words: ﴿among the grateful﴾. So the Messenger of God ﷺ threw the parchment from his hand, then called us, and we drew near. He was saying: (Peace be upon you. Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy). So we would sit with him, and when he wished to rise, he rose and left us. Then God, may He be exalted, revealed: (And keep yourself patient with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance) (al-Kahf, 28). After that the Messenger of God ﷺ would sit with us, and we would draw close to him until our knees nearly touched his knee. When the hour came for him to rise, we rose and left him until he stood up. He said to us: "Praise be to God who did not take my life until He commanded me to keep myself patient with a people from my community. With you is my living, and with you is my dying."[[Narrated by al-Tabari: 11/376–377, and Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, no. (4127): 2/382–383. In al-Zawa'id he said: its chain is authentic and its narrators are trustworthy. Part of it was also related by Muslim and al-Nasa'i from the hadith of Sa'd. See Sahih Muslim, Fada'il al-Sahaba, no. (2413): 4/1887. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir: 2/136 and said: "This is a strange hadith, for this verse is Meccan, and al-Aqra' ibn Habis and 'Uyayna only embraced Islam long after the Hijra." There is no basis for this strangeness, for when they said that they were not Muslims.]]

Al-Kalbi said: They said to him, "Set aside a day for us and a day for them." He said, "I will not do that." They said, "Then make the gathering one gathering: turn toward us and turn your back to them." So God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.

Mujahid said: The Quraysh said, "Were it not for Bilal and the son of Umm 'Abd [Ibn Mas'ud], we would have pledged allegiance to Muhammad." So God revealed this verse: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾.[[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr: 3/274 to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi Shayba, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: It means they worship their Lord morning and evening, that is, the dawn prayer (Subh) and the afternoon prayer ('Asr). It is also related from him that what is meant is the five daily prayers. That was because some poor believers were with the Prophet, peace be upon him, and some of the nobles said: "When we pray, put these people behind us, so that they may pray behind us." So the verse was revealed.

Mujahid said: I prayed the dawn prayer with Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. When the imam finished the greeting, the people rushed to the storyteller (al-qass). Sa'id said: "How quickly people hasten to this gathering!" Mujahid said: I said, "They interpret His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿who call upon their Lord morning and evening﴾." He said: "Is it about this? Rather, it refers to the prayer from which we have just turned away."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: It means they remember their Lord. It was also said that what is meant is the actual supplication (du'a').

﴿Seeking His countenance﴾, meaning they seek God through their obedience. Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: They seek the reward of God.

Then He said: ﴿Nothing of their reckoning is upon you, and nothing of your reckoning is upon them﴾, meaning you are not charged with their affairs, and they are not charged with yours. It was also said: their provision is not upon you, so that you should be weary of them, nor is your provision upon them. His words ﴿so you would drive them away﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿Nothing of their reckoning is upon you﴾, and His words ﴿and you would be among the wrongdoers﴾ are the answer to His words ﴿And do not drive away﴾. The first is the answer to the negation, and the second is the answer to the prohibition.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 53–54:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And thus We have tried some of them by means of others﴾, meaning: We tested them. He intended the testing of the rich by the poor and of the noble by the lowly. That is because when the noble man sees the lowly man has preceded him in faith, he refrains from Islam on account of him, and so this becomes a trial for him. This is His saying: ﴿so that they say, "Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?"﴾ Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ This is the answer to their saying ﴿Is it these whom Allah has favoured from among us?﴾, and it is a rhetorical question in the sense of affirmation, meaning: Allah knows best who is thankful for Islam, since Allah, mighty and majestic, has guided him.

Al-Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu al-'Abbas 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Harun al-Taysafuni informed us: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Turabi related to us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn Bistam related to us: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Sayyar al-Qurashi related to us: Musaddad informed us: Ja'far ibn Sulayman related to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, from al-'Ala' ibn Bashir al-Muzani, from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I sat in a group of poor emigrants, and some of them were covering themselves with others because of their nakedness, and a reciter was reciting to us. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came and stood over us. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood, the reciter fell silent. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greeted us with salam and said: "What were you doing?" We said: "O Messenger of Allah, a reciter was reciting to us, and we were listening to the Book of Allah, the Exalted." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Praise be to Allah who has placed among my community those whom He commanded me to keep myself patient with." He said: Then he sat among us so that he might make himself one of us, and then he gestured with his hand, "like this," and they formed a circle, and their faces were displayed before him. He said: I did not see the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recognize any of them except me. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O assembly of the destitute emigrants, with complete light on the Day of Resurrection: you will enter Paradise before the wealthy of people by half a day, and that is the equivalent of five hundred years." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in the Book of Knowledge, chapter on stories: 5/255. Al-Mundhiri said: "In its chain is Ziyad ibn al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad, Abu al-Hasan, and there is some criticism of him. Ahmad narrated it: 3/63, 96, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. The author [al-Baghawi] also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/191. It has a supporting narration in al-Tirmidhi (Zuhd), Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban, so it is strengthened by it.]].

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you, say: Peace be upon you﴾. 'Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning those whom Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade His Prophet from driving away, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) saw them, he would begin with the greeting of peace [[See: al-Tabari: 11/380; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 252.]].

And 'Ata' said: It was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Bilal, Salim, Abu 'Ubaydah, Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, Hamzah, Ja'far, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, 'Ammar ibn Yasir, al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, and Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Asad, may Allah be pleased with them all.

﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, meaning: He has decreed for Himself mercy. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance﴾. Mujahid said: he does not know the lawful from the unlawful, so out of his ignorance he commits the sin. It was also said: he is ignorant of what that sin will bring upon him. It was also said: his ignorance is that he preferred disobedience over obedience and the small, immediate gain over the great, deferred reward. ﴿Then repents after that﴾, meaning: returns from his sin. ﴿And amends﴾ his conduct. It was said: he makes his repentance sincere. ﴿Then indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾ Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim and Ya'qub read ﴿that whoever of you does﴾ and ﴿then indeed He is Forgiving, Merciful﴾ with a fatha on the alif in both places, as a substitution for "mercy." The meaning is: He prescribed for Himself that whoever of you does [evil], then He made the second as a substitution for the first, like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Does he promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will indeed be brought forth?﴾ (al-Mu'minun: 35). The people of Madinah read the first of them with a fatha and the second with a kasra, as a new sentence, and the others read both with a kasra as new sentences.
