Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 55–56:

﴿And thus do We detail the signs﴾, i.e., thus indeed. It is also said: its meaning is, "Just as We have detailed for you in this surah Our proofs and Our declarations against the polytheists, thus do We detail the signs," i.e., We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof in every truth that the people of falsehood deny. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾, i.e., the path of the criminals. The people of Madinah read "wa-litastabina" with a ta' (feminine), and "sabila" is in the accusative, addressing the Prophet ﷺ: i.e., "and that you, O Muhammad, may know the way of the criminals." It is said: istabtu al-shay' and tabayyantuhu, meaning "I came to know the thing." Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read "wa-liyastabina" with a ya' (masculine), and "sabilu" in the nominative. The others read "wa-litastabina" with a ta' and "sabilu" in the nominative, i.e., that the way may become manifest and clear. The word sabil (way) may be treated as masculine or feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And if they see the way of rectitude, they will not adopt it as a way﴾ (al-A'raf, 146). The evidence for the feminine is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ (Al 'Imran, 99).

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah. Say: I will not follow your desires﴾ in worshipping idols and in driving away the poor, ﴿for then I would have gone astray, and I would not be of the guided﴾. Meaning: if I were to do that, I would have abandoned the way of truth and taken a path other than the way of guidance.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 55–56:

﴿And thus do We detail the signs﴾, i.e., thus indeed. It is also said: its meaning is, "Just as We have detailed for you in this surah Our proofs and Our declarations against the polytheists, thus do We detail the signs," i.e., We distinguish and make clear to you Our proof in every truth that the people of falsehood deny. ﴿And that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾, i.e., the path of the criminals. The people of Madinah read "wa-litastabina" with a ta' (feminine), and "sabila" is in the accusative, addressing the Prophet ﷺ: i.e., "and that you, O Muhammad, may know the way of the criminals." It is said: istabtu al-shay' and tabayyantuhu, meaning "I came to know the thing." Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read "wa-liyastabina" with a ya' (masculine), and "sabilu" in the nominative. The others read "wa-litastabina" with a ta' and "sabilu" in the nominative, i.e., that the way may become manifest and clear. The word sabil (way) may be treated as masculine or feminine. The evidence for the masculine is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And if they see the way of rectitude, they will not adopt it as a way﴾ (al-A'raf, 146). The evidence for the feminine is His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Why do you bar from the way of Allah those who believe, seeking to make it crooked?﴾ (Al 'Imran, 99).

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides Allah. Say: I will not follow your desires﴾ in worshipping idols and in driving away the poor, ﴿for then I would have gone astray, and I would not be of the guided﴾. Meaning: if I were to do that, I would have abandoned the way of truth and taken a path other than the way of guidance.

﴿Say: "Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord, and you have denied it"﴾, meaning: upon clarity, insight and proof. ﴿"and you have denied it"﴾, meaning: what I have brought. ﴿"What you seek to hasten is not with me"﴾. It was said that this refers to their seeking to hasten the punishment. They used to say: "If this is the truth from You, then rain down stones upon us" (Al-Anfal, 32), and so on. It was also said that it refers to the Resurrection, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾ (Ash-Shura, 18).

﴿"The decision is only for Allah; He relates the truth"﴾. The people of the Hijaz and ʿĀṣim recited *yaqussu* with a *ḍamma* on the *qāf* and a shadda on the *ṣād*, meaning *yaqūlu al-ḥaqq* ("He speaks the truth"). This is because in all the codices (*maṣāḥif*) it is written without a *yā'*, and because it says *al-ḥaqq* and not *bi-l-ḥaqq*. The others recited *yaqḍī* (﴿He decides﴾) with a *sukūn* on the *qāf* and a *kasra* on the *ḍād*, from *qaḍaytu* (I decided), meaning: He judges with the truth. The evidence for this is that He said: ﴿And He is the best of deciders﴾, and deciding (*al-faṣl*) occurs in judgment. They omitted the *yā'* because the *alif* and *lām* (of *al-ḥaqq*) are burdensome, as in His saying ﴿roasting in the Blazing Fire﴾ (As-Saffat, 163) and similar expressions. He did not say *bi-l-ḥaqq* because *al-ḥaqq* is an adjective of the verbal noun (*maṣdar*); it is as if He had said: "He decides the true decision."

﴿Say: "If what you seek to hasten were with me"﴾, meaning: in my power, ﴿"of punishment"﴾, ﴿"the matter would have been decided between me and you"﴾.

That is: the punishment would have been completed, [and you would have been destroyed] [[In manuscript B: "and you would have been destroyed."]], meaning: I would have hastened it so that I might be rid of you. ﴿"And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers"﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 59–60:

The Most High said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾. "Keys of the unseen" means His treasuries, the plural of miftah (key).

The scholars differed concerning "the keys of the unseen." Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Khirqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan al-Taysafuni informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Kushmihani informed us; 'Ali ibn Hujr informed us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar informed us that he heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five, none knows them but Allah: none knows what the wombs carry except Allah the Exalted, [and none knows what tomorrow holds except Allah the Mighty and Majestic] [[Omitted from "b".]] and none knows when the rain will come except Allah, and no soul knows in what land it will die, and none knows when the Hour will be established except Allah." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Istisqa', chapter "None knows when the rain will come except Allah": 2/524, and in the Book of Tawhid and in the Book of Tafsir. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/422.]]

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: the keys of the unseen are the treasuries of the earth and the knowledge of the descent of punishment.

'Ata' said: they are what is hidden from you of reward and punishment.

It was also said: they are the terms of lifespans. It was said: they are the states of the servants, whether of happiness or misery, and the endings of their deeds. It was said: they are what has not yet occurred, whether it will occur or not, how what will occur will occur, and what would occur were it to occur, how it would occur.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Your Prophet was given knowledge of everything except the knowledge of the keys of the unseen." [[Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Ya'la, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, Majma' al-Zawa'id: 8/263. See also Fath al-Bari: 1/124 and 8/291; 'Alam al-Ghayb wa al-Shahadah by 'Uthman Jum'ah Dumairiyyah, pp. 80–81.]]

﴿And He knows what is on the land and in the sea﴾. Mujahid said: "the land" means the deserts and wastelands, and "the sea" means the towns and cities; nothing happens in them without His knowing it. It was also said: it refers to the land and the sea in their well-known sense.

﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it﴾: he means falling and remaining, that is, He knows the number of what falls from the leaves of trees and what remains upon them. It was said: He knows how many times it turned from its back to its belly until it fell to the ground.

﴿Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth﴾: it was said this is the well-known grain in the depths of the earth. It was said it is beneath the rock in the lowest parts of the earths.

﴿Nor anything fresh or dry﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "the fresh" is water and "the dry" is the desert. 'Ata' said: he means what grows and what does not grow. It was said: it means neither living nor dead. It was said: it is an expression for everything.

﴿Except that it is in a Clear Record﴾: meaning that all of it is written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

The Most High said: ﴿And it is He who takes your souls by night﴾, that is, He seizes your spirits when you sleep at night. ﴿And He knows what you have earned﴾, that is, what you have committed, ﴿by day. Then He raises you up therein﴾, that is, He wakes you during the day, ﴿that a specified term may be fulfilled﴾, meaning the term of life until death, he means the full completion of lifespan. ﴿Then to Him is your return﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿Then He will inform you﴾, that is, He will tell you, ﴿of what you used to do﴾.

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verses 61–63:**

His Exalted and Majestic words: ﴿He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends guardians over you﴾. He means: the angels who guard the deeds of the children of Adam. It is the plural of *hafiz* (guardian). Its parallel is: "Indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders" (al-Infitar, 11). ﴿Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him (tawaffathu)﴾. Hamzah read (tuwaffihi) and (istahwihi) with a *ya'* and used *imalah* (vocal inclination) for both. ﴿Our messengers﴾ means the assistants of the Angel of Death, who seize him and then hand him over to the Angel of Death, who takes his soul, as He said: "Say: The Angel of Death who has been charged with you will take you" (al-Sajdah, 11). It is also said that the assistants take him by the command of the Angel of Death, so the Angel of Death is considered to have taken him, because they act upon his command. It is also said that by "the messengers" He meant the Angel of Death alone, and used the plural form for the singular. It has come in reports that Allah, Exalted is He, placed this world before the Angel of Death like a small table, so he takes from here and from there. When the souls become many, he calls the souls and they respond to him. ﴿And they do not fail﴾ means they do not fall short.

﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master (mawlahum al-haqq)﴾. It means the angels. It is also said that it means the servants, who are returned at death to Allah, their true Master. If it is asked: this verse concerns both believers and disbelievers, yet in another verse He said: "And the disbelievers have no protector (mawla)" (Muhammad, 11). How then is the verse reconciled? It is answered: *mawla* in that verse means a helper, and the disbelievers have no helper. Here *mawla* means the King who manages their affairs, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the Owner of all and the Manager of affairs. It is also said that here He meant only the believers, who are returned to their Master, while the disbelievers are followers in this matter. ﴿Verily, judgment belongs to Him﴾, that is, the decision belongs to Him alone, not to His creation. ﴿And He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾, that is, when He reckons, His reckoning is swift, because He does not need thought, observation, or counting on the fingers.

His Exalted and Majestic words: ﴿Say: Who rescues you﴾. Ya'qub read it with *takhfif* (lightened form), while the majority read it with *tashdid* (doubled form). ﴿From the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾, that is, from their hardships and terrors. When they traveled by land and sea and lost the way and feared destruction, they called upon Allah, sincerely devoting religion to Him, and He rescued them. This is His statement: ﴿calling upon Him humbly and secretly﴾, that is, openly and privately. Abu Bakr reported from 'Asim (*wa khifyah*) with a kasra on the *kha'* here and in al-A'raf, while the others read it with a damma. Both are dialects. ﴿If He rescues us﴾, that is, they say: "If You rescue us." The people of Kufa read: "If Allah rescues us" (anjana Allah). ﴿From this﴾, meaning from these darknesses. ﴿We will surely be among the grateful.﴾ Gratitude (shukr) is recognizing the blessing together with fulfilling its due.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 64–65:

﴿Say, "It is Allah who delivers you from them and from every distress."﴾ The people of Kufa and Abu Ja'far read "yunajjikum" (delivers you) with the doubled letter (tashdid), like His saying: ﴿Say, "Who delivers you?"﴾ The others read this with a single letter (takhfif). ﴿And from every distress﴾: al-Karb (distress) is the utmost grief that seizes the soul. ﴿Then you associate partners﴾: He means that they acknowledge that the One they call upon in hardship is the One who delivers them, then they associate with Him the idols, which they know neither harm nor benefit.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say, "He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you"﴾. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: the verse was revealed concerning the people of faith; and others said it was revealed concerning the polytheists.

His saying ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ means: the Blast, the stones, the wind and the flood, as He did to 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Shu'ayb, the people of Lut and the people of Nuh. ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾ means: the earthquake and the sinking into the earth, as He did to the people of Shu'ayb and to Qarun.

From Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ refers to the oppressive rulers, and ﴿from beneath your feet﴾ refers to the evil slaves. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿from above you﴾ means from the direction of your elders, ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means from below you, ﴿or confuse you into sects﴾ means mixing you into factions and spreading among you divergent desires, ﴿and make some of you taste the violence of others﴾ means the various swords, with some of you killing others.

Akhbarana 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi: Ana Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi: Ana Muhammad ibn Yusuf: Ana Muhammad ibn Isma'il: Ana Abu al-Nu'man: Ana Hammad ibn Zayd, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Jabir, who said: When this verse was revealed, ﴿Say, "He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you"﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I seek refuge in Your face." He then said: ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾, and he said, "I seek refuge in Your face." He said: ﴿or confuse you into sects and make some of you taste the violence of others﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "This is easier, or this is less." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Surah al-An'am, chapter "Say, He is able to send upon you ..." 8/291, and in al-I'tisam and al-Tawhid. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/217.]]

Akhbarana Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi: Ana Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri: Ana Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali Duhaym al-Shaybani: Akhbarana Ahmad ibn Hazim ibn Abi Gharazah: Ana Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd al-Tanafisi: Ana 'Uthman ibn Hakim, from 'Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, who said: We set out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until we passed by the mosque of Banu Mu'awiyah. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 64–65:

﴿Say, "It is Allah who delivers you from them and from every distress."﴾ The people of Kufa and Abu Ja'far read "yunajjikum" (delivers you) with the doubled letter (tashdid), like His saying: ﴿Say, "Who delivers you?"﴾ The others read this with a single letter (takhfif). ﴿And from every distress﴾: al-Karb (distress) is the utmost grief that seizes the soul. ﴿Then you associate partners﴾: He means that they acknowledge that the One they call upon in hardship is the One who delivers them, then they associate with Him the idols, which they know neither harm nor benefit.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say, "He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you"﴾. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: the verse was revealed concerning the people of faith; and others said it was revealed concerning the polytheists.

His saying ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ means: the Blast, the stones, the wind and the flood, as He did to 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Shu'ayb, the people of Lut and the people of Nuh. ﴿Or from beneath your feet﴾ means: the earthquake and the sinking into the earth, as He did to the people of Shu'ayb and to Qarun.

From Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid: ﴿a punishment from above you﴾ refers to the oppressive rulers, and ﴿from beneath your feet﴾ refers to the evil slaves. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿from above you﴾ means from the direction of your elders, ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾ means from below you, ﴿or confuse you into sects﴾ means mixing you into factions and spreading among you divergent desires, ﴿and make some of you taste the violence of others﴾ means the various swords, with some of you killing others.

He then said: ﴿or from beneath your feet﴾, and he said, "I seek refuge in Your face." He said: ﴿or confuse you into sects and make some of you taste the violence of others﴾, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "This is easier, or this is less." ﴿And your people denied it﴾, that is, the Qur'an. It was also said: the punishment. ﴿Yet it is the truth.﴾ Say: ﴿I am not a guardian over you﴾, that is, a watcher, and it was also said: one empowered to compel you to Islam whether you wish or refuse. ﴿I am only a messenger.﴾

﴿For every news﴾, that is, every report of the histories of earlier generations, ﴿there is a fixed time﴾, a reality and an end to which it arrives, whereby its truth is distinguished from its falsehood and its right from its wrong, either in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿And you will come to know﴾. Muqatil said: for every report that Allah gives, there is a time that He has set and a place where it occurs, without any failure or delay. Al-Kalbi said: for every saying and every deed there is a reality, either in this world or in the Hereafter. ﴿And you will come to know﴾: what was in this world, you will recognize it, and what was in the Hereafter, it will become manifest to you.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses﴾, meaning: concerning the Qur'an, with mockery, ﴿then turn away from them﴾, leave them, ﴿until they engage in talk about something else. And if Satan causes you to forget﴾. Ibn 'Amir recited it with a fatha on the nun and a shaddah on the sin, while the others recited it with a sukun on the nun and without a shaddah on the sin. ﴿[Satan]﴾ is the subject. ﴿So do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: if you sit with them forgetfully, then leave their company once you have remembered.

﴿Nor is anything upon those who fear Allah for their account﴾: it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: when this verse was revealed, ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, then turn away from them﴾, the Muslims said: how can we sit in the Sacred Mosque and circumambulate the House while they are constantly engaged in vain talk? In another narration, the Muslims said: we fear sin when we leave them and do not forbid them. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Nor is anything upon those who fear Allah﴾, that is, from engaging in such talk, ﴿for their account﴾, that is, for the sins of those who engage in it, ﴿anything; but it is a reminder﴾, that is, remind them and admonish them with the Qur'an. The dhikr and the dhikra are one and the same; the meaning is: remind them of My reminder, so that it is in the accusative position. ﴿That perhaps they may fear Allah﴾ from such talk when you admonish them. Thus he permitted sitting with them for the purpose of admonition, perhaps it will restrain them from that vain talk. It was also said: perhaps they will feel shame.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 70–71:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion﴾, meaning: the disbelievers who, when they hear the signs of Allah, mock them and play around when they are mentioned. It is also said: Allah the Exalted made for every people a festival (ʿid), so every people took their religion, that is their festival, as amusement and diversion. The festival of the Muslims is the prayer, the takbir, and doing good, such as the Friday (Jumu'ah), the Fast-Breaking (al-Fitr), and the Sacrifice (al-Nahr). ﴿And the worldly life has deceived them, but remind by it﴾, that is, admonish with the Qur'an. ﴿Lest a soul be given up﴾, that is, lest it be delivered up, that is, handed over, ﴿a soul﴾ to destruction, ﴿for what it has earned﴾. This was said by Mujahid, ʿIkrimah and al-Suddi. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it perishes. Qatadah said: it is held back. al-Dahhak said: it is burned. Ibn Zayd said: it is seized. Its meaning is: remind them so that they may believe, lest a soul perish for what it has earned. Al-Akhfash said: tubsal means "is requited." It was also said: "is disgraced." al-Farra' said: "is held in pledge." The original meaning of al-ʾibsal is prohibition, and al-basl is the forbidden; then it was made a description of every severe hardship that is feared and avoided. ﴿It shall have no﴾, that is, that soul shall have no, ﴿besides Allah any protector﴾, nearby, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ who intercedes in the Hereafter, ﴿and if it offers every compensation﴾, that is, ransoms with every ransom, ﴿it will not be accepted from it.﴾ ﴿Those are the ones who are given up﴾, delivered to destruction, ﴿for what they earned. For them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because they used to disbelieve.﴾

﴿Say: Shall we invoke, besides Allah, that which neither benefits us﴾ if we worship it, ﴿nor harms us﴾ if we abandon it, meaning: the idols, in which there is neither benefit nor harm, ﴿and be turned back on our heels﴾ to polytheism [apostatizing] [[In "B": (mutaraddidin).]] ﴿after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have lured away in the earth﴾, that is: our situation would be like the situation of one whom the devils have lured away, that is, misled, ﴿bewildered﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "like one whom the ghouls have lured in the wilderness (mahamah) and misled, so he is bewildered and lost." Al-ḥayrān is one who hesitates in a matter and cannot find a way out of it. ﴿He has companions who call him to the guidance: "Come to us."﴾ This is a parable which Allah the Exalted has struck for one who calls to idols and for one who calls to Allah the Exalted: it is like a man in a traveling company whom the ghoul has led astray from the road, while his companions from among the caravan call him: "Come to the road!" and the ghoul calls him [come] [[Addition from "B".]], so he remains bewildered, not knowing where to go. If he answers the ghoul, it carries him off until it casts him into ruin; and if he answers those who call him to the road, he is guided. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 11/452.]]

﴿Say: Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the guidance﴾; it restrains from worshipping idols, as if he were saying: do not do that, for the guidance is the guidance of Allah, not any other guidance. ﴿And we have been commanded to submit﴾, that is, that we submit, ﴿to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ The Arabs say: "I commanded you to do" and "that you do" and "in that you do."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 72–73:

﴿And that you establish the prayer and fear Him.﴾ That is: "And we have been commanded to establish the prayer (salah) and to have taqwa (God-consciousness)." ﴿And it is He to whom you will be gathered.﴾

That is: you will be assembled at the Standing (al-mawqif) for the reckoning (hisab).

﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth.﴾ It has been said: the "ba" (in bi-al-haqq) carries the meaning of "lam", that is, "to make the truth manifest," because He made His handiwork a proof of His oneness. ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is.﴾ It has been said: this refers to the heavens and the earth and the creation, in the sense of the decree (al-qada') and the measuring (al-taqdir); that is, every thing that He decreed and measured, He said to it, "Be," and it is.

It has also been said: it refers to the Resurrection (al-qiyamah), indicating the swiftness of the matter of the Resurrection and the Hour, as if He said: and on the day He says to the creation, "Die," and they die, and "Rise," and they rise. ﴿His word is the truth﴾, that is, the true reality that will certainly occur; He means that what He promised is true and will come to pass. ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown.﴾ He means: the dominion of kings on that day is gone, like His saying: "Master of the Day of Judgment," and as He said: "And the command on that day is for Allah." The command belongs to Him at all times, but on that day no one has any command alongside the command of Allah. The Sur (Trumpet) is a horn into which one blows. Mujahid said: "It is like the shape of a bugle (buq)." It has been said: it is in the language of the people of Yemen. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-sur is al-suwar, which is the plural of al-surah (form), and this is the saying of al-Hasan. The first is more correct.

The evidence for this is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah [ibn Abi Tawbah: Abu Tahir al-Muharibi told us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i told us: Abu 'Abd Allah] [[Omitted from manuscript "a".]] ibn Mahmud told us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khallal told us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Aslam, from Bishr ibn Shighaf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "What is the Sur?" He said: "A horn that is blown into." Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 72–73:

﴿And that you establish the prayer and fear Him.﴾ That is: "And we have been commanded to establish the prayer (salah) and to have taqwa (God-consciousness)." ﴿And it is He to whom you will be gathered.﴾

That is: you will be assembled at the Standing (al-mawqif) for the reckoning (hisab).

﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth.﴾ It has been said: the "ba" (in bi-al-haqq) carries the meaning of "lam", that is, "to make the truth manifest," because He made His handiwork a proof of His oneness. ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is.﴾ It has been said: this refers to the heavens and the earth and the creation, in the sense of the decree (al-qada') and the measuring (al-taqdir); that is, every thing that He decreed and measured, He said to it, "Be," and it is.

It has also been said: it refers to the Resurrection (al-qiyamah), indicating the swiftness of the matter of the Resurrection and the Hour, as if He said: and on the day He says to the creation, "Die," and they die, and "Rise," and they rise. ﴿His word is the truth﴾, that is, the true reality that will certainly occur; He means that what He promised is true and will come to pass. ﴿And His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown.﴾ He means: the dominion of kings on that day is gone, like His saying: "Master of the Day of Judgment," and as He said: "And the command on that day is for Allah." The command belongs to Him at all times, but on that day no one has any command alongside the command of Allah. The Sur (Trumpet) is a horn into which one blows. Mujahid said: "It is like the shape of a bugle (buq)." It has been said: it is in the language of the people of Yemen. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-sur is al-suwar, which is the plural of al-surah (form), and this is the saying of al-Hasan. The first is more correct.

The evidence for this is what Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah [ibn Abi Tawbah: Abu Tahir al-Muharibi told us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i told us: Abu 'Abd Allah] [[Omitted from manuscript "a".]] ibn Mahmud told us: Ibrahim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Khallal told us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Aslam, from Bishr ibn Shighaf, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, who said: A Bedouin came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "What is the Sur?" Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 74–76 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. Ya'qub (Yaʿqub) read "Āzaru" in the nominative (raf'), meaning "Āzaru" (as a vocative or in apposition). The well-known reading is in the accusative (naṣb). It is a non-Arabic proper noun (ism aʿjamī) that does not take nunation (lā yanṣarif), so it takes the accusative in the position of the genitive (khafḍ).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi said: Azar is the name of Abraham's father, and he is also Tarakh, like Isra'il and Ya'qub. He was from Kuthā [[Pronounced with a damma then sukun, the tā' is triangular (muthallatha), and it is an alif maqsura, written with a yā' because it is the fourth letter of the name. See: Mu'jam al-Buldan 4/487.]], a village in the outskirts of Kufa. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and others said: Azar is a title (laqab) of Abraham's father, and his name was Tarakh.

Sulayman al-Taymi said: it is an insult and a defect, and its meaning in their speech is "the crooked one." It was also said: its meaning in Persian is "the old man, the feeble." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Mujahid said: Azar is the name of an idol. According to this, it is in the place of the accusative, its implied sense being: "Do you take Azar as gods?" — His saying: ﴿idols as gods﴾ besides God, ﴿Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error﴾.

﴿And thus did We show Abraham﴾, i.e., just as We granted him insight into his religion and the truth in opposition to his people, We showed him ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾. Malakut means dominion (al-mulk); the tā' was added to it for emphasis, like jabarut, rahamut and rahbut. Ibn Abbas said: it means the creation of the heavens and the earth. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means the signs of the heavens and the earth. That is because he was placed upon a rock, and the heavens and the earth were uncovered for him, up to the Throne and the lowest of the earths, and he looked at his place in Paradise. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾, meaning: We showed him his place in Paradise.

It is narrated from Salman, may Allah be pleased with him, and some of them raised it [from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him] [[Omitted in manuscript "B".]]: When Abraham was shown the dominion of the heavens and the earth, he saw a man committing an immorality, so he invoked a curse upon him and he perished. Then he saw another and invoked a curse upon him and he perished. Then he saw yet another and wanted to invoke a curse upon him, so the Lord, mighty and majestic, said to him: "O Abraham, you are a man whose supplication is answered, so do not curse My servants, for I have three ways with a servant: either he repents and I accept his repentance, or I bring forth from him a soul that worships Me, or he is brought to Me, and if I wish I pardon him, and if I wish I punish him." In another narration: "Or he turns away, for Hell is behind him." [[Al-Suyuti said in al-Durr al-Manthur 3/302: "Narrated by ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim from Shahr ibn Hawshab. Shahr is truthful but frequently mistaken."]]

Qatada said: the dominion of the heavens is the sun, the moon and the stars, and the dominion of the earth is the mountains, the trees and the seas.

﴿And that he might be among the certain﴾ is a conjunction upon the meaning. Its meaning: We showed him the dominion of the heavens and the earth so that he might draw evidence from it and so that he might be among the certain.

﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star﴾ – the verse. The people of tafsir said: Abraham, peace be upon him, was born in the time of Nimrod ibn Kan'an. Nimrod was the first to place a crown upon his head and to call the people to worship him. He had soothsayers and astrologers, who said to him: "A boy will be born in your land this year who will change the religion of the people of the earth, and your destruction and the end of your kingdom will be at his hands." It is said that they found this in the books of the prophets, peace be upon them.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod saw in his dream as if a star had risen and had taken away the light of the sun and the moon until neither of them had any light. He was terrified by this with great terror, so he summoned the sorcerers and the priests and asked them about it. They said: "He is a boy who will be born in your region this year, and your destruction, the destruction of your kingdom and the people of your household will be at his hands." They said: So he ordered the slaughter of every boy born in his region that year, and he ordered that men be separated from women. He set one man over every ten men, and when a woman menstruated he let her be with her husband, because they did not have intercourse during menstruation; but when she became pure he kept them apart. Azar returned and found his wife had become pure from menstruation, so he lay with her, and she conceived Abraham, peace be upon him. [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur 3/304. We mention here again that these details which the author, may Allah have mercy on him, related do not have any authentic text that must be relied upon, and understanding the verses does not depend on these reports and traditions.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Nimrod sent to every pregnant woman in the town and detained her with him, except for the mother of Abraham, peace be upon him, for he did not know of her pregnancy because she was a young girl whose pregnancy did not show in her belly.

Al-Suddi said: Nimrod took the men out to a camp and kept them away from the women, out of fear that this child would come to be. He remained like this for as long as God willed. Then he had a need in the city, and he did not entrust it to anyone of his people except Azar. He sent for him, summoned him and said to him: "I have a need which I wished to entrust to you, and I send no one but because of my trust in you. I swear to you that you must not approach your family." Azar said: "I am more protective of my religion than that." So he entrusted him with his need. He entered the city and fulfilled his need, then said: "If only I went in to my family and looked at them." When he looked at the mother of Abraham, peace be upon him, he could not restrain himself until he lay with her, and she conceived Abraham, peace be upon him.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: When Abraham's mother became pregnant, the soothsayers said to Nimrod: "The boy about whom we informed you has been conceived by his mother tonight." So Nimrod ordered the slaughter of the boys. When the time of Abraham's mother's delivery drew near and her labour pains seized her, she went out in flight, fearing that someone would notice her and kill her child. She gave birth to him in a dry river, then wrapped him in a cloth and placed him among reeds. She returned and informed her husband that she had given birth, and that the child was in such and such a place. His father went and took him from that place, dug a tunnel (sarab) for him beside a river, hid him in it, and closed its entrance with a rock for fear of wild beasts. His mother used to come to him and nurse him.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When the mother of Abraham felt the pains of labour, she went out at night to a cave near her, and gave birth to Abraham, peace be upon him, in it. She attended to what is done for a newborn, then sealed the cave over him and returned to her house. Then she would look in on him to see what had become of him, and find him alive, sucking his thumb.

Abu Rawq said: One day Abraham's mother said: "I will certainly look at his fingers." She found him sucking water from one finger, milk from another, honey from another, dates from another, and ghee from another.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Azar had asked the mother of Abraham about her pregnancy: "What became of it?" She said: "I bore a boy, but he died." He believed her and remained silent about it. The day for Abraham in youth was like a month, and the month like a year, so Abraham did not remain in the cave more than fifteen months until he said to his mother: "Bring me out." She brought him out in the evening, and he looked and reflected upon the creation of the heavens and the earth, and said: "Indeed He who created me, provided for me, fed me and gave me drink, is my Lord, and I have no god other than Him." Then he looked at the sky and saw a star and said: "This is my lord." Then he followed it with his gaze until it set. When it set, he said: "I do not love those that set." Then he saw the moon rising and said: "This is my lord," and he followed it with his gaze until it set. Then the sun rose, and so on to the end. Then he returned to his father Azar, his course having been made straight, and he knew his Lord and had disassociated himself from the religion of his people, except that he had not yet called them to it. So he informed his father that he was his son, and his mother informed him that he was his son, and told him what she had done concerning him. Azar was delighted by this and rejoiced with great joy.

It was said: he remained in the tunnel seven years; it was also said thirteen years, and it was also said seventeen years. They said: When Abraham, peace be upon him, grew up while he was in the tunnel, he said to his mother: "Who is my Lord?" She said: "I am." He said: "Then who is your lord?" She said: "Your father." He said: "Then who is the lord of my father?" She said to him: "Be quiet," and he was quiet. Then she returned to her husband and said: "Have you seen the boy about whom we were told that he would change the religion of the people of the earth? He is your son." Then she informed him of what he had said. His father Azar came to him, and Abraham, peace be upon him, said to him: "O father, who is my Lord?" He said: "Your mother." He said: "And who is my mother's lord?" He said: "I am." He said: "And who is your lord?" He said: "Nimrod." He said: "Then who is the lord of Nimrod?" So he struck him a slap and said: "Be quiet." When night covered him, he approached the entrance of the tunnel and looked through a gap in the rock, and saw a star, and said: "This is my lord."

It is said that he said to his parents: "Take me out." So they took him out of the tunnel, and they set off with him when the sun had set. Abraham looked at the camels, the horses and the sheep, and asked his father what these were. He said: "Camels, horses and sheep." He said: "There must be a lord and creator for these." Then he looked, and behold, Jupiter had risen; it is also said Venus. That night was at the end of the month, so the rising of the moon was delayed, and he saw the star before the moon. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿So when the night covered him﴾, i.e., entered. It is said: "The night covered (janna) and became dark (ajanna), and the night overcame him (janna-hu), and the night covered him (ajanna ʿalayhi) — it covers (yajinnu) with covering (junūnan and jinānan) when it grows dark and veils everything. The junūn of the night is its blackness." ﴿Saw a star﴾: Abu ʿAmr read "raʾā" with a fatḥa on the rāʾ and a kasra on the alif; Ibn ʿĀmir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read both with a kasra. If it is joined to a kāf or hāʾ, Ibn ʿĀmir gave both a fatḥa; if it is followed by a sākin, Hamza and Abu Bakr gave the rāʾ a kasra and the hamza a fatḥa, while the others gave both a fatḥa.

﴿He said: "This is my lord."﴾

They differed concerning his saying this. Some of them took it at face value and said: Abraham, peace be upon him, was seeking guidance and seeking monotheism, until God granted him success and gave him his right guidance, so this did not harm him in the state of reasoning. Also, this occurred in his childhood before the proof was established upon him, so it was not disbelief. [[This view was preferred by al-Tabari. It is not correct; the preponderant view is that Abraham, peace be upon him, was debating his people in this. See: Ibn Kathir 2/152.]]

Others rejected this view and said: It is not permissible for a messenger of God to reach a time at which he is not a monotheist who knows God and is free of every deity other than Him. How could this be imagined of one whom God protected, purified, and granted his right guidance beforehand, and about whom He informed, saying: "When he came to his Lord with a sound heart" (al-Saffat, 84), and said: "And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth" — do you think He showed him the dominion so that he would become certain, and when he became certain he saw a star and said: "This is my lord," believing in it? This is something that can never be.

Then they said: In it there are four aspects of interpretation:

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 74–76 (part 2 of 2):**

The first explanation: Abraham, peace be upon him, intended to draw the people on gradually with this statement, and to make them aware of their error and ignorance in exalting what they exalted. They used to exalt the stars and worship them, and they believed that all affairs were in their hands. So he showed them that he too exalted what they exalted and sought guidance from the same source they sought it from. Then, when it set, he showed them the deficiency that befalls the stars, in order to establish the error of what they claimed. A similar example is that of the Hawari (the helper) who came upon a people who worshipped an idol. He showed his reverence for it, and they honoured him, until they acted on his opinion in many matters. Then an enemy attacked them, and they consulted him about the matter. He said: "The opinion is that we call upon this idol so that it may remove from us what has come upon us." They gathered around it, humbling themselves. When it became clear to them that it neither benefits nor harms, he urged them to call upon God, so they called upon Him, and He turned away from them what they had feared, and they became Muslims.

The second interpretation: he said it in the form of a question, its implied meaning being: "Is this my lord?" Like the words of God Most High: ﴿Then if you die, will they be the immortals?﴾ (al-Anbiya, 34), meaning: "Will they then be the immortals?" He mentioned it in the form of rebuke, denouncing their act, meaning: "Would something like this be a lord?" That is, "This is not my lord."

The third interpretation: he said it by way of argument against them, saying: "Is this my lord according to your claim?" Then when it set, he said: "If it were a god, it would not have set." Like the words [﴿Taste it; indeed you are the mighty, the noble﴾] (al-Dukhan, 49), meaning: "In your own estimation and according to your claim." And like what He related about Moses, that he said: [﴿And look at your god to which you remained devoted; we will surely burn it﴾] (Ta-Ha, 97), meaning: "Your god according to your claim."

The fourth interpretation: there is an implied element, and its implied meaning is: "They say, 'This is my lord.'" Like His words: (﴿And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [they said], "Our Lord, accept from us"﴾) (al-Baqarah, 127), meaning: "They say, 'Our Lord, accept from us.'"

﴿Then when it set, he said, "I do not like those that set."﴾ That is, that which does not endure.

﴿When he saw the sun rising (bāzighatan), he said, "This is my lord, this is greater."﴾ That is, greater than the stars and the moon. He did not say "hādhihi" (the feminine form) even though al-shams (the sun) is feminine, because he meant "hādhā al-ṭāli'" (this rising one), or he referred it back to the meaning, which is light and brightness, because he saw it as brighter than the stars and the moon. ﴿When it set﴾, meaning it went down, ﴿he said, "O my people, I am free of what you associate with Allah."﴾

Allah the Exalted said: "His people argued with him. He said: Do you argue with me concerning Allah, when He has already guided me?" (6:80)

When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) returned to his father, and had reached a stage of youth, the hope of the sellers of idols (al-dhabbahin) fell away from him. Azar took him into his own household and began making idols and giving them to Ibrahim to sell. He would take them away and call out to whoever would buy what harms them and does not benefit them, but no one would buy them. When they had gone unsold for him, he would take them to a river, strike their heads in it, and say, "Drink," mocking his people and the misguidance they were in. His mockery of them spread among his people and the people of his town. So his people argued with him, that is, disputed with him and contended with him about his religion. "He said: Do you argue with me concerning Allah?" The people of Madina and Ibn Amir read the nun with tashdid... [sic]

Note: the passage as given reads: The people of Madina and Ibn Amir read it with the nun lightened (takhfif), and the others read it with tashdid (shaddah), assimilating one of the two nuns into the other (idgham). Whoever lightens it drops one of the two nuns for ease, meaning: "Do you dispute with me about the Oneness of Allah, when He has guided me to the Oneness and the truth?" "And I do not fear what you associate with Him" (6:80). This is because they said to him: "Beware of the idols, for we fear that they will touch you with harm, through madness or insanity, because of your insulting them." So he said to them: "And I do not fear what you associate with Him, except that my Lord wills something." This is not an exception from the first clause, but a disconnected exception (istithna' munqati'), meaning: "But if my Lord wills some harm, then what He wills will happen." "My Lord's knowledge encompasses all things" (6:80), that is, His knowledge surrounds everything. "Will you not then remember?" (6:80)

"And how should I fear what you associate (with Allah), while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has sent down to you no authority?" (6:81) That is, the idols, which neither see nor hear, nor harm nor benefit. "For which He has sent down to you no authority" means no proof or evidence. He is the Subduer, the Capable over all things. "So which of the two parties has more right" to security, "I or you, if you know?" (6:81)

Then Allah the Exalted said, judging between them: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾ — they do not mix their belief with polytheism (shirk) — ﴿for them there is security, and they are guided﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 85–89:

﴿And Zakariyya﴾ — he is Zakariyya son of Adhan; ﴿and Yahya﴾ — he is his son; ﴿and ʿIsa﴾ — he is the son of Maryam daughter of ʿImran; ﴿and Ilyas﴾ — concerning him they differed. Ibn Mas'ud said: he is Idris, and he has two names, like Ya'qub and Israil. The correct view, however, is that he is other than Idris, because Allah the Exalted mentioned him among the descendants of Nuh, whereas Idris was the grandfather of the father of Nuh. And Ilyas is Ilyas (Elias), son of Yasin, son of Finhas, son of ʿIzar, son of Harun, son of ʿImran. ﴿Each of them was among the righteous﴾.

﴿And Isma'il﴾ — he is the son of Ibrahim; ﴿and al-Yasaʿ﴾ — he is the son of Akhtub, son of al-ʿAjuz. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "wa-l-Yasaʿa" with a doubled lam and a sukun on the ya, here and in Sad. ﴿And Yunus﴾ — he is Yunus son of Matta; ﴿and Lut﴾ — he is Lut son of Haran, the nephew of Ibrahim. ﴿And each We preferred over the worlds﴾, i.e., the worlds of their own times.

﴿And of their fathers﴾ — min here is partitive, because some of their fathers were polytheists; ﴿and their offspring﴾, i.e., and of their offspring. He meant by it the offspring of some of them, because ʿIsa and Yahya had no children, and among the offspring of some of them there was one who was a disbeliever; ﴿and their brothers﴾; ﴿and We chose them﴾ — We selected them and preferred them; ﴿and guided them﴾ — We directed them; ﴿to a straight path﴾.

﴿That is the guidance of Allah﴾ — the religion of Allah; ﴿by which He guides﴾ — He directs by it; ﴿whomever He wills of His servants. And if they had associated﴾ — i.e., these whom We have named; ﴿then would have become void﴾ — would have been nullified and gone; ﴿from them is what they used to do﴾.

﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book﴾ — i.e., the revealed scriptures sent down to them; ﴿and the judgment﴾ — meaning knowledge and understanding; ﴿and prophethood. So if these disbelieve in them﴾ — the disbelievers, meaning the people of Makkah; ﴿then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them﴾ — meaning the Ansar and the people of Madinah. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid. Qatadah said: "If these disbelievers disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them" refers to the eighteen prophets whom Allah mentioned here. Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi said: its meaning is: if the people of the earth disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to the people of the heavens, who are the angels, who are not disbelievers in them.

And Ilyas is Ilyas (Elias), son of Yasin, son of Finhas, son of ʿIzar, son of Harun, son of ʿImran. ﴿Each of them was among the righteous﴾.

﴿And Isma'il﴾ — he is the son of Ibrahim; ﴿and al-Yasaʿ﴾ — he is the son of Akhtub, son of al-ʿAjuz. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "wa-l-Yasaʿa" with a doubled lam and a sukun on the ya, here and in Sad. ﴿And Yunus﴾ — he is Yunus son of Matta; ﴿and Lut﴾ — he is Lut son of Haran, the nephew of Ibrahim. ﴿And each We preferred over the worlds﴾, i.e., the worlds of their own times.

﴿And of their fathers﴾ — min here is partitive, because some of their fathers were polytheists; ﴿and their offspring﴾, i.e., and of their offspring. He meant by it the offspring of some of them, because ʿIsa and Yahya had no children, and among the offspring of some of them there was one who was a disbeliever; ﴿and their brothers﴾; ﴿and We chose them﴾ — We selected them and preferred them; ﴿and guided them﴾ — We directed them; ﴿to a straight path﴾.

﴿That is the guidance of Allah﴾ — the religion of Allah; ﴿by which He guides﴾ — He directs by it; ﴿whomever He wills of His servants. And if they had associated﴾ — i.e., these whom We have named; ﴿then would have become void﴾ — would have been nullified and gone; ﴿from them is what they used to do﴾.

﴿Those are the ones to whom We gave the Book﴾ — i.e., the revealed scriptures sent down to them; ﴿and the judgment﴾ — meaning knowledge and understanding; ﴿and prophethood. So if these disbelieve in them﴾ — the disbelievers, meaning the people of Makkah; ﴿then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them﴾ — meaning the Ansar and the people of Madinah. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid. Qatadah said: "If these disbelievers disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them" refers to the eighteen prophets whom Allah mentioned here. Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi said: its meaning is: if the people of the earth disbelieve in them, then We have entrusted them to the people of the heavens, who are the angels, who are not disbelievers in them.

Ma'alim al-Tanzil (the Commentary of al-Baghawi) on Surah 6, verses 90–91:

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided﴾, that is, Allah guided them. ﴿So follow their guidance﴾, that is, follow their way and their conduct. ﴿Iqtadih﴾ (follow him). The ha' in it is the ha' of pause (ha' al-waqf). Hamzah and al-Kisa'i omitted the ha' in continuous recitation (wasl), while the rest of the readers kept it both in continuous recitation and at pause. Ibn 'Amir read ﴿iqtadihi﴾ with the ha' vowelled by a kasrah (ishba' al-ha' kasran). ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it. It is only a reminder﴾, that is, an admonition and a warning, ﴿to the worlds﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾, that is, they did not magnify Him with His true magnificence. It is also said: they did not describe Him with His true description. ﴿When they said: Allah has not sent down anything to a human being﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man from the Jews called Malik ibn al-Sayf came to dispute with the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "I adjure you by Him who sent down the Torah to Musa, do you not find in the Torah that Allah hates the fat rabbi?" He was a fat rabbi, so he became angry and said: "By Allah, Allah has not sent down anything to a human being at all."[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (11/521–522), al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (p. 253), and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, from Ka'b as his own statement. It is also reported from Malik ibn Dinar who said: "I read in al-Hikmah: Indeed Allah hates every fat rabbi." It was attributed by al-Suyuti to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim, and abridged by Ibn Hisham in al-Sirah (1/547). In al-Maqasid al-Hasanah it is said: "I do not know of it as a marfu' report, except that Ahmad narrated in al-Musnad (3/471 and 4/339), and al-Hakim (4/121–122) said it is sahih in its chain and al-Dhahabi agreed, and al-Bayhaqi with a good chain, from Ja'dah al-Jushami that the Prophet ﷺ looked at a fat man, pointed to his belly, and said: "If this were in other than this, it would be better for you." It was attributed by al-Mundhiri in al-Targhib (3/138) to Ibn Abi al-Dunya and al-Tabarani with a good chain, and to al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi. See also: Tamyiz al-Tayyib min al-Khabith (p. 53), Kashf al-Khafa (1/289–290), Majma' al-Zawa'id (5/31), al-Durr al-Manthur (3/314), and al-Albani's Silsilat al-Da'ifah (3/265–267).]]

Al-Suddi said: It was revealed concerning Finhas ibn 'Azura', and he is the one who made this statement.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (11/522). Al-Suyuti attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. Al-Durr al-Manthur (3/314).]]

In the story: when the Jews heard that statement from him, they reproached him and said: "Did not Allah send down the Torah to Musa? Why did you say: Allah has not sent down anything to a human being?" Malik ibn al-Sayf said: "Muhammad angered me, so I said that." They said to him: "When you become angry, you say [about Allah] [[omitted from manuscript "b".]] what is not true." So they removed him from the rabbinical office (al-Hibriyyah) and put Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf in his place.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Jews said: "O Muhammad, has Allah sent down a book to you?" He said: "Yes." They said: "By Allah, Allah has not sent down any book from the heaven." So Allah revealed: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said: Allah has not sent down anything to a human being﴾. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Who sent down the Book which Musa brought, as light and guidance for mankind﴾, meaning the Torah,[[Narrated by al-Tabari (11/523).]] ﴿which you make into scrolls, displaying them and concealing much﴾, that is, you write from it notebooks and separate books, which you display, that is, you display what you like and conceal much of the description of Muhammad ﷺ and the verse of stoning. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read ﴿yaj'alunahu﴾, ﴿yubdunaha﴾ and ﴿yukhfunaha﴾ all with the letter ya' (third person), in accordance with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾. The others read with ta' (second person), in accordance with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Musa brought﴾.

His saying: ﴿And you were taught what you did not know﴾. Most of the commentators hold that this is an address to the Jews, meaning: you were taught through the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ what you did not know, ﴿neither you nor your fathers﴾. Al-Hasan said: The knowledge of what Muhammad ﷺ brought was given to them, but they neglected it and did not benefit from it. [The words between the brackets are omitted from manuscript "b".]

Mujahid said: This is an address to the Muslims, reminding them of the blessing in what He taught them through the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ.

﴿Say: Allah﴾. This refers back to His saying: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Musa brought﴾. If they answer you, well and good; otherwise, you say: Allah, that is, say: Allah sent it down. ﴿Then leave them in their idle talk, playing﴾.

﴿وَهَذَا كِتَابٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مُبَارَكٌ﴾ That is, the Qur'an is a blessed Book that We have sent down. ﴿مُصَدِّقُ الَّذِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَلِتُنْذِرَ﴾ [It confirms what came before it] and so that you (O Muhammad) may warn. Abu Bakr related from Asim: "وَلِيُنْذِرَ" with the yā' (ya), meaning: "and so that the Book may warn." ﴿أُمَّ الْقُرَى﴾ means Makkah. It was called Umm al-Qura (the Mother of Towns) because the earth was spread out from beneath it, so it is the origin of the whole earth, just as the mother is the origin of offspring. By it He means the people of Umm al-Qura. ﴿وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾ means the people of the whole earth, east and west. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ﴾ believe in it, that is, in the Book. ﴿وَهُمْ عَلَى صَلاتِهِمْ﴾ means the five prayers. ﴿يُحَافِظُونَ﴾ means they are constant in them. By this He means the believers.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى﴾ that is, who fabricated ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا﴾ a lie against God, claiming that God had sent him as a prophet, ﴿أَوْ قَالَ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ﴾ or who said, "It has been revealed to me," when nothing had been revealed to him. Qatadah said: It was revealed concerning Musaylimah the Liar of Banu Hanifah. He used to speak in rhymed prose and practise soothsaying. He claimed prophethood and asserted that God had revealed to him. He had sent two messengers to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Do you testify that Musaylimah is a prophet?" They said, "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Were it not that messengers are not killed, I would have struck off your necks." [[Related by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter on the delegation of Banu Hanifah and the hadith of Thumamah: 8/89, and in al-Ta'bir; and Muslim in al-Ru'ya, chapter on the dream of the Prophet (ﷺ), no. (2274): 4/1781, from Abu Hurayrah and from Ibn Abbas. The author also related it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/252.]]

Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Man'i'i related to us: Abu Tahir al-Ziyadi related to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan related to us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami related to us: Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma'mar related to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: Abu Hurayrah related to us, saying: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "While I was sleeping, I was brought the treasures of the earth, and two golden bracelets were placed in my hands. They were heavy upon me and troubled me. Then it was revealed to me that I should blow on them, so I blew, and they vanished. I interpreted them as the two liars between whom I am: the lord of San'a' and the lord of al-Yamamah." [[Related by Muslim in al-Ru'ya: 4/1781; Abd al-Razzaq: 11/99; al-Tabari: 11/535; Abu Dawud: 4/64; and Ahmad: 1/390.]] By "the lord of San'a'" he meant al-Aswad al-Ansi, and by "the lord of al-Yamamah" he meant Musaylimah the Liar.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ It is said: It was revealed concerning Abd Allah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh. He had embraced Islam and used to write for the Prophet (ﷺ). When he dictated to him, [the Prophet would say] "samī'an baṣīran," and he would write "ʿalīman ḥakīman"; and when he said "ʿalīman ḥakīman," he would write "ghafūran raḥīman." When the verse ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ سُلَالَةٍ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ (al-Mu'minun, 12) was revealed, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) dictated it to him, and Abd Allah was amazed at the detail of the creation of man, and said: "Blessed is God, the best of creators." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Write it, for thus was it revealed." Abd Allah doubted and said: "If Muhammad is truthful, then it has been revealed to me as it was revealed to him." So he apostatised from Islam and joined the polytheists. Then Abd Allah returned to Islam before the conquest of Makkah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) stopped at Marr al-Zahran. [[See: al-Tabari: 11/534, 535; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 254; al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/317.]]

Ghamarat is the plural of ghamrah, and the ghamrah of anything is its greatest part. Its original sense is that which covers things and conceals them; then it was used for hardships and distresses. ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَاسِطُو أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ stretching out their hands with punishment and striking, hitting their faces and their backs. It is also said: with the seizing of souls. ﴿أَخْرِجُوا﴾ that is, they say: "Bring out" ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمُ﴾ that is, your souls, unwillingly, because the soul of the believer eagerly goes forth to meet its Lord. Ibn Abbas said: His saying ﴿وَمَنْ قَالَ سَأُنْزِلُ مِثْلَ مَا أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ refers to the mockers. It is a reply to their saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشَاءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هَذَا﴾ ("If we wished, we could say the like of this").

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿إِذِ الظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَاتِ الْمَوْتِ﴾ in the agonies of death. Ghamarat is the plural of ghamrah, and the ghamrah of anything is its greatest part. Its original sense is that which covers things and conceals them; then it was used for hardships and distresses. ﴿وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ بَاسِطُو أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ stretching out their hands with punishment and striking, hitting their faces and their backs. It is also said: with the seizing of souls. ﴿أَخْرِجُوا﴾ that is, they say: "Bring out" ﴿أَنْفُسَكُمُ﴾ that is, your souls, unwillingly, because the soul of the believer eagerly goes forth to meet its Lord. The answer is omitted, meaning: if you could see them in this state, you would see a dreadful thing. ﴿الْيَوْمَ تُجْزَوْنَ عَذَابَ الْهُونِ﴾ that is, the punishment of humiliation, ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ غَيْرَ الْحَقِّ وَكُنْتُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهِ تَسْتَكْبِرُونَ﴾ "for what you used to say against God other than the truth, and because you were arrogant toward His signs," meaning you exalted yourselves above believing in the Qur'an and did not confirm it.

This is a report from Allah that He will say to the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time﴾, meaning barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, ﴿alone (furadā)﴾, meaning individually, with no wealth, wife, child, or servant with you. Furādā is the plural of fardān, like sakrān and sukārā (drunk), and kaslān and kusālā (lazy). Al-A'raj read it as fardā without an alif, like sukrā.

﴿And you have left behind﴾ meaning you abandoned ﴿what We bestowed upon you﴾ meaning what We gave you of wealth, children, and servants, ﴿behind your backs﴾ meaning behind your backs in the world.

﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners among you﴾. This is because the polytheists claimed that they worship the idols because they are Allah's partners and their intercessors with Him.

﴿Indeed, the bond between you has been severed﴾. The people of Madina, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs on the authority of 'Asim read "baynakum" with a fatha on the nun, meaning: indeed, what was between you of connection has been severed, or: the matter between you has been severed. The others read "baynukum" with a damma on the nun, meaning: indeed, your connection has been severed. This is like His saying: ﴿and the means of connection were cut off from them﴾ (al-Baqarah, 166), meaning the connections (al-wasalat). Al-bayn is one of the words with opposite meanings (al-adداد, words that carry two contrary senses): it can mean connection and it can mean separation.

﴿And what you used to claim has vanished from you﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verses 95–98:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Indeed, Allah splits the grain and the date-stone﴾. *Al-falq* means *al-shaqq* (splitting). Al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: its meaning is that He splits the grain from the ear of grain and the date-stone from the date palm, bringing forth the plant from it. *Al-habb* is the plural of *al-habbah*, which is a name for all seeds and grains, such as wheat, barley and maize, and everything that does not have a stone. [Al-Zajjaj said: He splits the dry grain and the dry stone, and brings forth green leaves from them.

Mujahid said: it refers to the two splittings that are in them, that is, He splits the grain to bring forth the plant from it, and splits the date-stone to bring forth the palm from it.] [[Omitted from "B".]]

*Al-nawa* is the plural of *al-nawah*, which is everything that is not a grain, such as dates, apricots and peaches, and the like.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ means: Creator of the grain and the date-stone. ﴿He brings the living out of the dead, and brings the dead out of the living. That is Allah, so how are you deluded?﴾ That is, how are you turned away from the truth?

﴿Splitter of the daybreak﴾: the one who splits the pillar of dawn from the darkness of the night and uncovers it, [which is the first that appears of the day; he means the originator of the dawn and its clarifier] [[Omitted from "B".]].

Al-Dahhak said: the Creator of the day. *Al-isbah* is a verbal noun like *al-iqbal* and *al-idbar*, and it means illumination; by it he meant the dawn.

﴿And He made the night a place of rest﴾, in which His creatures rest. The people of Kufa read *wa-ja'ala* in the past tense, and *al-layla* in the accusative case, following the *Mushaf* (the written codex of the Qur'an). Ibrahim al-Nakha'i read ﴿Splitter of the daybreak﴾ and ﴿He made the night a place of rest, and the sun and the moon a reckoning﴾. That is: He made the sun and the moon by a fixed reckoning, which they do not exceed, until they reach the farthest of their stations. *Al-husban* is a verbal noun like *al-hisab*. ﴿That is the decree of the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And He it is who made the stars for you﴾, that is, created them for you, ﴿so that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea﴾.

Allah, exalted is He, created the stars for several benefits:

The first of these is this: that the rider on the sea and the traveller in the deserts are guided by them at night to their destinations.

The second: that they are an adornment for the heaven, as He said: "And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps" (Al-Mulk, 5).

Among them: the stoning of the devils, as He said: "And We have made them missiles against the devils" (Al-Mulk, 5).

﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who know﴾.

﴿And He it is who brought you into being﴾, that is, created you and originated you, ﴿from a single soul﴾, meaning Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿Then there is a place of lodging and a place of storage﴾. Ibn Kathir and the people of Basra read *fa-mustaqirr* with a kasra on the qaf, meaning: among you is one who has a place of lodging, and among you is one who has a place of storage. The others read it with a fatha on the qaf, meaning: for you there is a place of lodging and a place of storage.

They differed concerning *al-mustaqarr* and *al-mustawda'*. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: the *mustaqarr* is in the womb until one is born, and the *mustawda'* is in the grave until one is resurrected.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata said: the *mustaqarr* is in the wombs of the mothers, and the *mustawda'* is in the loins of the fathers. This is the narration of Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn Abbas said to me, "Have you married?" I said, "No." He said: "Indeed, whatever is deposited in your back, Allah, mighty and majestic, will bring it forth."

It is narrated from Ubayy that he said: the *mustaqarr* is in the loins of the fathers, and the *mustawda'* is in the wombs of the mothers.

It was also said: the *mustaqarr* is in the womb, and the *mustawda'* is above the earth. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We cause to remain in the wombs what We will﴾ (Al-Hajj, 5).

Mujahid said: the *mustaqarr* is upon the surface of the earth in this world, and the *mustawda'* is with Allah in the Hereafter. Supporting this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and enjoyment for a time﴾ (Al-Baqarah, 36).

Al-Hasan said: the *mustaqarr* is in the graves and the *mustawda'* is in this world. He used to say: "O son of Adam, you are a deposit within your family, and soon you will join your companion."

It was also said: the *mustawda'* is the grave, and the *mustaqarr* is Paradise and Hellfire, because of His saying, may He be exalted and glorified, describing Paradise and Hellfire: ﴿How good a place of rest﴾ (Al-Furqan, 76) and ﴿How evil a place of rest﴾ (Al-Furqan, 66). ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 6, verse 99:**

﴿It is He who sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth by it﴾: that is, by the water. ﴿the vegetation of every thing; then We bring forth from it﴾: that is, from the water. It is also said: from the vegetation. ﴿green (khadiran)﴾: meaning, green, like ﴿al-awar﴾ and ﴿al-a'war﴾ (both meaning "one-eyed"). That is, what is moist and green of what grows of wheat, barley, and the like. ﴿We bring forth from it grain piled up (mutarakiban)﴾: that is, piled one upon another, ﴿like the ears of wheat, barley, rice, and all other grains.﴾ ﴿And from the palm trees, from their spathe (talN)﴾: the talʿ is the first thing that emerges from the fruit of the palm tree. ﴿clusters (qinwan)﴾: the plural of qinw, which is the ʿidhq (cluster of dates), like ṣinw and ṣinwan. There is no parallel to these two in the language. ﴿hanging low (dániyah)﴾: that is, its reach is near, so that it can be picked by one standing or sitting. Mujahid said: ﴿hanging (mutadalliyah)﴾. al-Dahhak said: ﴿short, clinging to the ground﴾. In this there is an ellipsis; its meaning is: "And from the palm trees are those whose clusters are low-hanging, and among them are those that are far away." He suffices with mentioning the near ones over the far ones because they come to mind first, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ (An-Naml, 81), meaning "the heat and the cold," and He suffices with mentioning one of them. ﴿And gardens of grapevines﴾: that is, and We brought forth from it gardens. Al-A'mash, from ʿAsim, read ﴿wa-jannatun﴾ with a nominative ending, as a coordinate to His saying ﴿qinwan﴾, but the majority of reciters read it otherwise. ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate﴾: that is, and the olive tree and the pomegranate tree. ﴿Similar and dissimilar (mushtabihan wa-ghayra mutashabih)﴾: Qatadah said: its meaning is that its leaves are similar while its fruit differs, because the leaves of the olive resemble the leaves of the pomegranate. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 100–102:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they made the jinn partners with Allah﴾, meaning: the disbelievers made the jinn partners with Allah. ﴿And He created them﴾, meaning: and it is He who created the jinn.

Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning the zanadiqa (heretics). They affirmed that Iblis shares in the creation, and they said: [Allah is the Creator of] [[In "B": (Allah created)]] the Light, the people, the animals and the cattle, while Iblis is the creator of the darkness, the predatory beasts, the snakes and the scorpions. This is like His saying: "And they have made between Him and the jinn a kinship" (al-Saffat, 158), and Iblis is of the jinn. ﴿And they invented﴾: the people of Madina read "wa kharraqu" with a doubled ra' for intensification, and the others read it with a single ra', meaning they fabricated. ﴿for Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾. This is like the saying of the Jews, "Uzayr is the son of Allah," and the saying of the Christians, "The Messiah is the son of Allah," and the saying of the disbelievers among the Arabs, "The angels are the daughters of Allah." Then He declared Himself free of that, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him and exalted above what they describe﴾.

﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the one who brought them into being without a pattern preceding them. ﴿How can He have a son when He has no companion?﴾, meaning: how could He have a son? ﴿And He has no wife﴾, that is, a spouse. ﴿And He created all things, and He is Knowing of all things.﴾

The Mu'tazilah (Mu'tazilites) hold to the apparent meaning of this verse in denying that Allah, exalted is He, can be seen with the eyes.

The position of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) is affirming the seeing of Allah, exalted is He, with the eyes, which the Qur'an and the Sunnah have brought. [[A portion of a hadith, narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir of Surah (Qaf): 8 / 597, and in al-Tawhid, and in Mawaqit al-Salat. And Muslim in al-Masajid, chapter on the virtue of the Fajr and 'Asr prayers, no. (633): 1 / 439. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2 / 224.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 106–108:

﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord.﴾ That is: the Qur'an; act upon it. ﴿There is no god but Him. And turn away from the polytheists.﴾ That is, do not dispute with them.

﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him.﴾ That is: had He willed, He would have made them believers. ﴿And We did not make you a guardian (ḥafīẓ) over them﴾, meaning a watcher (raqīb). ʿAṭāʾ said: "And We did not make you a guardian over them" means you would protect them from Me; that is, you were not sent to protect the polytheists from punishment; you were only sent as a conveyer of the message (muballigh).
