**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 109:**

His words, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿They swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths﴾ – the verse. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Kalbi said: The Quraysh said, "O Muhammad, you tell us that Musa had a staff with which he struck the rock, and twelve springs gushed forth from it, and you tell us that 'Isa (peace be upon him) used to revive the dead. So bring us some signs so that we may believe you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "What is it that you wish?" They said, "Turn Safa into gold for us, or raise up for us some of our dead so that we may ask them about you, whether what you say is true or false, or show us the angels bearing witness for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "If I do some of what you ask, will you believe me?" They said, "Yes, by Allah, if you do it, we will all follow you." The Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to bring the sign down upon them so that they would believe. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, calling upon Allah to turn Safa into gold. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and said, "Choose what you wish. If you wish, it will become gold, but if they do not believe, I will punish them. And if you wish, I will leave them until one of them repents." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Rather, let one of them repent." Then Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, revealed: ﴿They swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 12/38; al-Wahidi p. 256. See also al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/340.]] That is, they swore by Allah with the utmost of their oaths, meaning the most emphatic and strongest of the oaths they were able to make.

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: When a man swears by Allah, that is the utmost of his oath.

﴿If a sign came to them﴾ as came to the nations before them, ﴿they would surely believe in it.﴾ Say, O Muhammad, ﴿Signs are only with Allah﴾, and Allah is able to send them down, ﴿and what will make you aware﴾, that is, what will make you know?

They differed concerning those addressed by His words ﴿and what will make you aware﴾. Some said: the address is to the polytheists who swore the oaths. Others said: the address is to the believers.

As for His exalted words ﴿that when it comes, they will not believe﴾, Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and Abu Bakr from 'Asim read "innaha" with a kasra on the alif (إِنَّهَا), as a new sentence (ibtida'), and they said: the speech is complete at His words ﴿and what will make you aware﴾. Whoever makes the address to the polytheists says its meaning is: "And what will make you aware, O polytheists, that if it came, you would believe?" Whoever makes the address to the believers says its meaning is: "And what will make you aware, O believers, that if they came, they would believe?" Because the Muslims were asking the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to call upon Allah so that He would show them what they had proposed, so that they would believe, He addressed them with His words ﴿and what will make you aware﴾, then began anew, saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿that when it comes, they will not believe﴾. This refers to a specific people about whom Allah has decreed that they will not believe.

The others read "annaha" with a fatha on the alif (أَنَّهَا), and made the address to the believers. They differed concerning His words ﴿they will not believe (la yu'minun)﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: ﴿la﴾ is superfluous (silah), and the meaning of the verse is: "And what will make you aware, O believers, that when the signs come to the polytheists, they will believe?" Like His words, exalted is He, ﴿And it is forbidden to a town which We have destroyed that they should not return﴾ (al-Anbiya', 95), meaning: that they will return. It was also said: "innaha" here means "la'alla" (perhaps), and so it is in the recitation of Ubayy. The Arabs say: "Go to the market, perhaps (annaka) you will buy something," meaning: la'allaka (perhaps you). 'Adi ibn Zayd said:

*"O reproacher, what will make you know that my death*
*is (perhaps) at an hour in the day or in the forenoon of tomorrow?"* [[See: Jamharat Ash'ar al-'Arab: 2/509, edition of Imam Muhammad ibn Sa'ud Islamic University, Riyadh. Lisan al-'Arab, entry "anna": 13/34.]]

That is, perhaps my death is at that hour. It was also said: there is an ellipsis here, and its implied sense is: "And what will make you aware that when they come [will they believe, or will they not believe?]" Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read "la tu'minun" with a ta' (لَا تُؤْمِنُونَ), as address to the disbelievers, and they took as evidence the recitation of Ubayy: "When they come to you, you will not believe." The others read with a ya' (يُؤْمِنُونَ), as report, and the evidence for it is the recitation of al-A'mash: "that when it comes to them, they will not believe."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 110–111:

﴿And We turn their hearts and their sight away, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. Ibn Abbas said: That is, We come between them and faith. Even if We brought them the signs they asked for, they would not believe in them, just as they did not believe in it the first time, that is, just as they did not believe in the signs before them, such as the splitting of the moon and others. It was also said: "just as they did not believe in it the first time" means the miracles of Musa and of the other prophets, peace be upon them, as in His saying, ﴿Did they not reject what was given to Musa before?﴾ (Al-Qasas, 48). In the verse there is an omission, and its implied meaning is: ﴿so they will not believe, just as they did not believe in it the first time﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas: "The first time" is the abode of this world. That is, if they were returned from the Hereafter to this world, We would turn their hearts and their sight away from faith, just as they did not believe in this world before their death, as He said: ﴿Even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ (Al-An'am, 28). ﴿And We leave them in their rebellion, wandering blindly﴾. Ata said: We forsake them and leave them in their error, to persist in it.

﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels﴾, so that they saw them face to face, ﴿and the dead had spoken to them﴾ through Our bringing them back to life, so that they bore witness to you as a prophet, just as they asked, ﴿and We gathered against them every thing﴾, and assembled it, ﴿qubulan﴾. The people of Madina and Ibn Amir read it as "qibalan" with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba, meaning "face to face" (mu'ayanatan). The others read it with a damma on the qaf and the ba. It is the plural of qabil (guarantor), which means kafil, like raghif and rughuf, and qadib and qudub, meaning: guarantors and sureties. It was also said that it is the plural of qabil, meaning tribe (qabila), that is, in groups, group by group. It was also said that it means "confronting" and "facing," from the saying of the Arabs: "I came to you qubulan, not dubura," when one comes to him from the direction of his face. ﴿They would not have believed unless Allah willed it﴾. ﴿But most of them are ignorant﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 112–113:

﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾: that is, enemies. This is a consolation for the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: just as We have tried you with these people, so too We appointed for every prophet before you enemies. Then He explained them, saying: ﴿devils of mankind and jinn﴾. ʿIkrimah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Suddī and al-Kalbī said: its meaning is the devils of mankind who are with mankind, and the devils of the jinn who are with the jinn; mankind has no devils [of its own]. This is because Iblis divided his army into two groups: he sent one group to mankind and one group to the jinn. Both groups are enemies of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of his allies, and they meet at all times. The devil of mankind says to the devil of the jinn: "I have led my companion astray by such-and-such, so lead your companion astray by the like of it." And the devils of the jinn say the same to the devils of mankind. This is the "inspiring of some of them to others."

Qatādah, Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan said: indeed, among mankind there are devils just as among the jinn there are devils. The shayṭān (devil; the rebellious, defiant one, from every thing) — they said: when the shayṭān is unable to overcome the believer and fails to lead him astray, he goes to a defiant man from mankind, who is a devil of mankind, and incites him against the believer to tempt him. What supports this is what is narrated from Abū Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "Have you sought refuge in Allah from the devils of the jinn and of mankind?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, do mankind have devils?" He said: "Yes, they are worse than the devils of the jinn." [Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in al-Istiʿādhah, chapter on seeking refuge from the evil of the devils of mankind, 8/275, without the words "they are worse than the devils of the jinn"; and Imam Aḥmad in al-Musnad, 1/265.]

Mālik ibn Dīnār said: the devils of mankind are harder on me than the devils of the jinn, because when I seek refuge in Allah, the devil of the jinn departs from me, but the devil of mankind comes to me and drags me openly into sins.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿inspires some of them to others﴾, that is: he casts; ﴿embellished speech﴾, which is speech that is disguised and adorned with falsehood, having no meaning beneath it; ﴿as deception﴾, meaning: these devils adorn the ugly deeds for the children of Adam, deceiving them with deception. Deception (ghurūr) is false speech. ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾, that is: they would not have done what the devil cast of whisperings [into the hearts]; ﴿so leave them and what they fabricate﴾.

﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾: that is, they incline toward it. The ṣaghw (inclination) is the leaning; it is said: "ṣaghw of so-and-so is with you," meaning his inclination. The verb from it is ṣagha yaṣghā, ṣagan, and ṣaghā yaṣghā, and yaṣghū ṣaghwan. The pronoun in "ilayhi" (toward it) refers to "embellished speech." ﴿And that they may be pleased with it, and that they may earn﴾, meaning: that they may acquire, ﴿what they are earning﴾. It is said: "iqtaraf fulān māl" when he acquired wealth. And Allah the Exalted said: (And whoever earns a good deed) (al-Shūrā, 23). Al-Zajjāj said: meaning, that they may commit of sins what they are committing.

[Narrated by al-Nasāʾī in al-Istiʿādhah, chapter on seeking refuge from the evil of the devils of mankind, 8/275, without the words "they are worse than the devils of the jinn"; and Imam Aḥmad in al-Musnad, 1/265.]

Mālik ibn Dīnār said: the devils of mankind are harder on me than the devils of the jinn, because when I seek refuge in Allah, the devil of the jinn departs from me, but the devil of mankind comes to me and drags me openly into sins.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿inspires some of them to others﴾, that is: he casts; ﴿embellished speech﴾, which is speech that is disguised and adorned with falsehood, having no meaning beneath it; ﴿as deception﴾, meaning: these devils adorn the ugly deeds for the children of Adam, deceiving them with deception. Deception (ghurūr) is false speech. ﴿And had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾, that is: they would not have done what the devil cast of whisperings [into the hearts]; ﴿so leave them and what they fabricate﴾.

﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾: that is, they incline toward it. The ṣaghw (inclination) is the leaning; it is said: "ṣaghw of so-and-so is with you," meaning his inclination. The verb from it is ṣagha yaṣghā, ṣagan, and ṣaghā yaṣghā, and yaṣghū ṣaghwan. The pronoun in "ilayhi" (toward it) refers to "embellished speech." ﴿And that they may be pleased with it, and that they may earn﴾, meaning: that they may acquire, ﴿what they are earning﴾. It is said: "iqtaraf fulān māl" when he acquired wealth. And Allah the Exalted said: (And whoever earns a good deed) (al-Shūrā, 23). Al-Zajjāj said: meaning, that they may commit of sins what they are committing.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 114–117:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is it other than Allah that I should seek as a judge?﴾ There is an elision in it, meaning: Say to them, O Muhammad, "Is it other than Allah that I should seek as a judge?" ﴿I should seek﴾ means I should demand ﴿a judge﴾, a qadi (judge) between me and you. This is because they used to say to the Prophet ﷺ: "Make a judge between us and you," and he answered them with this. ﴿And it is He who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed﴾, meaning: with His command and prohibition made clear in it, that is, the Qur'an. It was also said: "fully detailed" means in fives and tens, as He said: ﴿That We may strengthen thereby your heart﴾ (al-Furqan, 32). ﴿And those to whom We gave the Book﴾

That is, the scholars of the Jews and the Christians to whom We gave the Torah and the Gospel. It was also said: they are the believers among the People of the Book. ʿAtaʾ said: they are the leading companions of the Prophet ﷺ. The intended meaning of "the Book" is the Qur'an. ﴿know that it is sent down﴾, that is, the Qur'an. Ibn ʿAmir [and Hafs] read "munazzal" with the doubled letter, from tanzil (gradual sending down), because it was revealed in separate installments. The others read it with the single letter, from inzal (sending down), based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who has sent down to you the Book﴾. ﴿from your Lord in truth, so do not be among the doubters﴾, meaning among those who doubt that they know this.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾. The people of Kufa and Ya'qub read "kalimat" in the singular, while the others read "kalimat" in the plural. By "the words" He means His command, His prohibition, His promise and His threat. ﴿in truth and justice﴾, that is: truthful in the promise and the threat, and just in the command and the prohibition. Qatadah and Muqatil said: truthful in what He promised and just in what He decreed. ﴿None can alter His words﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: none can reject His decree, nor change His judgment, nor break His promise. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. It was said: by "the words" He meant the Qur'an, which none can alter; the distorters cannot add to it or subtract from it.

It was also said: He meant that they disputed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers about eating carrion, and said: "Do you eat what you kill, but do not eat what Allah has killed?" So He said: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth﴾, that is, if you obey them regarding eating carrion, they will mislead you from the way of Allah. ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture﴾. He means that the religion they hold is conjecture [and desire], which they did not take up with insight. ﴿And they do nothing but guess﴾, that is, they lie.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way﴾. It was said: the position of "man" (who) is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, meaning: "about who strays." Al-Zajjaj said: its position is nominative as the subject, and its wording is the wording of a question, and the meaning is: "Indeed, your Lord is most knowing which of the people strays from His way." ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾. He informed that He is most knowing of both groups, the astray and the transgressors, and He will reward each according to what it deserves.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 118–119:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.﴾ That is, eat of what has been slaughtered in the name of Allah.

This is because they used to forbid certain kinds of livestock and make lawful carrion (al-amwat), so it was said to them: "Make lawful what Allah has made lawful, and forbid what Allah has forbidden."

Then He said: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you that you do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned,⦆ meaning: what reason do you have, and what prevents you from eating of the slaughtered animals over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, ﴿while He has already detailed for you what He has forbidden to you﴾. The people of Medina, Ya'qub and Hafs read "faṣṣala" (ﻓَﺼَّﻞَ) and "ḥarrama" (ﺣَﺮَّﻡَ) both with a fatha, meaning: Allah has detailed what He has forbidden to you, in accordance with His saying ﴿the name of Allah﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and Abu 'Amr read both with a damma on the fa' and the ha' and a kasra on the sad and the ra', in the passive form, in accordance with His saying ﴿has been mentioned﴾ (dhukira). Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read "faṣṣala" with a fatha and "ḥurrima" with a damma. By the detailing of the forbidden things he intended what was mentioned in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood⦆ (al-Ma'idah, 3), ﴿except what you are compelled to,⦆ from these things, for it is lawful for you in cases of necessity. ﴿And indeed, many lead [others] astray⦆. The people of Kufa read "yuḍillūna" with a damma on the ya', and likewise His saying "liyuḍillū" in Surah Yunus, in accordance with His saying, may He be exalted: (who would mislead you from the way of Allah). It was also said that by this he intended 'Amr ibn Luhayy and those among the polytheists after him who instituted the baḥa'ir and the sawa'ib. The others read it with a fatha, in accordance with His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows best who strays﴾ and ﴿by their desires without knowledge⦆, when they refused to eat what the name of Allah had been mentioned over and called to eating carrion. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors﴾, those who go beyond the lawful to the unlawful.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 120–121:

﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾ means: all sins, for they cannot be free of these two aspects. Qatadah said: "Its open and its secret." Mujahid said: "The outward of sin is what one commits with the limbs of sins, and its inward is what one intends and purposes in the heart, like one who persists in sin and is determined to commit it."

Al-Kalbi said: "Its outward is adultery and its inward is taking a lover (al-mukhalah)." Most commentators hold that the outward of sin is openly committing adultery, and they are the people of the narrations, and its inward is committing it secretly. That is because the Arabs used to love adultery; the noble among them would take pride in it and do it in secret, while the non-noble did not care and would make it public. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade both. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The outward of sin is marrying those within the prohibited degrees (al-mahram), and its inward is adultery."

Ibn Zayd said: "The outward of sin is being stripped of clothing and going naked in [the circumambulation] [[In "B": (the roads).]], and the inward is adultery." Hibban narrated from al-Kalbi: "The outward of sin is men circling the House naked by day, and its inward is women circling it naked by night." ﴿Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿for what they used to commit﴾ [acquire in this world] [[Omitted from "B".]].

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The verse concerns the prohibition of carrion and what is similar to it, such as the strangled animal and others."

Ata' said: "The verse concerns the prohibition of slaughtered animals which they would slaughter in the name of idols."

The scholars differed concerning the slaughter of a Muslim when he does not mention the name of Allah over it. One group held that it is forbidden, whether he deliberately omitted the basmalah or forgot it. This is the view of Ibn Sirin and al-Sha'bi, and they argued from the apparent meaning of this verse.

Another group held that it is permissible. This is reported from Ibn Abbas and is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Another group held that if he deliberately omits the basmalah it is not lawful, but if he omits it forgetfully it is lawful. Al-Kharaqi, among the companions of Ahmad, related that this is his school, and it is the view of al-Thawri and the companions of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

Whoever permitted it said: "The meaning of the verse is carrion, or what is slaughtered for other than Allah, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and indeed it is sinful (fisq)﴾, and sinfulness (fisq) is in mentioning the name of other than Allah, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater...﴾ up to His saying ﴿or a sinful thing over which other than Allah has been invoked﴾."

Those who permitted it also argued with what 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, saying: I heard Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrating from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, there are people here who have recently left polytheism, who bring us meat, and we do not know whether they mention the name of Allah over it or not?" He said: "Mention the name of Allah yourselves and eat." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Tawhid, Bab al-Su'al bi-asma' Allah ta'ala wa al-isti'adhah biha: 13/379, and in al-Buyu'. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/194.]]

If the basmalah were a condition for permissibility, then doubt about its presence would prevent eating the animal, just as doubt about the slaughter itself would.

The Most High said: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾. He meant: the devils whisper to their allies among the polytheists to dispute with you. This is because the polytheists said: "O Muhammad, tell us about a sheep when it dies, who killed it?" He said: "Allah killed it." They said: "Do you claim that what you and your companions kill is lawful, and what the dog and the falcon kill is lawful, but what Allah kills is unlawful?" So Allah revealed this verse. ﴿And if you obey them﴾ in eating carrion, ﴿indeed you are then polytheists﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "In this is evidence that whoever makes lawful something that Allah has made unlawful, or makes unlawful what Allah has made lawful, is a polytheist."

Ibn Zayd said: "The outward of sin is being stripped of clothing and going naked in [the circumambulation] [[In "B": (the roads).]], and the inward is adultery." The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "The verse concerns the prohibition of carrion and what is similar to it, such as the strangled animal and others."

Ata' said: "The verse concerns the prohibition of slaughtered animals which they would slaughter in the name of idols."

The scholars differed concerning the slaughter of a Muslim when he does not mention the name of Allah over it. One group held that it is forbidden, whether he deliberately omitted the basmalah or forgot it. This is the view of Ibn Sirin and al-Sha'bi, and they argued from the apparent meaning of this verse.

Another group held that it is permissible. This is reported from Ibn Abbas and is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with them all.

Another group held that if he deliberately omits the basmalah it is not lawful, but if he omits it forgetfully it is lawful. Al-Kharaqi, among the companions of Ahmad, related that this is his school, and it is the view of al-Thawri and the companions of opinion (ashab al-ra'y).

Whoever permitted it said: "The meaning of the verse is carrion, or what is slaughtered for other than Allah, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and indeed it is sinful (fisq)﴾, and sinfulness (fisq) is in mentioning the name of other than Allah, as He said at the end of the surah: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater...﴾ up to His saying ﴿or a sinful thing over which other than Allah has been invoked﴾."

Those who permitted it also argued with what 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, saying: I heard Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrating from his father, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: They said: "O Messenger of Allah, there are people here who have recently left polytheism, who bring us meat, and we do not know whether they mention the name of Allah over it or not?" He said: "Mention the name of Allah yourselves and eat." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Tawhid, Bab al-Su'al bi-asma' Allah ta'ala wa al-isti'adhah biha: 13/379, and in al-Buyu'. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/194.]]

If the basmalah were a condition for permissibility, then doubt about its presence would prevent eating the animal, just as doubt about the slaughter itself would.

The Most High said: ﴿And indeed the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾. He meant: the devils whisper to their allies among the polytheists to dispute with you. This is because the polytheists said: "O Muhammad, tell us about a sheep when it dies, who killed it?" He said: "Allah killed it." They said: "Do you claim that what you and your companions kill is lawful, and what the dog and the falcon kill is lawful, but what Allah kills is unlawful?" So Allah revealed this verse. ﴿And if you obey them﴾ in eating carrion, ﴿indeed you are then polytheists﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: "In this is evidence that whoever makes lawful something that Allah has made unlawful, or makes unlawful what Allah has made lawful, is a polytheist."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 122:

His saying, exalted and mighty is He: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life﴾. Nafi' read "mayyitan" and (﴿the flesh of his brother dead﴾, al-Hujurat, 12) and (﴿and a dead land We have revived it﴾, Surat Ya-Sin, 33) with the shadda (emphatic doubling) in all of them, while the others read them with the light form. ﴿And We gave him life﴾, meaning: he was astray and We guided him; he was dead through disbelief and We gave him life through faith. ﴿And made for him a light﴾ by which he is illuminated, ﴿to walk among the people with it﴾ upon the straight path. It was said: the light is Islam, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He brings them out of darknesses into the light﴾ (al-Baqarah, 257). Qatadah said: it is the Book of Allah, a clear proof from Allah with the believer; by it he acts, by it he takes, and to it he returns. ﴿Like one whose likeness is in darknesses﴾: "al-mathal" is a redundant (silah) element, meaning: like one who is in darknesses, ﴿not coming out of them﴾, meaning: out of the darkness of disbelief.

It was said: this verse was revealed concerning two specific men, then they differed about them. Ibn Abbas said: "We made for him a light" refers to Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and "like one whose likeness is in darknesses" refers to Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. That was because Abu Jahl threw filth (farth) at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Hamzah was informed of what Abu Jahl had done while he was returning from his hunting with a bow in his hand, and Hamzah had not yet embraced Islam. So he came in anger and struck Abu Jahl with the bow, while Abu Jahl was pleading before him and saying: "O Abu Ya'la, do you not see what he has brought? He has made our minds foolish, reviled our gods, and opposed our fathers." Hamzah said: "And who is more foolish than you? You worship stones besides Allah. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger." Then Allah revealed this verse. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, pp. 257-258, and the account of Hamzah's conversion in: Ibn Hisham, al-Sirah 1/291-292, and al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak 3/192, though neither mentions that the verse was revealed concerning this.]]

al-Dahhak said: it was revealed concerning Umar ibn al-Khattab and Abu Jahl. [[Tafsir al-Tabari 12/89; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 258; al-Durr al-Manthur 3/352.]]

Ikrimah and al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl. [[Narrated by al-Tabari 22/90, and Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim; see al-Durr al-Manthur 3/352.]]

﴿Thus has the evil of their deeds been made attractive to the disbelievers﴾, [meaning] of disbelief and disobedience. Ibn Abbas said: meaning Satan made the worship of idols attractive to them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 123–124:

His, the Exalted and Majestic, saying: ﴿And thus We have placed in every town its greatest criminals﴾, meaning: just as the wicked ones of Makkah are its great men, so too have We placed the wicked ones of every town [[In (B): "nation".]] as its great men, that is, its dignitaries, the plural of akbar (greatest), like afdal (most excellent) and afadil (excellent ones), and aswad (black) and asawid (black ones). This is the way of Allah, the Exalted, that He placed in every town the followers of the messengers as their weak ones, as He said in the story of Nuh, peace be upon him: ﴿Shall we believe you when the lowest ones follow you?﴾ (al-Shu'ara', 111), and He placed their wicked ones as their great men. ﴿That they may plot therein﴾. That is because they set four men on every road of Makkah to turn people away from belief in Muhammad ﷺ, saying to everyone who arrived: "Beware of this man, for he is a soothsayer, a sorcerer, a liar."

﴿But they plot only against themselves﴾, because the evil consequence of their plotting returns upon them. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾ that this is so.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what the messengers of Allah were given."﴾ That is, the like of what the messengers of Allah were given of prophethood. This is because al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said: "If prophethood were true, I would be more deserving of it than you, for I am older than you in years and greater than you in wealth." So Allah, the Exalted, revealed this verse [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3/353.]].

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Abu Jahl, because he said: "The Banu Abd Manaf have competed with us in nobility until we have become like two racehorses in a race. They say: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes.' By Allah, we will never believe in him or follow him unless revelation comes to us just as it comes to him." So Allah, the Exalted and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And when they come﴾ [[Ibn Ishaq related the story in al-Sirah: 1/315-316, and did not mention that it was the occasion of revelation of the verse.]], a proof of the truthfulness of Muhammad ﷺ. They said, meaning Abu Jahl: ﴿We will not believe until we are given the like of what the messengers of Allah were given﴾, meaning Muhammad ﷺ.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾. Ibn Kathir and Hafs read risalatahu (His message) in the singular, while the others read risalatihi (His messages) in the plural. The meaning: Allah knows best who is most worthy of the prophethood.

﴿Those who committed crimes will be struck with humiliation﴾, meaning disgrace and abasement, ﴿before Allah﴾, that is, from Allah, ﴿and a severe punishment for what they used to plot.﴾ 124 It has been said: humiliation in this world and severe punishment in the Hereafter.

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-An'am (6), verse 125:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾. That is, He opens his heart and illuminates it until he accepts Islam. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked about the expansion of the breast (sharh al-sadr). He said: "It is a light that Allah casts into the heart of the believer, so that it expands and widens." It was said: "Is there a sign (amarah) of that?" [In another version: "a sign (min 'alamah)".] He said: "Yes: turning in repentance (inabah) toward the abode of eternity, withdrawing from the abode of delusion, and preparing for death before death comes."[[Narrated by al-Tabari (12/98-102) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat (1/257-258). Al-Bayhaqi said: "This is munqati' (disconnected)." See also al-Durr al-Manthur (3/354), where it is attributed to Ibn al-Mubarak in al-Zuhd, 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Shaykh Mahmud Shakir weakened it in his notes on al-Tabari. Ibn Kathir strengthened it because of its multiple chains (2/176).]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast narrow﴾. Ibn Kathir read ḍayyiqan (ضَيِّقًا) with a light pronunciation here and in al-Furqan, while the rest read it with the doubled letter (ḍayyiqan, ضَيِّقًا). Both are dialectal variants (lughatan), like hayn and hayyin, and layn and layyin. ﴿Harajan﴾ (حَرَجًا) was read with a kasra on the ra' (ḥariijan) by the people of Madina and Abu Bakr, and with a fatha by the rest. Both are also dialectal variants, like al-dinaf and al-danaf. Sibawayh said: with a fatha, ḥaraj is the verbal noun (masdar), like al-talab, and its meaning is "one who has ḥaraj"; with a kasra it is the noun (ism), and it means the utmost narrowness. The meaning is: He makes his heart narrow so that faith cannot enter it. Al-Kalbi said: "There is no outlet for good in it." Ibn 'Abbas said: "When he hears the remembrance of Allah, his heart recoils (ishma'azza), and when he mentions something of the worship of idols, he feels at ease with it."

'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, recited this verse and asked a Bedouin of Kinanah: "What is al-ḥarijah among you?" He said: "Among us, al-ḥarijah is a tree among trees that no grazing animal, no wild beast, and nothing else can reach." 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Likewise, the heart of the hypocrite: nothing of good reaches it."

﴿As if he were climbing up into the sky﴾. Ibn Kathir read yaṣṣa'idu (يَصْعَدُ) with a light pronunciation. Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Asim, read yaṣṣā'adu (يَصَّاعَدُ) with an alif, meaning yatasa'addu (he climbs). The others read yaṣṣa''adu (يَصَّعَّدُ) with a doubled ṣad and 'ayn, meaning yatasa''adu (he climbs with effort). The meaning: faith is as burdensome for him as climbing to the sky would be. The root meaning of ṣu'ud (climbing) is hardship, and from it is His saying, may He be exalted: (I will overwhelm him with a arduous climb, ṣa'ūdan), meaning a steep, difficult ascent.

﴿Thus Allah places the rijs upon those who do not believe﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: rijs is Satan, meaning he is given power over him. Al-Kalbi said: it is sin (ma'tham). Mujahid said: rijs is whatever has no good in it. 'Ata' said: rijs is punishment, like rijs (itself). It was also said: it is najas (impurity). It is narrated that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the privy (al-khala'), he would say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the rijs and the najas."[[Narrated by Ibn Majah, Kitab al-Taharah, no. 299 (1/109). He said in al-Zawa'id: its isnad is weak. It was also narrated by Ibn al-Sunni in 'Amal al-Yawm wa'l-Laylah, p. 12, through Isma'il ibn Rafi' from Duraid ibn Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar, and by Ibn 'Asakir from Ibn Mas'ud. Al-Mundhiri said: "This hadith is weak." Al-'Iraqi said: "Isma'il is disputed, and Duraid ibn Nafi''s narration from Ibn 'Umar is disconnected." See Fayd al-Qadir by al-Munawi (5/128). What is established in the two Sahihs and the Sunan is that when he ﷺ entered the privy he would say: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the male and female unclean spirits (al-khubth wa'l-khaba'ith)."]] Al-Zajjaj said: rijs is a curse in this world and punishment in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 126–128:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾ [i.e., this which We have explained. And it was said: this which you are upon, O Muhammad, is the path of your Lord and His religion which He has chosen for Himself, straight] [[Addition from "b".]] with no crookedness in it, and it is Islam.

﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who remember﴾

﴿For them is the abode of peace with their Lord﴾, meaning: Paradise. Most of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: As-Salam is Allah, and His abode is Paradise. It was also said: As-Salam is safety, [i.e., for them is the abode of safety] [[Omitted from "b".]] from calamities, and it is Paradise. It was named the abode of peace because everyone who enters it is safe from afflictions and misfortunes.

It was also said: It was named thus because all of its states are accompanied by peace. It is said at the beginning: (Enter it in peace, secure) (Al-Hijr, 46); (And the angels enter upon them from every gate: "Peace be upon you") (Ar-Ra'd, 23); and He said: (They will not hear therein any vain speech or sin, but only the word "Peace, peace") (Al-Waqi'ah, 26); and He said: (Their greeting therein will be "Peace") (Ibrahim, 23); (Peace, a word from a Lord, Most Merciful) (Ya-Sin, 58).

﴿And He is their Guardian for what they used to do﴾. Al-Husayn [[In "b": Al-Hasan.]] ibn al-Fadl said: He takes charge of them in this world by granting success, and in the Hereafter by recompense.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And the Day He will gather them﴾. Hafs recited ﴿yahshuruhum﴾ with the letter ya'. ﴿All together﴾, meaning: the jinn and mankind; He will gather them at the station of the Resurrection, and He will say: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾. The jinn here means the devils. ﴿You have acquired much from mankind﴾, i.e., you have acquired much from mankind through misguidance and seduction, meaning: you have led many astray. ﴿And their allies from mankind will say﴾, meaning: the allies of the devils from mankind who obeyed them. ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: The benefit of mankind from the jinn is that a man, when he traveled and stopped in a barren land and feared for himself from the jinn, would say: "I seek refuge in the lord of this valley from the foolish ones of his people," and he would spend the night under their protection.

As for the benefit of the jinn from mankind: they said, "We have become masters over mankind along with the jinn, since they seek refuge with us," so they would increase in honour among their people and in greatness in their own estimation. This is like His saying, exalted is He: (And there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in burden) (Al-Jinn, 6).

It was also said: The benefit of mankind from the jinn is what they used to receive from them of false reports, sorcery and soothsaying, and their adorning for them of the matters they desire and facilitating the path to them. The benefit of the jinn from mankind is mankind's obedience to them in what they adorn for them of misguidance and sins.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It is the obedience of some of them to others and the agreement of some of them with others.

﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾, meaning: the Resurrection and the Resurrecting. ﴿He said﴾, Allah, exalted is He: ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, your dwelling place, ﴿abiding therein, except what Allah wills﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning this exception, as they differed concerning His saying: (Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills) (Hud, 107).

It was said: He intended, except the duration of the period between their resurrection and their entry into Hell; meaning: they abide in the Fire except for this measure.

It was also said: The exception refers to the punishment, which is His saying ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, meaning: abiding in the Fire, apart from what Allah wills of the various kinds of punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The exception refers to a people for whom Allah's knowledge had preceded that they would embrace Islam and thus leave the Fire, and "ma" in this interpretation means "man" (those who). ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾. It was said: Knowing of the one whom He excepted, and of what is in their hearts of righteousness and piety.

﴿And He is their Guardian for what they used to do﴾. Al-Husayn [[In "b": Al-Hasan.]] ibn al-Fadl said: He takes charge of them in this world by granting success, and in the Hereafter by recompense.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And the Day He will gather them﴾. Hafs recited ﴿yahshuruhum﴾ with the letter ya'. ﴿All together﴾, meaning: the jinn and mankind; He will gather them at the station of the Resurrection, and He will say: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾. The jinn here means the devils. ﴿You have acquired much from mankind﴾, i.e., you have acquired much from mankind through misguidance and seduction, meaning: you have led many astray. ﴿And their allies from mankind will say﴾, meaning: the allies of the devils from mankind who obeyed them. ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another﴾.

Al-Kalbi said: The benefit of mankind from the jinn is that a man, when he traveled and stopped in a barren land and feared for himself from the jinn, would say: "I seek refuge in the lord of this valley from the foolish ones of his people," and he would spend the night under their protection.

As for the benefit of the jinn from mankind: they said, "We have become masters over mankind along with the jinn, since they seek refuge with us," so they would increase in honour among their people and in greatness in their own estimation. This is like His saying, exalted is He: (And there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in burden) (Al-Jinn, 6).

It was also said: The benefit of mankind from the jinn is what they used to receive from them of false reports, sorcery and soothsaying, and their adorning for them of the matters they desire and facilitating the path to them. The benefit of the jinn from mankind is mankind's obedience to them in what they adorn for them of misguidance and sins.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It is the obedience of some of them to others and the agreement of some of them with others.

﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾, meaning: the Resurrection and the Resurrecting. ﴿He said﴾, Allah, exalted is He: ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, your dwelling place, ﴿abiding therein, except what Allah wills﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning this exception, as they differed concerning His saying: (Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills) (Hud, 107).

It was said: He intended, except the duration of the period between their resurrection and their entry into Hell; meaning: they abide in the Fire except for this measure.

It was also said: The exception refers to the punishment, which is His saying ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, meaning: abiding in the Fire, apart from what Allah wills of the various kinds of punishment.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The exception refers to a people for whom Allah's knowledge had preceded that they would embrace Islam and thus leave the Fire, and "ma" in this interpretation means "man" (those who). ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Wise, Knowing﴾. It was said: Knowing of the one whom He excepted, and of what is in their hearts of righteousness and piety.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah al-An'am (6), verses 129–130:

﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn.﴾ [It is said: that is,] [[In MS "B": "(it is said)".]] just as We abandoned the disobedient among the jinn and humankind, until some of them benefited from others. "We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others" means: We give some of them power over others, so We take vengeance on the wrongdoer through another wrongdoer. This is like what has come in the report: "Whoever helps a wrongdoer, Allah will give him power over him." [[Al-Suyuti, in *al-La'ali*, said: "Ṣāḥib al-Firdaws mentioned it with its chain from a ḥadīth of Ibn Mas'ud." In *al-Maqasid al-Hasana*, he said: Ibn 'Asakir narrated it in his *Ta'rikh* from Ibn Mas'ud, traced to the Prophet. Its chain includes Ibn Zakariya al-'Adawi, who is accused of fabricating ḥadīth, and this is its defect. Al-Daylami also cited it in *al-Firdaws* without a chain, from Ibn Mas'ud. See *Kashf al-Khafa'*: 2/297–298; *Fayd al-Qadir*: 6/72; *Tamyiz al-Tayyib min al-Khabith*, p. 177.]]

Qatadah said: "We make some of them allies of others. So the believer is an ally of the believer wherever he is, and the disbeliever is an ally of the disbeliever wherever he is." It is narrated from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "We make them follow one another into the Fire, through allegiance." It is also said: its meaning is that We make the wrongdoers among humankind rulers over the wrongdoers among the jinn, and the wrongdoers among the jinn rulers over the wrongdoers among humankind; that is, We leave some of them to others. This is like the verse ﴿We leave him to what he has chosen for himself﴾ (al-Nisa', 115).

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), concerning its interpretation: when Allah, Exalted, intends good for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their best; and when He intends evil for a people, He places their affairs in the hands of their worst.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind! Did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ They differed over whether a messenger was sent to the jinn from among themselves. Al-Dahhak was asked about it and said: "Yes. Have you not heard Allah say, ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾" He means by this: messengers from humankind and messengers from the jinn. Al-Kalbi said: the messengers before Muhammad (ﷺ) were sent to both the jinn and humankind together.

Mujahid said: "The messengers are from humankind, and the warners are from the jinn." Then he recited ﴿They returned to their people as warners﴾ (al-Ahqaf, 29), and these are a people who heard the words of the messengers and then conveyed to the jinn what they had heard. The jinn have no messengers. According to this view, the saying ﴿messengers from among you﴾ refers to one of the two kinds, namely humankind, as in the verse ﴿From both of them come forth pearls and coral﴾ (al-Rahman, 22). Pearls come out only from the salt water, not the sweet, and He said ﴿and He made the moon in them a light﴾ (Nuh, 16), though it is in one heaven.

﴿They recount to you My signs﴾: that is, they recite to you ﴿My signs﴾, meaning My books, ﴿and warn you of the meeting of this day of yours﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿They will say: "We bear witness against ourselves"﴾, that they had indeed been informed. Muqatil said: this was when their limbs testified against them concerning their polytheism and disbelief. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿The worldly life deceived them﴾, so that they did not believe, ﴿and they bore witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 135–137:

﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"O my people, act according to your standing. Indeed, I am acting"﴾. Abu Bakr, on the authority of ʿAsim, read ﴿makanatikum﴾ in the plural wherever it occurs, meaning: according to your firm positions (tamakkun). ʿAtaʾ said: according to your states in which you are. Al-Zajjaj said: act according to what you are upon. It is said to a man when he is ordered to remain in a certain condition: "Stay in your place, O so-and-so," meaning: remain upon what you are upon. This is a command of threat, in an exaggerated manner, as if he were saying: "Tell them: act according to what you are doing." ﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ in accordance with what my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded me. ﴿So you will come to know who will have the good outcome of the [Final] Abode﴾, that is, Paradise. Hamzah and al-Kisai read ﴿yakunu﴾ with a ya here and in al-Qasas, while the others read it with a ta' because ʿaqibah (outcome) is feminine. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not be successful﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: its meaning is that whoever disbelieves in Me and associates others with Me will not be happy. Al-Dahhak said: he will not triumph.

The statement of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And they assign to Allah a portion of what He has created of the crops and livestock﴾, to the end of the verse. The polytheists would assign to Allah a portion of their crops, livestock, fruits, and all their other wealth, and to the idols a portion. What they assigned to Allah they gave to guests and the needy, and what they assigned to the idols they spent on the idols and their attendants. If something fell from what they had assigned to Allah into the share of the idols, they left it there and said: "Allah is free of need of this." But if something fell from the share of the idols into what they had assigned to Allah, they returned it to the idols and said: "They are in need." And if something from what they had assigned to Allah was lost or diminished, they did not care; but if something from what they had assigned to the idols was lost or diminished, they made it up from what they had assigned to Allah. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they assign to Allah a portion of what He has created [dhara'a, i.e., created]﴾ ﴿of the crops and livestock﴾ a portion. There is an ellipsis in it; its meaning is: they assigned to Allah a portion and to their partners a portion.

﴿So they say, "This is for Allah," by their claim﴾. Al-Kisai read ﴿bi-zu'mihim﴾ with a damma on the zay, while the rest read it with a fatha; both are dialects, and it means saying something without reality. ﴿And this is for our partners﴾, meaning the idols. ﴿But what was for their partners does not reach Allah, while what was for Allah reaches their partners.﴾ Its meaning: they did not complete what they had assigned to Allah for the idols, and they did not complete what they had assigned to the idols for Allah... (as in the original sense: they would complete what they had assigned to the idols from what they had assigned to Allah, but would not complete what they had assigned to Allah from what they had assigned to the idols). Qatadah said: when a year of drought struck them, they used what they had apportioned to Allah, ate from it, and set aside what they had apportioned to their partners, without eating from it anything at all. ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is: wretched is what they do.

﴿And likewise, to many of the polytheists their partners have made attractive the killing of their children﴾. That is, just as the prohibition of the crops and livestock was made attractive to them, so likewise was the killing of their children made attractive to many of the polytheists. Mujahid said: "their partners" means their devils, who adorned and beautified for them the burying of daughters alive out of fear of poverty. The devils were called partners because they obeyed them in disobedience to Allah, and the partners were attributed to them because they took them.

Al-Kalbi said: "their partners" are the custodians of their gods, who used to adorn for the disbelievers the killing of children. So a man among them would swear: "If such-and-such a boy is born to me, I will surely sacrifice one of them," as ʿAbd al-Muttalib swore concerning his son ʿAbd Allah.

Ibn ʿAmir read ﴿zuyyina﴾ with a damma on the zay and a kasra on the ya, ﴿qatlu﴾ in the nominative, ﴿awladahum﴾ in the accusative, and ﴿shurakaʾihim﴾ in the genitive, by way of anteposition, as if he said: "The killing of their partners' children has been made attractive to many of the polytheists," so he separated the verb from its agent by the object, namely the children, as the poet said: "So I thrust him, settled, the thrust of the she-camel by Abu Mazadah..." meaning: the thrust of Abu Mazadah's she-camel. The statement of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿to destroy them﴾, that is, to bring them to ruin, ﴿and to confuse them﴾, that is, to mix up for them, ﴿their religion﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: to introduce doubt into their religion. They were upon the religion of Ismaʿil, but they turned away from it through the Satanic confusion. ﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have done it﴾, that is: had Allah willed, He would have protected them so that they would not have done such prohibition of crops and livestock and killing of children. ﴿So leave them, O Muhammad, and what they fabricate﴾, that is, what they invent of lies, for indeed Allah is watchful over them.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verses 138–139:

﴿And they say﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿"These are cattle and tilth, forbidden (ḥijr)"﴾, that is, prohibited. This refers to what they had set aside for God and for their idols of the tilth and the cattle, as has been mentioned previously. Mujahid said: by "the cattle" he means the baḥīra (a she-camel whose ear was slit and was released), the sā'iba (a beast released free), the waṣīla (a she-camel or sheep that gave twins in succession), and the ḥām (a stallion camel released after it had sired a certain number of offspring). ﴿None may eat of them except whom we will, by their claim﴾, meaning men but not women. ﴿And cattle whose backs have been forbidden﴾, meaning the ḥawāmī (cattle released for idols), which they did not ride. ﴿And cattle over which they do not mention the name of God﴾, that is, they slaughter them in the name of the idols, not in the name of God. Abu Wa'il said: its meaning is that they do not perform the pilgrimage on them, nor ride them for the sake of doing good. Because it was customary to mention the name of God over acts of goodness, he used the mention of God, exalted is He, to express the doing of good.

﴿Fabricating against Him﴾, meaning: they do that and claim that God commanded them to do it, fabricating against Him. ﴿He will repay them for what they used to fabricate﴾.

﴿And they say: "What is in the bellies of these cattle is exclusively for our males, and forbidden to our wives"﴾, that is, our women. Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada and al-Sha'bi said: he meant the fetuses of the baḥā'ir and the sawā'ib. Whatever was born alive from them was exclusively for the men and not the women, and whatever was born dead, men and women both ate of it. The tā' marker was added to "khāliṣa" (exclusively) for emphasis, as in "al-khāṣṣa" and "al-'āmma" (the special and the general), and as in their saying "nassāba" and "'allāma" (very knowledgeable). Al-Farra' said: the tā' was added to agree in feminine gender with "al-an'ām" (the cattle), because what is in their bellies is like them, so it was made feminine to match their feminine form. Al-Kisa'i said: "khāliṣ" and "khāliṣa" are one and the same, like "wa'ẓ" and "mawʿiẓa" (admonition).

﴿And if it is dead (maytatan)﴾. Ibn 'Amir [and Abu Ja'far] [[In "B": (and Abu Ḥafṣ).]] read "takun" with a tā', ﴿maytatun﴾ in the nominative. He marked the verb with the feminine sign because "al-maytatu" is feminine in form. Abu Bakr, from 'Asim, read "takun" with a tā', ﴿maytatan﴾ in the accusative, meaning: and if the fetuses should be dead. Ibn Kathir read ﴿wa-in yakun﴾ with a yā', ﴿maytatun﴾ in the nominative, because the intended sense of "maytatun" is "mayyit" (dead), meaning: and if what is in the bellies should occur dead. The others read ﴿wa-in yakun﴾ with a yā', ﴿maytatan﴾ in the accusative, referring it back to "mā" (what), meaning: and if what is in the bellies should be dead. What indicates this is that He said ﴿they are partners in it﴾ and did not say "in them", and He intended that the men and women are partners in it. ﴿He will repay them for their description﴾, that is, for their attribution (of these rulings), or for their describing the lie against God, exalted is He. ﴿Indeed He is Wise, All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verses 140–141:

﴿Those who have certainly lost are those who killed their children﴾. Ibn 'Amir and Ibn Kathir read "قَتَلُوا" (*qatalu*, "they killed") with a doubled *ta'* for intensification (*al-taksir*, emphasis on the number of killings). The others read it with a single *ta'* (*al-takhfif*).

﴿Foolishly﴾: out of ignorance.

﴿Without knowledge﴾: It was revealed concerning Rabi'ah, Mudar, and some other Arabs as well. They used to bury their daughters alive for fear of captivity and poverty. The Banu Kinanah did not do this [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3 / 366.]].

﴿And they forbade what Allah had provided for them﴾: meaning the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and was released), the *sa'iba* (a animal released freely), the *wasila* (a she-camel or sheep that gave birth to females in succession), and the *ham* (a stallion camel released after siring a set number of offspring). ﴿Inventing a lie against Allah﴾, since they said that Allah had commanded them to do so. ﴿They have certainly gone astray and were not guided.﴾

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who produced﴾, meaning He originated.

﴿Gardens﴾: orchards. ﴿Trellised and untrellised﴾: that is, raised up on supports and not raised up. Ibn 'Abbas said: "*Ma'rushat*" refers to what spreads over the ground and trails, like grapevines, gourds, watermelons and the like. "*Ghayr ma'rushat*" refers to what stands upon a trunk and rises high, like date palms, crops, and all other trees.

Al-Dahhak said: both kinds apply to the grapevine in particular; some of it is trellised and some is not.

﴿And the date palm and the crops﴾: that is, and He produced the date palm and the crops. ﴿Varying in their produce﴾: their fruit and taste, some of them sweet, some sour, some good, and some bad. ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾: similar in appearance, and dissimilar in taste, like two pomegranates whose color is the same but whose taste differs. ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit﴾: this is a command of permission.

﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: The people of Basra, Ibn 'Amir, and 'Asim read "حَصَادِهِ" (*hasadihi*) with a *fatha* on the *ha'*. The others read it with a *kasra*. Their meanings are the same, like *al-sirām* and *al-sarām*, and *al-jazāz* and *al-jizāz* (both forms of the word for cutting/harvesting).

They differed concerning this due. Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, al-Hasan, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: it is the obligatory *zakat* (almsgiving), the tenth or half of the tenth (*'ushr* and *nisf al-'ushr*).

'Ali ibn al-Husayn, 'Ata', Mujahid, Hammad, and al-Hakam said: it is a right in wealth other than *zakat*, which He commanded to be given, because this verse is Meccan, and *zakat* was made obligatory in Medina.

Ibrahim said: it is the *dighth* (a handful of the harvest given to the poor). Al-Rabi' said: it is the gleanings of the ears of grain.

Mujahid said: they used to hang a cluster of dates when harvesting, and whoever passed by would eat from it.

Yazid ibn al-Asamm said: when the people of Medina harvested, they would bring a cluster and hang it at the side of the mosque, and the needy person would come and strike it with his stick so that some of it fell, and he would take it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: this was a right that was commanded to be given at the beginning of Islam, but it became abrogated (*mansukh*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by the obligation of the tithe (*'ushr*).

Miqsam, quoting Ibn 'Abbas, said: *zakat* abrogated every other expenditure mentioned in the Qur'an.

﴿And do not be excessive; indeed, He does not like the excessive﴾. It was said: by excess He meant giving everything away. Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas harvested five hundred date palms and distributed them all in one day, leaving nothing for his family, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3 / 369.]]. Al-Suddi said: "Do not be excessive" means do not give away your wealth so that you end up as paupers. Al-Zajjaj said: according to this, if a person gives away all his wealth and provides nothing for his dependents, he has been excessive, because it has come in a report: "Begin with those you are responsible for" [[A fragment of a hadith of Abu Hurayrah, related by al-Bukhari in *Zakat*, chapter "There is no charity except from surplus wealth": 3 / 294, and by Muslim in *Zakat*, chapter on the best charity being that given by a healthy, miserly person, no. (1034): 2 / 717, and by the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 5 / 178, 179.]]. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: its meaning is "do not withhold charity." So the interpretation of the verse according to this is: do not go beyond the limit in stinginess and withholding, to the point that you withhold the obligatory charity.

Muqatil said: do not associate idols with the tilling and the livestock.

Al-Zuhri said: do not spend in disobedience. Mujahid said: excess is whatever you fall short in regarding the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He also said: if Abu Qubays were gold and a man spent it in obedience to Allah, he would not be excessive; but if he spent a single dirham or a *mudd* in disobedience to Allah, he would be excessive. Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: whatever you exceed the command of Allah with is extravagance and excess. Ibn Wahb narrated from Abu Zayd, who said: the address is to the rulers, meaning: do not take more than your right.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 6, verses 140–141:

﴿Those who have certainly lost are those who killed their children﴾. Ibn 'Amir and Ibn Kathir read "قَتَلُوا" (*qatalu*, "they killed") with a doubled *ta'* for intensification (*al-taksir*, emphasis on the number of killings). The others read it with a single *ta'* (*al-takhfif*).

﴿Foolishly﴾: out of ignorance.

﴿Without knowledge﴾: It was revealed concerning Rabi'ah, Mudar, and some other Arabs as well. They used to bury their daughters alive for fear of captivity and poverty. The Banu Kinanah did not do this [[al-Durr al-Manthur: 3 / 366.]].

﴿And they forbade what Allah had provided for them﴾: meaning the *bahira* (a she-camel whose ear was slit and was released), the *sa'iba* (a animal released freely), the *wasila* (a she-camel or sheep that gave birth to females in succession), and the *ham* (a stallion camel released after siring a set number of offspring). ﴿Inventing a lie against Allah﴾, since they said that Allah had commanded them to do so. ﴿They have certainly gone astray and were not guided.﴾

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And it is He who produced﴾, meaning He originated.

﴿Gardens﴾: orchards. ﴿Trellised and untrellised﴾: that is, raised up on supports and not raised up. Ibn 'Abbas said: "*Ma'rushat*" refers to what spreads over the ground and trails, like grapevines, gourds, watermelons and the like. "*Ghayr ma'rushat*" refers to what stands upon a trunk and rises high, like date palms, crops, and all other trees.

Al-Dahhak said: both kinds apply to the grapevine in particular; some of it is trellised and some is not.

﴿And the date palm and the crops﴾: that is, and He produced the date palm and the crops. ﴿Varying in their produce﴾: their fruit and taste, some of them sweet, some sour, some good, and some bad. ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾: similar in appearance, and dissimilar in taste, like two pomegranates whose color is the same but whose taste differs. ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit﴾: this is a command of permission.

﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest﴾: The people of Basra, Ibn 'Amir, and 'Asim read "حَصَادِهِ" (*hasadihi*) with a *fatha* on the *ha'*. The others read it with a *kasra*. Their meanings are the same, like *al-sirām* and *al-sarām*, and *al-jazāz* and *al-jizāz* (both forms of the word for cutting/harvesting).

They differed concerning this due. Ibn 'Abbas, Tawus, al-Hasan, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: it is the obligatory *zakat* (almsgiving), the tenth or half of the tenth (*'ushr* and *nisf al-'ushr*).

'Ali ibn al-Husayn, 'Ata', Mujahid, Hammad, and al-Hakam said: it is a right in wealth other than *zakat*, which He commanded to be given, because this verse is Meccan, and *zakat* was made obligatory in Medina.

Ibrahim said: it is the *dighth* (a handful of the harvest given to the poor). Al-Rabi' said: it is the gleanings of the ears of grain.

Mujahid said: they used to hang a cluster of dates when harvesting, and whoever passed by would eat from it.

Yazid ibn al-Asamm said: when the people of Medina harvested, they would bring a cluster and hang it at the side of the mosque, and the needy person would come and strike it with his stick so that some of it fell, and he would take it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: this was a right that was commanded to be given at the beginning of Islam, but it became abrogated (*mansukh*, i.e., superseded by a later ruling) by the obligation of the tithe (*'ushr*).

Miqsam, quoting Ibn 'Abbas, said: *zakat* abrogated every other expenditure mentioned in the Qur'an.

﴿And do not be excessive; indeed, He does not like the excessive﴾. It was said: by excess He meant giving everything away. Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of al-Kalbi, said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas harvested five hundred date palms and distributed them all in one day, leaving nothing for his family, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 3 / 369.]]. Al-Suddi said: "Do not be excessive" means do not give away your wealth so that you end up as paupers. Al-Zajjaj said: according to this, if a person gives away all his wealth and provides nothing for his dependents, he has been excessive, because it has come in a report: "Begin with those you are responsible for" [[A fragment of a hadith of Abu Hurayrah, related by al-Bukhari in *Zakat*, chapter "There is no charity except from surplus wealth": 3 / 294, and by Muslim in *Zakat*, chapter on the best charity being that given by a healthy, miserly person, no. (1034): 2 / 717, and by the author in *Sharh al-Sunnah*: 5 / 178, 179.]]. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib said: its meaning is "do not withhold charity." So the interpretation of the verse according to this is: do not go beyond the limit in stinginess and withholding, to the point that you withhold the obligatory charity.

Muqatil said: do not associate idols with the tilling and the livestock.

Al-Zuhri said: do not spend in disobedience. Mujahid said: excess is whatever you fall short in regarding the right of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He also said: if Abu Qubays were gold and a man spent it in obedience to Allah, he would not be excessive; but if he spent a single dirham or a *mudd* in disobedience to Allah, he would be excessive. Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: whatever you exceed the command of Allah with is extravagance and excess. Ibn Wahb narrated from Abu Zayd, who said: the address is to the rulers, meaning: do not take more than your right.

The Exalted said: ﴿And of the cattle﴾, that is, and He produced from the cattle, ﴿burden-bearing [animals]﴾, which are every one of the camels that are ridden for carrying loads, ﴿and [animals] for flat-lying [for slaughter]﴾, which are the young camels that do not carry loads.

﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow in the footsteps of Satan﴾, do not tread his path and his traces in forbidding the tilth and the cattle, ﴿for indeed he is to you a manifest enemy﴾.

Then He explained the burden-bearing and the flat-lying [animals], saying: ﴿eight mates﴾. It is in the accusative as a substitution (badal) for "burden-bearing" and "flat-lying", meaning: and He produced from the cattle eight kinds in pairs. ﴿Of sheep, two﴾, that is, the male and the female; [the male is one mate and the female is one mate]. The Arabs call the one a "zawj" (mate) when it cannot be separated from the other. The ḍa'n (sheep) are the ewes, which are the woolly ones of the flock; the singular is ḍa'in, the female is ḍa'inah, and the plural is ḍawa'in. ﴿And of goats, two﴾. Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Amir and the people of Basra read "min al-ma'az" with a fatḥah on the ʿayn, while the rest read it with a sukūn on it. Al-ma'z and al-ma'za are a collective noun with no singular from its own form; they are the hairy ones of the flock. The plural of al-ma'iz is ma'ir, and the plural of al-ma'izah is mawa'iz. ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"Is it the two males that He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?"﴾, meaning the male of the sheep and the goat, the female of the sheep and the goat, and what the wombs of the two females contain of them, for they contain only a male or a female. ﴿Inform me﴾, tell me ﴿with knowledge﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: explain what you have forbidden with knowledge. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ that Allah the Exalted has forbidden that.

The Exalted said: ﴿And of the cattle﴾, that is, and He produced from the cattle, ﴿burden-bearing [animals]﴾, which are every one of the camels that are ridden for carrying loads, ﴿and [animals] for flat-lying [for slaughter]﴾, which are the young camels that do not carry loads.

﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow in the footsteps of Satan﴾, do not tread his path and his traces in forbidding the tilth and the cattle, ﴿for indeed he is to you a manifest enemy﴾.

Al-Zajjaj said: explain what you have forbidden with knowledge. ﴿If you are truthful﴾ that Allah the Exalted has forbidden that.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 144–145:**

﴿And of camels two, and of cattle two. Say: "Has He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain?"﴾ And that is because they used to say: "These are cattle and tilth, forbidden (ḥijr)," and they said: "What is in the bellies of these cattle is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives." And they forbade the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, the waṣīlah and the ḥām, and some of them they forbade to men and women, and some they forbade to women but not to men. So when Islam came and the rulings were established, they argued with the Prophet ﷺ. Their spokesman was Mālik ibn ʿAwf Abū al-Aḥwaṣ al-Jushamī, who said: "O Muhammad, it has reached us [[omitted in manuscript "a"]] that you forbid things which our fathers used to do." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "You have forbidden categories of livestock without any basis. Allah created these eight mates only for eating and for benefit from them. So from where has this prohibition come? Is it from the male or from the female?" Mālik ibn ʿAwf fell silent and was bewildered, and did not speak. For if he had said the prohibition came because of the males, it would necessarily follow that he forbid all males; and if he said because of the females, it would necessarily follow that he forbid all females; and if it was because the womb contains it, then he should forbid all of them, because the womb contains only a male or a female. As for restricting the prohibition to the fifth offspring, or the seventh, or some and not others, from where does that come?

It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to Mālik: "O Mālik, why do you not speak?" Mālik said to him: "Rather, you speak, and I will listen to you."

﴿Or were you witnesses﴾ present ﴿when Allah enjoined this upon you? Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah, to mislead people without knowledge?﴾ It is said: he meant ʿAmr ibn Luḥayy and whoever came after him in his way. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

Then He explained that prohibition and permission come by revelation and descent, so He said: ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden"﴾. It is reported that they said: "Then what is forbidden?" So it was revealed: ﴿Say﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿"I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden"﴾, i.e., anything prohibited ﴿to an eater who eats it﴾, ﴿unless it be carrion﴾. Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Jaʿfar read "takūna" with a ta', ﴿carrion﴾ in the nominative, meaning: unless carrion occurs. Ibn Kathīr and Ḥamzah read "takūna" with a ta', ﴿maytatan﴾ in the accusative, on the assumption of a feminine noun, i.e., unless the soul, or the carcass, is a dead thing. The rest read "yakūna" with a yā', "maytatan" in the accusative, meaning: unless the food is carrion. ﴿Or blood poured forth﴾, i.e., spilled and flowing. Ibn ʿAbbās said: it means what comes out of the living animal while they are alive, and what comes out of the veins (arwāḥ) and what flows from the ducts (adwāj) at slaughter. It does not include the liver and spleen, because they are solid, and the Law has permitted them. Nor does it include blood mixed into the meat, because it is not flowing.

ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr said: I asked Abū Mijlaz about the blood mixed into meat, and about a cooking pot in which the redness of blood is seen? He said: There is no harm in it; He only forbade flowing blood.

Ibrāhīm said: There is no harm in blood in a vein or in marrow, except flowing blood that one intentionally does. ʿIkrimah said: Were it not for this verse, the Muslims would have followed the veins as the Jews follow them.

﴿Or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is an abomination﴾, i.e., forbidden, ﴿or a sinful thing over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked﴾, which is what was slaughtered for other than the name of Allah the Exalted. Some scholars held that the prohibition is restricted to these things. This is narrated from ʿĀ'ishah and Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: The strangled animal (al-munkhaniqah), the beaten animal (al-mawqūdhah), and what is mentioned at the beginning of Surah al-Mā'idah enter under carrion. [[See what has preceded, the explanation of the verse from Surah al-Mā'idah in this part, p. (10–12). See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 7/116 ff., Aḥkām al-Qur'ān of al-Ṭabarī, edited by al-Harras: 3/346–347.]]

Most scholars hold that the prohibition is not restricted to these things, and that what is forbidden by the explicit text of the Book is what is mentioned here. (3)

This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say: "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden"﴾, and the Sunnah has forbidden other things which must be affirmed.

Among them: what Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAbd al-Qāhir informed us: ʿAbd al-Ghāfir ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Juludī narrated to us: Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn Sufyān narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muʿādh al-ʿAnbarī narrated to us: my father informed us: Shuʿbah informed us, from al-Ḥakam, from Maymūn ibn Mihrān, from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade every animal with fangs among the predators, and every bird with talons." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Hunting and Slaughtered Animals, chapter on the prohibition of eating every animal with fangs among predators… no. (1934): 3/1534. And the author in Sharḥ al-Sunnah: 11/234.]]

Abū al-Ḥasan al-Sarakhsī informed us: Zāhir ibn Aḥmad narrated to us: Abū Isḥāq al-Hāshimī narrated to us: Abū Muṣʿab narrated to us, from Mālik, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ḥakīm, from ʿUbaydah ibn Sufyān al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Eating every animal with fangs among predators is forbidden." [[Narrated by Muslim in the same place, no. (1933): 3/1534. And the author in the same place.]]

According to al-Shāfiʿī, the principle is: whatever has no explicit text of prohibition or permission, if it is among what the Law has ordered to be killed—as he said: "Five vermin-like creatures are to be killed in the sanctuary and outside it" [[Narrated by al-Bukhārī in the Chapter on Hunting Penalties, on what the muḥrim may kill of animals: 4/34, and Muslim in the Book of Ḥajj, chapter on what is recommended for the muḥrim and others to kill, no. (1198): 2/856.]]—or which he forbade to be killed, as it is narrated that he forbade killing the bee and the ant—then it is forbidden. As for everything else, the reference is to the prevailing custom of the Arabs: what the majority of them eat is lawful, and what the majority of them do not eat is forbidden, because Allah the Exalted addressed them saying: (Say: "Lawful for you are the good things"). So it is established that what they found good is lawful.

﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He permitted eating these prohibited things in cases of necessity, provided it is not transgression.
