Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 146:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾, meaning the Jews. "Every animal with claws" is that which does not have split hooves, among the beasts and birds, such as the camel, the ostrich, the goose and the duck. Al-Qutaybi said: it is every bird with talons (mikhlab) and every solid-hoofed animal (dhu hafir) among the beasts [[In "a": (predatory beasts).]], and he related this from some of the exegetes, and said: the hoof was called a claw (zufr) by way of metaphor (isti'arah).

﴿And of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat﴾, meaning the fat of the inner parts, which is the thurb (the omentum) and the fat of the two kidneys. ﴿Except what their backs carry﴾, that is, except what clings to the back and the flank from the inside of their bellies. ﴿Or the entrails﴾, which are the intestines (maba'ir), singular: hawiyah and hawiyyah, that is, the fat which the entrails carry. ﴿Or what is mixed with bone﴾, meaning the fat of the tail (alyah). All of this falls within the exception, and the prohibition is specific to the thurb [[Thurb: on the pattern of (fals): a thin fat covering the stomach and intestines.]] and the fat of the kidney.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us: Qutaybah narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say in the year of the Conquest while he was in Makkah: "Indeed Allah and His Messenger have forbidden the sale of wine, carrion, swine and idols." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the fat of carrion, for it is used to coat ships, to grease hides, and people use it for lamps?" He said: "No, it is forbidden." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said at that time: "May Allah fight the Jews! When Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade their fat, they melted it, then sold it and ate its price." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Buyu', chapter on the sale of carrion and idols: 4/424, and Muslim in Musaqah, chapter on the prohibition of selling wine, carrion, swine and idols, no. (1581): 3/207. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 8/30.]]

﴿That We repaid them﴾, that is, that prohibition was a punishment for them ﴿for their transgression﴾, that is, for their wrongdoing: their killing of the prophets, their turning people away from the way of Allah, their taking of usury, and their lawful taking of people's wealth by falsehood. ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾ in reporting what We forbade them and their transgression.

﴿If they deny you, say: "Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy,"﴾ by delaying the punishment from you. ﴿But His punishment will not be averted from the guilty people﴾ when its time comes.

﴿Those who associated partners [with God] will say﴾ when the proof has been established against them and they have become certain of the falsehood of their association of partners with God and of their prohibition of what God did not prohibit: [They said]: ﴿"Had God willed, we would not have associated partners [with Him], nor would our fathers, ﴾ before us, ﴿nor would we have prohibited anything﴾ such as the baheera (a she-camel whose ear was slit), the saiba (a freed camel), and others. They wanted to make His words, ﴿"Had God willed, we would not have associated partners,"﴾ a proof for themselves to justify persisting in polytheism. They said that God, exalted is He, is able to prevent us from what we are doing so that we would not do it. Therefore, had He not been pleased with what we are upon, and willed it from us, and commanded us to it, He would have prevented us from that. So God, exalted is He, said, rejecting them: ﴿Thus did those before them deny [their messengers],﴾ from the disbelieving nations of the past, ﴿until they tasted Our might,﴾ that is, Our punishment.

The people of qadar (the Qadariyya, who deny God's predetermination of human acts) use this verse as evidence. They say: when they said, "Had God willed, we would not have associated partners," God rejected them and refuted them, saying, "Thus did those before them deny."

We reply: the denial does not lie in their saying "Had God willed, we would not have associated partners," for that statement is true. Rather, the denial lies in their saying that God, exalted is He, commanded us to it and was pleased with what we are upon. As He related about them in Surat al-A'raf (verse 28): ﴿And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to it."﴾ So the refutation of them in this is as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: "Indeed, God does not command immorality."﴾

The evidence that the denial was directed at what we have stated, and not at their saying "Had God willed, we would not have associated partners," is His words: ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾ with tashdid [i.e., the form kadhdhaba, with doubled dal, meaning "denied", rather than kadhaba, meaning "lied"] [126a]. Had this been a report from God, mighty and majestic, about their lying in their saying, ﴿"Had God willed, we would not have associated partners,"﴾ He would have said kadhaba (without tashdid), "those before them lied," and so would have attributed to them lying, not denial. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: If they had mentioned this statement in glorification and reverence of God, mighty and majestic, and out of knowledge of Him, He would not have censured them for it, because God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And had God willed, they would not have associated partners,﴾ and He said: ﴿And they would not have believed unless God willed﴾ (Al-An'am, 111). And the believers say this. But they said it as denial, as fabrication and as disputation, without knowledge of God and of what they were saying. A parallel to this is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿And they say, "Had the Most Merciful willed, we would not have worshipped them,"﴾ (Az-Zukhruf, 20). God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾ (Al-An'am, 116)

It has also been said regarding the meaning of the verse: they were speaking the truth with this statement, except that they regarded it as an excuse for themselves and made it a proof for themselves for abandoning faith. He rejected them in this, because God's command is separate from His will and volition. He wills all existing things, but He does not command all that He wills. The servant must follow His command, and he has no right to cling to His will, for His will is never an excuse for anyone.

﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge?"﴾ that is, a book or proof from God, ﴿so that you may bring it out for us?﴾ until what you claim against God, exalted is He, of associating partners or prohibiting what you have prohibited becomes manifest. ﴿You follow only conjecture﴾ that you follow in what you are upon, ﴿without knowledge or certainty.﴾ ﴿And you are only guessing﴾ that is, lying.

﴿If they deny you, say: "Your Lord is possessed of vast mercy,"﴾ by delaying the punishment from you. ﴿But His punishment will not be averted from the guilty people﴾ when its time comes.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 149–151:

﴿Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof. So had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ The conclusive proof (al-hujjah al-baligha) is the complete proof over His creation, through the Book [and the Messenger] [[In "A": (and the messengers).]] and the clear explanation. ﴿So had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾: this indicates that He did not will the faith of the disbelievers, and had He willed, He would have guided them.

﴿Say: "Bring forth (halumma)"﴾: it is said to one, two, or many. ﴿your witnesses who testify﴾, i.e., bring your witnesses who will testify ﴿that God has forbidden this﴾. This refers back to what preceded concerning their forbidding things upon themselves and their claim that God had commanded them to do so. ﴿If they testify﴾ falsely, ﴿then do not testify﴾ yourself ﴿with them. And do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs, and of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who ascribe equals to their Lord﴾, i.e., who associate partners (with Him).

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him"﴾. This is because they asked and said: "What is it that God Most High has forbidden?" So He, Exalted and Majestic, said: "Say: 'Come, I will recite'", i.e., I will read what your Lord has forbidden you, as a truth, a certainty, not a supposition nor a lie as you claim.

If it is said: What is the meaning of His saying "your Lord has forbidden you that you associate nothing with Him," when what is forbidden is association, not the abandonment of association?

It is said: The position of "an" (that) is in the nominative, meaning: "that you not associate." It is also said: its position is in the accusative, and they differ over the way it is in that state. It is said: its meaning is "He has forbidden you to associate with Him," and "la" is an extra particle, like His Most High saying: (What prevented you from not prostrating?) (al-A'raf, 12), i.e., what prevented you from prostrating. It is also said: the speech is complete at His saying "your Lord has forbidden," then He said: "upon you that you associate nothing with Him" as an exhortation (al-igra'). Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible that this be understood according to its meaning, i.e., "I recite to you the prohibition of association," and it is permissible that it means: "I enjoin upon you that you associate nothing with Him."

﴿And be good to parents, and do not kill your children out of poverty﴾, i.e., poverty, ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾, i.e., do not bury your daughters for fear of destitution, for I am the one who provides for you and for them. ﴿And do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is hidden﴾ [what is apparent means the open, and what is hidden] [[Omitted from "B".]] means the secret.

The people of the Jahiliyyah used to find fornication in the open repugnant, and saw no harm in it in secret, so God Most High forbade fornication both in the open and in secret.

Al-Dahhak said: what is apparent is wine, and what is hidden is fornication.

﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾: God Most High forbade the killing of the believer and the covenanted person except by right, that is, except by what permits his killing, such as apostasy, retaliation (qisas), or adultery that requires stoning.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Hiri narrated to us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Hammad narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Abd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The blood of a Muslim man who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah may not be shed except in one of three cases: the married adulterer, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Diyat, chapter on God's saying "that the life is for the life..", 12/201, and Muslim in Qasamah, chapter on the explanation of what permits the blood of a Muslim (1676): 3/1302, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/147.]]

﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾, i.e., commanded you with, ﴿that you may understand﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 152:

﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan, except in the way that is best﴾. That is: with that which brings about its betterment and its growth. Mujahid said: it means trading with it. Al-Dahhak said: it means that one seeks to invest it for him and does not take any of its profit. ﴿Until he reaches his maturity (ashudd)﴾. Al-Sha'bi and Malik said: al-ashudd is the age of puberty (al-hulm), until good deeds are recorded for him and bad deeds are recorded against him. Abu al-Aliyah said: until he understands and his strength is gathered. Al-Kalbi said: al-ashudd is from eighteen years to thirty years. It was also said: to forty years. It was also said: to sixty years. Al-Dahhak said: twenty years. Al-Suddi said: thirty years. Mujahid said: al-ashudd is thirty-three years.

Al-Ashudd is the plural of shadd, like qadd and aqudd, and it means the consolidation of the strength of his youth and age. From it comes "shadd al-nahar," which is its rising (the height of the day). It was also said that reaching al-ashudd is that his sound judgment (rushd) is perceived after puberty.

The meaning of the verse is: "And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best, forever, until he reaches his maturity. Then give him his property if he is of sound judgment (rashid)."

﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾, that is, with fairness, ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, that is, its ability in giving full measure and weight. That is: He did not burden the giver with more than what was obligatory upon him, nor did He burden the rightful owner to be satisfied with less than his right, so that his soul would not be constrained by it. Rather, He commanded each of them with what is within his capacity, which involves no hardship for him.

﴿And when you speak, be just﴾, that is, be truthful in judgment and testimony, ﴿even if it concerns a near relative﴾, that is, even if the one judged or testified against is a relative. ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember﴾, that is, that you may be admonished. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited "tadhakkarun" with a light (khafifah) dhal throughout the Qur'an, while the others recited it with a doubled (mushaddadah) dhal.

Ibn Abbas said: these verses are muhkamat (clear, firm rulings) in all the scriptures; nothing has abrogated them (naskh), and they are forbidden to all of the children of Adam. They are the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab). Whoever acts upon them enters Paradise, and whoever abandons them enters the Fire.

**"And that this is My path, straight, so follow it."** That is: this which I have enjoined upon you in these two verses is **"My path"** (ṣirāṭī), meaning My way and My religion, **"straight"** (mustaqīman), meaning level and upright, **"so follow it"** (fa-ittabi'ūhu).

Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read **"wa-inna"** (and indeed) with a kasrah on the alif (wa-inna), as a fresh sentence (isti'nāf, a resumed statement that begins a new clause). The others read it with a fatḥah on the alif (wa-anna). Al-Farrā' said: the meaning is, "I recite to you that this is My path, straight." Ibn 'Āmir and Ya'qūb read it with a sukūn on the nūn (wa-annā, with the nūn silent).

**"And do not follow the ways"** (al-subul), that is, the various roads other than this road, such as Judaism, Christianity and all the other creeds. It is also said: they are the desires and innovations (bid'ah). **"Lest they scatter you"** (fa-tafarraqa), that is, lead you astray (fa-tamīla), **"away from His way"** (bikum), and scatter you (wa-tashattata), **"from His path"** (ʿan sabīlih), that is, from His way and His religion which He has approved and with which He has enjoined. **"That is what He has enjoined upon you"** (dhālikum waṣṣākum bih), namely what I have mentioned, **"so that you may be righteous"** (la'allakum tattaqūn).

Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ṣamad al-Tarābī, known as Abū Bakr ibn Abī al-Haytham, informed us: al-Ḥākim Abū al-Faḍl Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥaddādī related to us: Abū Yazīd Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Khālid related to us: Abū Yaʿqūb Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm al-Ḥanẓalī related to us: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī related to us, from Ḥammād ibn Zayd, from ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, from Abū Wā'il, from ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) drew a line for us, then said: "This is the path of God." Then he drew lines to his right and to his left, and said: "These are paths; upon each path is a devil calling to it." Then he recited: **"And that this is My path, straight, so follow it"** to the end of the verse.

Al-Haythamī said in al-Majma' (7/22): "Narrated by Aḥmad and al-Bazzār; in its chain is ʿĀṣim ibn Bahdalah, who is trustworthy (thiqah) but has some weakness." The author also narrated it in Sharḥ al-Sunnah: 1/196–197. See also Tafsīr Ibn Kathīr: 2/191.]]

**His saying, Mighty and Majestic:** **"Then We gave Moses the Book"** (thumma ātaynā Mūsā al-kitāb). If it is asked: why did He say "then We gave" when the particle "thumma" (then) indicates sequence, while the giving of the Book to Moses happened before the coming of the Qur'an? It is answered: the meaning is, "Then I inform you that We gave Moses the Book," so "thumma" enters to delay the report, not to delay the revelation.

**"As completion upon him who did good"** (tamāman ʿalā alladhī aḥsan). Scholars differed on this. It is said: a completion upon those among his people who did good, so that "alladhī" means "man" (whoever), that is, upon whoever among his people did good, for among them there were both good-doers and wrongdoers. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "ʿalā alladhīna aḥsanū" (upon those who did good). Abū ʿUbaydah said: the meaning is "upon everyone who did good," that is, We completed Moses' excellence through the Book upon the good-doers, meaning: We made his merit manifest over them. The good-doers are the prophets and the believers. It is also said: "alladhī aḥsan" refers to Moses, and "alladhī" means "mā" (what), that is, "upon what Moses did well." Its sense is: We gave him the Book, namely the Torah, as a completion of the favour upon him, because of his good conduct in obedience and worship, his conveying of the message and his performance of the command.

It is also said: "iḥsān" here means "ʿilm" (knowledge), and "aḥsana" means "ʿalima" (knew). The meaning is: as a completion upon what Moses knew of knowledge and wisdom; that is, We gave him the Book in addition to that.

It is also said: the meaning is "as a completion from Me in return for My good to Moses."

**"And as a detailed explanation"** (wa-tafṣīlan), a clarification **"of everything"** (li-kulli shay'), that is needed **"of the laws of the religion"**; **"and as guidance and mercy"** (wa-hudan wa-raḥmah). This is a description of the Torah. **"So that they might believe in the meeting with their Lord"** (la'allahum bi-liqā'i rabbihim yu'minūn). Ibn ʿAbbās said: so that they would believe in the Resurrection and affirm the reward and the punishment.

**"And that this is My path, straight, so follow it."** That is: this which I have enjoined upon you in these two verses is **"My path"** (ṣirāṭī), meaning My way and My religion, **"straight"** (mustaqīman), meaning level and upright, **"so follow it"** (fa-ittabi'ūhu).

Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read **"wa-inna"** (and indeed) with a kasrah on the alif (wa-inna), as a fresh sentence (isti'nāf, a resumed statement that begins a new clause). The others read it with a fatḥah on the alif (wa-anna). Al-Farrā' said: the meaning is, "I recite to you that this is My path, straight." Ibn 'Āmir and Ya'qūb read it with a sukūn on the nūn (wa-annā, with the nūn silent).

**"And do not follow the ways"** (al-subul), that is, the various roads other than this road, such as Judaism, Christianity and all the other creeds. It is also said: they are the desires and innovations (bid'ah). **"Lest they scatter you"** (fa-tafarraqa), that is, lead you astray (fa-tamīla), **"away from His way"** (bikum), and scatter you (wa-tashattata), **"from His path"** (ʿan sabīlih), that is, from His way and His religion which He has approved and with which He has enjoined. **"That is what He has enjoined upon you"** (dhālikum waṣṣākum bih), namely what I have mentioned, **"so that you may be righteous"** (la'allakum tattaqūn).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 155–157:

﴿And this﴾ means the Qur'an, ﴿is a Book We have sent down, blessed, so follow it﴾, and act upon what is in it, ﴿and be mindful of God﴾, and obey Him, ﴿so that you may receive mercy﴾.

﴿Lest you say﴾ means: lest you should say, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (An-Nisa, 176), meaning: lest you go astray. It was also said: its meaning is, We sent it down out of aversion to ﴿your saying﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: its meaning is, beware lest you say, O people of Makkah, ﴿The Book was only sent down to two groups before us﴾, meaning the Jews and the Christians, ﴿and we were indeed﴾, and we were, ﴿unaware of their study﴾, their recitation, ﴿heedless﴾, not knowing what it contained. Its meaning is: We sent down the Qur'an to you lest you say that the Book was sent down to those before us in their tongue and language, so we did not understand what was in it and were heedless of studying it, and so you would make this an excuse for yourselves.

﴿Or lest you say: If the Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than them﴾. A group of the disbelievers did say this: if what was sent down to the Jews and Christians had been sent down to us, we would have been better than them. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a clear proof from your Lord﴾, a manifest argument in a language you understand, ﴿and guidance﴾, an explanation, ﴿and mercy﴾, and a blessing for whoever follows it. ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of God and turns away﴾ from them? ﴿We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment﴾, meaning severe punishment, ﴿for what they used to turn away﴾ [they used to turn away] [[Omitted from manuscript B.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 158:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do they await﴾, i.e., do they await, after their denial of the Messengers and their rejection of the Qur'an, ﴿except that the angels should come to them﴾ to seize their souls? It is also said: with the punishment. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "yaʾtiyahum" (with the ya', "they come to them") here and in al-Nahl, while the rest read it with the ta' (ta'tiyahum). ﴿Or that your Lord should come﴾, without modality (bila kayf), to decide the judgment among His creation on the Day of Standing (mawqif al-qiyamah). ﴿Or that some of the signs of your Lord should come﴾, meaning the rising of the sun from its west. This is what most of the exegetes hold, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri related it as a marfu' report [[Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the saying of Allah, exalted is He: "Or that some of the signs of your Lord should come," that he said: "The rising of the sun from its west." Al-Tirmidhi said: this is a gharib hadith; some of them narrated it without raising it to the Prophet. See: al-Sunan, Tafsir Surat al-An'am: 8/448-449. It is supported by what he also narrated from Abu Hurairah, which is the hadith that follows it.]].

﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith﴾, i.e., faith will not benefit them at the appearance of the sign that compels them to belief. ﴿Or earned good through its faith﴾ means: the faith of a disbeliever is not accepted, nor is the repentance of a sinner. ﴿Say: Wait﴾, O people of Makkah, ﴿indeed we are waiting﴾ for the punishment to befall you.

Abu 'Ali Hassan ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi related to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan related to us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami related to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us: Ma'mar related to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih: Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, related to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its west. When it rises and people see it, they will all believe, and that is the time when no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith" [[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir Surat al-An'am, chapter on the saying of Allah, "Bring forward your witnesses": 8/297, and Muslim in Iman, chapter on explaining the time when Allah does not accept faith, no. 157: 1/137.]].

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us: Muhammad ibn Hammad related to us: Abu Mu'awiyah al-A'mash related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Ubaydah, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two hands of Allah are outstretched for the one who does evil by night, that he may repent by day, and for the one who does evil by day, that he may repent by night, until the sun rises from its west" [[Related by Muslim in al-Tawbah, chapter on accepting repentance from sins, no. (2759): 4/2113, with the wording: "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, extends His hand by night that one may repent..." And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/82.]].

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Mansur Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sam'an related to us: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us: Hisham related to us, from Ibn Sirin, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever repents before the sun rises from its west, Allah will accept his repentance" [[Related by Muslim in al-Dhikr wa'l-Du'a, chapter on the recommendation of seeking forgiveness, no. (2703): 4/2076, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/83.]].

'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah informed us: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us: 'Asim ibn Abi al-Najud related to us, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh who said: I came to Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, and he mentioned from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Indeed Allah, mighty and majestic, has placed in the West a door whose width is seventy years' travel, for repentance, which is not closed until the sun rises from its direction." That is the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before﴾ [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter on what has come concerning the virtue of repentance and seeking forgiveness: 9/517-519, at length, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. Also related by Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, chapter on the rising of the sun from the west, no. (4070): 2/1353; al-Tayalisi in al-Musnad, pp. (160-161); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/89.]].

Abu Hazim related from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three things, when they come forth, no soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith: the Dajjal, the Beast, and the rising of the sun from its west." [[Related by Muslim in Iman, chapter on explaining the time when Allah does not accept faith, no. (158): 1/138.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verse 159:

His saying, exalted and mighty is He: ﴿Indeed, those who have divided their religion﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "fara'qu" (they parted from) with an alif here and in Surat al-Rum, meaning: they went out of their religion and abandoned it. The others read "farraqu" with a shaddah, meaning: they made the religion of God, which is one, the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, the ḥanifiyyah, into various different religions. So one people became Jews and another people became Christians. What indicates this is His saying, exalted and mighty is He: ﴿and have become sects﴾, meaning: they became divided into different groups. They are the Jews and the Christians, according to Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

It has also been said: they are the people of innovations (bid'ah) and doubtful matters (shubuhat) from this community. It was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Aisha: "O Aisha, indeed those who have parted from their religion and have become sects, they are the people of innovations and doubtful matters from this community" [[Ibn Kathir attributed it to Ibn Mardawayh and said: "It is gharib, and its ascription to the Prophet is not sound." Then he said: "The apparent meaning is that the verse is general for everyone who has parted from the religion of Allah and opposed it, for Allah sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to make it prevail over all religion, and its law is one, with no disagreement or division in it." Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/197.]].

Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Hanafi narrated to us: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Ansari informed us: Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Aqil ibn al-Azhari ibn Aqil al-Faqih al-Balkhi informed us: al-Ramadi, Ahmad ibn Mansur, informed us: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad informed us: Thawr ibn Yazid related to us: Khalid ibn Ma'dan related to us from Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr al-Sulami, from al-Irbad ibn Sariyah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led us in the dawn prayer and then admonished us with an eloquent admonition, from which the eyes shed tears and the hearts trembled. A speaker said: 'O Messenger of Allah, it is as if this is the admonition of one bidding farewell, so advise us.' He said: 'I advise you to have taqwa of Allah and to hear and obey, even if it is an Abyssinian slave. For whoever of you lives will see much disagreement, so hold fast to my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the rightly-guided Caliphs who came after me. Bite onto it with your molars, and beware of newly-invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance.'" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah, chapter on adhering to the Sunnah: 7/11, and al-Mundhiri was silent on it. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Ilm, chapter on what has come concerning adhering to the Sunnah and avoiding innovations: 7/437-442, and he said: hasan sahih. Ibn Majah in the Introduction, nos. (42 and 43): 1/15-16. al-Darimi in the Introduction: 1/44. Ibn Hibban authenticated it, p. (102) of Mawarid al-Zam'an. Also narrated by al-Lalaka'i in Sharh Usul I'tiqad Ahl al-Sunnah: 1/74-75, al-Ajurri in al-Shari'ah pp. (46-47), Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah: 1/17-19. al-Hakim: 1/95 and said: sahih with no defect. Imam Ahmad: 4/126-127. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/205.]].

It was narrated from Abd Allah ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the Children of Israel divided into seventy-two sects, and my community will divide into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one." They said: "Who is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Those who are upon what I am upon and my Companions." [[This hadith has been narrated through many routes from a number of Companions with different wordings. It was narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunnah: 7/3-4; al-Tirmidhi in al-Iman, chapter on the division of this community: 7/397, and he said: hasan sahih. Ibn Majah in al-Fitan, no. (3991): 2/1321. al-Darimi in al-Siyar: 2/241. Ibn Hibban, no. (1834) of al-Mawarid. al-Hakim authenticated it on the condition of Muslim and al-Dhahabi agreed: 1/128-129. Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/232. Also narrated by Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunnah: 1/7, al-Lalaka'i: 1/100, and al-Ajurri in al-Shari'ah pp. (14-16). See also: al-Wasiyyah al-Kubra of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, edited by us, pp. (45-46), published by Maktabat al-Siddiq.]].

Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed the best speech is the Book of Allah, and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the worst matters are their newly-invented ones." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, chapter on following the Sunnahs: 13/251. Also al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/211. Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath: "The apparent context of the hadith is that it is mawquf (halted at a Companion), but the part that has the ruling of being marfu' (traced to the Prophet) is his saying: 'and the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad (ﷺ),' for it is a report about one of the attributes of the Prophet (ﷺ), and this is one of the categories of marfu'. Few have pointed this out. It is like what is agreed upon by the compilers who restricted themselves to marfu' hadiths in the traditions describing his (ﷺ) characteristics, most of which relate to the description of his creation and person, such as his face and hair, and likewise to the description of his character, such as his forbearance and forgiveness. This is included in that, and the hadith comes from Ibn Mas'ud explicitly traced to the Prophet by another route, narrated by the authors of the Sunan, but it is not on the condition of al-Bukhari."]]. Jabir narrated it traced to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) [[This narration was recorded by Muslim in the Book of Friday prayer, chapter on shortening the prayer and the sermon, no. (867): 2/592. Also al-Musannif in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/211. See Fath al-Bari: 13/253.]].

His saying, exalted and mighty is He: ﴿you are not of them in anything﴾. It was said before: you are not of their fighting in anything, abrogated by the verse of fighting [[See what has preceded regarding the commentary on the explanation of verse (13) of Surat al-Ma'idah in this part, pp. (32-33).]]. This is according to the view of those who say the verse refers to the Jews and the Christians. And whoever said that the verse means the people of desires said: the meaning of His saying "you are not of them in anything" is: you are free of them and they are free of you. The Arabs say: "If you do such and such, then you are not of me and I am not of you," meaning each of us is free from the other. ﴿Their affair is only with Allah﴾, meaning: in the recompense and requitals. ﴿Then He will inform them of what they used to do﴾ when they return on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 6, verses 160–163:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten times the like thereof﴾, meaning: he shall have ten good deeds like it. Ya'qub read "ʿashar" with tanwin, and "amthaluha" in the nominative (raf'). ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, he shall not be recompensed except the like thereof, and they will not be wronged﴾.

Ishaq ibn Sa'id al-Mani'i informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi narrated to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Qattan narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sulami narrated to us: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, informing us: Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, narrated to us: Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you makes his Islam good, every good deed he does is written for him as ten times its like, up to seven hundred times, and every evil deed he does is written for him as its like, until he meets Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Iman, chapter on the goodness of a person's Islam: 1/100, and in a similar form in Kitab al-Tawhid; and Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, chapter: when a servant intends a good deed it is written, and when he intends an evil deed it is not written, no. 129: 1/118-119; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/338.]]

And Isma'il ibn ʿAbd al-Qahir al-Jurjani informed us: ʿAbd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi narrated to us: Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: Whoever comes with a good deed, he shall have ten times its like, and I shall add [more]. Whoever comes with an evil deed, its recompense is the like of it, or I shall forgive. Whoever draws near to Me a span, I draw near to him a cubit; whoever draws near to Me a cubit, I draw near to him a fathom; whoever comes to Me walking, I come to him running; and whoever meets Me with earth-filling sin, not associating anything with Me, I meet him with forgiveness equal to it."

[[Narrated by Muslim in Kitab al-Dhikr wa al-Du'a', chapter on the virtue of remembrance and supplication to Allah Exalted, no. 2687: 4/2068; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/25-26.]]

Ibn ʿUmar said: The verse refers to good deeds other than charities; as for charities, they are multiplied seven hundred times.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a upright religion﴾. The people of Kufa and Syria read "qiyaman" with a kasra on the qaf and a light (unshaddated) ya' with a fatha; the others read with a fatha on the qaf and a kasra on the ya' with shaddah. Both have the same meaning, namely "the upright, straight." Its accusative (intisab) is on the sense of "He guided me to a religion, upright," ﴿the creed of Abraham, a hanif, and he was not of the polytheists﴾.

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice﴾. It was said: by "nusuk" he meant the sacrificial animal in Hajj and ʿUmrah. Muqatil said: "nusuki" means my Hajj. It was also said: my religion. ﴿And my living and my dying﴾, meaning: my life and my death, ﴿are for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾, meaning: He gives me life and causes me to die. It was also said: my living is by righteous action, and my dying, if I die upon faith, is for Allah, Lord of the worlds. And it was said: my obedience during my life is for Allah, and my recompense after my death is from Allah, Lord of the worlds. The people of Medina read "wa-mahyaya" with the ya' sukun and "wa-mamati" with a fatha; the common reading is "mahyaya" with a fatha on the ya', to avoid two consecutive unvocalized letters.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has no partner, and of this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾. Qatadah said: "and I am the first of the Muslims" means the first of Muslims of this Ummah.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah al-An'am, verses 164–165:

﴿Say, "Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of everything?"﴾ Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "(Rabb means) a master and a god." ﴿And He is the Lord of everything.﴾ This was because the disbelievers used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Return to our religion." Ibn 'Abbas said: al-Walid ibn al-Mughira used to say: "Follow my path, and I will bear your burdens." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And no one earns [guilt] except against himself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another.﴾ No soul is held responsible except for the sin it committed, and no soul bears the burden of another, meaning that no one is held to account for the sin of someone else. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾

﴿And it is He who made you successors (khala'if) upon the earth.﴾ That is: He destroyed the people of the earlier generations and gave you, O community of Muhammad (ﷺ), the earth after them, making you successors in place of them, to succeed them in it and to inhabit it after them. The word khala'if (الْخَلَائِفُ) is the plural of khalifah (خَلِيفَةٌ), just as al-wasa'if (الْوَصَائِفُ) is the plural of wasifah (وَصِيفَةٌ). Anyone who comes after one who has passed away is a khalifah, because he succeeds him.

﴿And He raised some of you above others in degrees.﴾ That is: He varied your conditions, making some of you higher than others in creation, provision, livelihood, strength and merit. ﴿That He may test you in what He has given you.﴾ That He may examine you concerning what He has provided you, meaning that He tests the rich and the poor, the noble and the lowly, the free and the slave, so that there may become manifest from you what you will merit of reward and punishment. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty.﴾ Because what is coming is near and imminent. It was said that this refers to destruction in this world. ﴿And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ 'Ata' said: He is swift in punishment toward His enemies, Forgiving toward His allies, and Merciful toward them.
